docs.title: 13. Implicit Mastery Through Valid Local Assessments
docs.text:
Binding Concept Revision of 4 November 2026

An explicit pass on a content goal establishes understanding. Passing a valid local assessment can establish independent application of the underlying competencies. That implicit mastery carries equal global weight: it satisfies subsequent prerequisites and counts toward cumulative attainment. Assessment and memory goals themselves remain strictly explicit.

Consider a learning unit containing the chain \( d{Q} o d{B} o d{A}\): assessment goal \( d{Q}\) requires content goal \( d{B}\), and \( d{B}\) requires \( d{A}\). As long as \( d{Q}\) remains open, the assessment still demands its prerequisites \( d{B}\) and \( d{A}\). Once the learner passes \( d{Q}\) under a valid local contract of that unit, both \( d{B}\) and \( d{A}\) count as independently applied – and hence implicitly mastered – even without separate explicit results of their own. The subsections below formalize that set equation and state the domain conditions required before evaluating it.

The Product Owner confirmed this recognition rule on 11 November 2026: an own ordinary goal is recognized once no open own assessment or memory goal of its unit still requires it. If assessments \( d{Q_1}\) and \( d{Q_2}\) belong to the same unit and both require \( d{A}\), then \( d{A}\) stays open after \( d{Q_1}\) is passed until \( d{Q_2}\) is passed as well (Figure 15); explicit mastery of \( d{A}\) remains possible at any time. The rule is sound only inside units that satisfy the validity conditions of Section 13.3.

The stored binary value \(m\) remains the sole persisted outcome per goal. This specification derives additional satisfaction without writing mastery backward, adding extra qualification records, introducing manual waiver masks, or requiring second partial exams. On main, this concept is not yet implemented; the current concept specification is authoritative.

docs.title: 13.1. Local Contract, Target Scope, and Protected Goal Types
docs.text:
Local contract.

A local contract belongs to an authoritative learning unit \(U\) from Section 11. It binds \(U\)'s own acquisition targets \(\Own(U)\), their canonical identities, the curriculum revision, and the domain-reviewed meaning of \(U\)'s own assessments; adjacent documents also call it a local recognition or acquisition contract. Total scope \(T(U)\) additionally aggregates child-unit targets, yet \(T(U)\) is never an enlarged substitute recognition scope for the parent unit, and a subsequent parent integration claim never retroactively widens child contracts. Neither a display filter nor a temporary focus nor the currently selected plan roots redefines that ownership. Section 11.2 names the fields that carry these parts.

Protected goals.

Let \(Q \subseteq A\) denote the authoritatively classified assessment goals and \(A_{\mathrm{mem}} \subseteq A\) the memory goals, while \(K = G \setminus A\) remains the set of structural clusters. A unit's own protected goals are

\[ Q_U = \Own(U) \cap Q, \qquad A_{\mathrm{mem},U} = \Own(U) \cap A_{\mathrm{mem}}, \qquad P_U = Q_U \cup A_{\mathrm{mem},U}. \]

\(P_U\) protects all own assessment and memory goals from implicit completion: passing another assessment substitutes neither for an assessment's own pass nor for verified recall of required flashcards. Orientation remains a distinct motivational goal type rather than a third protected class: an orientation marker may enter \(I_U\) as a derivatively closed entry anchor without certifying domain competence or asserting that a motivational dialogue actually took place. Outside support beyond \(T(U)\) never enlarges the completion denominator, and competencies outside \(\Own(U)\) receive no implicit recognition from \(U\)'s own contract – child targets are governed by their respective child contracts. The remaining own goals – content goals and any orientation goals – are called unprotected below.

Underlying relation.

All formulas below evaluate the fully inherited and atomically expanded prerequisite relation \(\Rat\) from Section 2.3, including hidden and cross-subject support. Every reference must resolve and the normalized relation must be acyclic; full prerequisite closure is evaluated prior to any display restriction.

docs.title: 13.2. Transitive Open Demand and Implicit Set
docs.text:
For any subset \(X \subseteq A\), let \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\Rat}^{*}(X)\) denote \(X\) itself together with every atom directly or transitively required by an element of \(X\):

\[ \operatorname{Reach}_{\Rat}^{*}(X) = X \cup \{b \in A \mid \exists a \in X : (a, b) \in \Rat^+\}. \]

Given global explicit mastery \(M = \{a \mid m(a) = 1\}\), define

\[ N_U = \operatorname{Reach}_{\Rat}^{*}(P_U \setminus M), ag{15} \]

\[ I_U = \Own(U) \setminus (M \cup P_U \cup N_U). ag{16} \]

Here \(N_U\) is open demand – the still-open protected goals of \(U\) together with their full atomic prerequisite demand – and \(I_U\) is the implicit set. An own goal belongs to \(I_U\) if and only if it is

  1. not already explicitly mastered,
  2. not protected, and
  3. no longer required by any open protected goal of the unit.

Reflexive reachability retains the open roots themselves together with all of their transitive prerequisites: traversal never stops at an explicitly mastered intermediate goal or at the boundary of \(\Own(U)\). Consequently, \(I_U\) remains invariant whenever a redundant shortcut edge is added or removed for required transitive minimality, and \(I_U \cap M = \varnothing\) as well as \(I_U \cap P_U = \varnothing\) hold unconditionally.

Figure 12 works through both starting states of \( d{Q} o d{B} o d{A}\) with \(\Own(U) = \{ d{Q}, d{B}, d{A}\}\) and \(P_U = \{ d{Q}\}\). In Case A, only \( d{B}\) is explicitly mastered; open assessment \( d{Q}\) continues to demand both \( d{B}\) and \( d{A}\), yielding \(N_U = \{ d{Q}, d{B}, d{A}\}\) and \(I_U = \varnothing\). In Case B, \( d{Q}\) is passed, leaving no open protected goal: \(N_U = \varnothing\) and \(I_U = \{ d{A}, d{B}\}\).

Figure 12 — Transitive demand across an explicitly mastered intermediate goal: Two independent starting states for \( d{Q} o d{B} o d{A}\): with \(M=\{ d{B}\}\), \( d{A}\) remains open; with \(M=\{ d{Q}\}\), \( d{Q}\) carries implicit application of \( d{A}\) and \( d{B}\). This is not a temporal sequence: an already explicitly mastered \( d{B}\) would stay in \(M\) when \( d{Q}\) is passed later. A direct edge \( d{Q} o d{A}\) would be redundant.

Complexity.

Let \(V_U^{\mathrm{reach}} = \operatorname{Reach}_{\Rat}^{*}(P_U \setminus M)\) denote the reachable atomic nodes and \(E_U^{\mathrm{reach}} = \{(a, b) \in \Rat \mid a \in V_U^{\mathrm{reach}}\}\) their outgoing prerequisite edges. Direct graph traversal visits each such node and edge at most once, computing \(I_U\) across \(\Own(U)\) in \(O(|\Own(U)| + |V_U^{\mathrm{reach}}| + |E_U^{\mathrm{reach}}|)\) steps – and globally in at most \(O(|A| + |\Rat|)\) – without materializing a quadratic transitive closure.

docs.title: 13.3. Why the Skill Graph Alone Does Not Prove Application
docs.text:
The set equations above may be evaluated only for a valid domain contract. The Product Owner decision of 11 November 2026 states its conditions as five rules and fixes where each is enforced (Table 7): the recognition rule is sound only if units satisfy them as hard rules.

Table 7: Validity conditions of a learning unit and where they are enforced (Product Owner decision of 11 November 2026). For learning units authored in the canonical landscapes, a validator checks R1, R3, and the uniqueness part of R4; R2 and R5 are not yet enforced.

Rule Requirement Placement R1 Every own ordinary content goal lies on a prerequisite path from at least one own assessment of the unit, directly or transitively; a path that leads only to a memory goal does not count. Validity condition of the unit definition, in the same class as acyclicity: hard from the first authored unit; a violating unit cannot be merged. R2 For every own ordinary goal, at least one own assessment that requires it has reviewed evidence that its tasks and normal grading really test the goal. Milestone M5 (assessment approval and coverage metadata), with the current per-goal binding at M7; without it the curriculum does not reach the milestone. R3 An assessment claims coverage only for goals it requires directly or transitively: \(\operatorname{Cov}(q)\subseteq\{b\in A\mid(q,b)\in\Rat^+\}\). As R1. R4 Every acquisition target has exactly one directly owning unit. As R1. R5 A later re-cut of units or later edges never grant additional recognition to existing results; the contract is versioned. Runtime contract; precondition before implicit recognition is enabled in production.

Structural conditions (R1, R3, R4).

Every content goal in \(\Own(U)\) must lie on a local prerequisite path from at least one local assessment in \(Q_U\): an own assessment of the unit must require it directly or transitively (R1). A path leading only to a memory goal never suffices, because verified card recall does not prove independent application. An isolated terminal content goal without a local assessment consumer is a contract defect rather than zero-work mastery; lacking a downstream consumer never proves competence. No ad-hoc mask of “recognition-eligible” subgoals exists – the formula governs the entire valid local contract.

Let \(\operatorname{Cov}(q)\) denote the goals whose independent application an assessment \(q\) claims to test according to its reviewed coverage claim. R3 requires \(q\) to require each of them directly or transitively. This guarantees that the assessment which actually tests a goal is among the open protected goals the recognition rule waits for: while an own assessment \(q\) is open, every own goal in \(\operatorname{Cov}(q)\) stays in \(N_U\). A missing path is a finding for subject review, not a reason to add a redundant direct edge. R4 makes the contract well defined: a goal with no or with several directly owning units belongs to no valid local contract.

Content condition (R2).

For every own ordinary goal, at least one own assessment that requires it must carry reviewed evidence that its authored tasks and normal grading rubric genuinely require independent application of that competence (R2), without reinterpreting an orientation marker as an assessable domain competence. Essential competencies must not be wholly omitted while still allowing unrelated points elsewhere to cross the passing threshold. Neither a local requires path nor a title, coveredGoalIds array, passing threshold, or formal DAG check proves that property: independent domain review inspects tasks, model solutions, rubrics, and claimed application coverage jointly across every passing assessment combination that releases a target under the set formula – checking only the union of all assessments never suffices.

No second status.

Passing an assessment remains the single ordinary binary pass of that assessment goal. Stronger application meaning resides in the pre-reviewed local contract rather than in an extra per-learner qualification field or a second follow-up exam, and a legacy assessment lacking that review never acquires expanded meaning retroactively from a new diagram or software update.

Consequence.

Implicit recognition exists only inside units whose contract satisfies R1–R4 with reviewed coverage. Otherwise the unit's own ordinary goals stay open – they can still be mastered explicitly – and the violation keeps the curriculum from reaching the respective milestone (Table 7). A goal that no assessment covers therefore stays open and is a rule violation; it is never recognized for free. Section 13.4 treats R5.

Current enforcement.

Learning units are declared in the placement layer of their skill landscape (Section 11.2); reviewed coverage of own assessments is the unit's coverageReviews. For the canonical Gymnasium landscapes, validate:learning-units (validateLearningUnits.ts) runs in the required curriculum CI. It reads goal kinds, prerequisites, and coveredGoalIds from the landscape and rejects a unit fail-closed when it violates R1 or R3, when two units own the same goal (uniqueness part of R4), or when its declaration, own goals, total scope, or unit hierarchy are malformed. The completeness part of R4 – every acquisition target has an owning unit – applies only to a landscape that declares learningUnitCoverage as complete; none does yet. R2 is not a condition of structural validity: the validator checks claimed coverage reviews against the current tasks and rubrics and reports the goals that still lack one, but no M5 or M7 gate consumes this. R5 and implicit recognition at runtime are not yet implemented on main. A reference evaluation of the set equations (learningUnitRecognition.ts) checks them in required CI against the same shared conformance cases.

docs.title: 13.4. Global Effectiveness and Durable Contract Binding
docs.text:
Let \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{valid}}\) denote the authoritative local contracts durably bound to this learner at their applicable revisions – rather than arbitrary visited views or all latest content revisions:

\[ \Meff = M \cup igcup_{U \in \mathcal U_{\mathrm{valid}}} I_U. \]

That union is not restricted to currently displayed learning units or the active Personal Curriculum view: contract identity, revision, and evidential meaning must remain evaluable across scope changes. Derivation always runs directly from explicit outcomes \(M\) and valid contracts without feeding previously derived implicit sets back as explicit mastery inputs.

A later learning unit \( d{U2}\) carrying another assessment \( d{q_2}\) must never reopen an application competence \( d{a}\) already established under \( d{U1}\) (Figure 13); instead, \( d{a}\) satisfies \( d{q_2}\)'s prerequisite. Under a fixed contract set, adding explicit mastery can only enlarge \(\Meff\): open protected roots shrink, their transitive demand contracts, and any newly explicitly mastered goal leaving \(I_U\) stays inside \(\Meff\) via \(M\).

Figure 13 — Local recognition remains globally effective for later learning units: \( d{U1}\) recognizes \( d{a}\) and \( d{b}\) under its own valid contract. The open later assessment \( d{q_2}\) does not block that recognition. Switching focus or plans does not erase the still-evaluable contract of \( d{U1}\).

A stable assessment goal ID binds a stable recognition meaning, and equivalent task variants must uphold that same qualified contract. Expanded recognition claims must never silently upgrade legacy exam passes: they require either a new assessment identity or an explicitly reviewed meaning-preserving migration, without adding per-learner qualification records. Whenever historical evidential meaning is unresolved, the explicit pass stands without fabricating broader application recognition, and genuine score or content corrections remain distinct from ordinary downstream consumer or plan switches.

Under rule R5, a later re-cut of units or later edges never grant additional recognition to existing results; the contract is versioned. This runtime contract is a precondition before implicit recognition is enabled in production.

docs.title: 13.5. Protected Goals and Full Unit Completion
docs.text:
Recognition is not yet full completion.

Full unit completion follows recursively from Equation (10): all own goals must be satisfied and every required child unit must be complete. Given global \(\Meff\), that condition coincides with \(T(U) \subseteq \Meff\) provided every required child obligation is represented inside \(T(U)\), and full completion always entails \(P_U \subseteq M\) on own protected goals.

Once every own assessment and memory goal of \(U\) is passed, \(N_U = \varnothing\), allowing \(U\)'s valid local contract to complete its own unprotected goals. Completion of required child units never follows from that fact alone: a parent synthesis assessment may stay open while child content competencies are already globally recognized, and conversely passing the parent synthesis never satisfies an open child assessment or memory obligation.

Open protected goals in the same contract.

An open own memory goal blocks full unit completion without blocking implicit recognition of another own content goal that it does not transitively require (Figure 14). Whenever an open memory goal does require a content goal directly or transitively, however, that content goal stays in open demand. Likewise, when multiple assessments inside the same local contract share a common foundation, all of them must be passed before that foundation leaves open demand.

Figure 14 — Protected memory goals and external support: Assessment \( d{q}\) is explicitly passed and carries application of \( d{a}\). The independent memory goal \( d{k}\) remains open and blocks full unit completion. External support \( d{h}\) outside \(\Own(U)\) receives no recognition.

That rule distinguishes multiple assessments inside the same local contract from a subsequent assessment in another learning unit (Figure 13). Figure 15 traces two successive passes at unchanged local scope without further protected obligations.

Figure 15 — Two local assessments sharing a common foundation: \( d{Q_1}\) and \( d{Q_2}\) both require \( d{A}\) in the same valid local contract. After \( d{Q_1}\) alone, \( d{A}\) stays in open demand because \( d{Q_2}\) is still open. Only after both assessments are passed does \( d{A}\) become implicitly mastered globally. The explicit pass of \( d{Q_1}\) is preserved; there are no further protected goals here.

Comparing that case with Figure 13 presupposes domain-justified, independently valid local contracts: an open assessment in a later unit never revokes recognition already established in an earlier unit, whereas inside a single contract the entire remaining open demand applies. Nothing here licenses splitting or rearranging assessments or units merely to engineer a desired calculation result.

Assessment access.

Existing direct assessment access remains the baseline of the current learner workflow, subject to task availability, authentication, session ownership, and explicit learner selection. Whether optional gated profiles later impose hard unit locks – and how deliberate direct assessment attempts behave under them – remains undecided (Section 11); recursive unit definitions introduce neither a hidden lock nor an unreviewed bypass. Ordinary prerequisite evaluation uses \(\Meff\) over the transitive effective relation while preserving normal and strict focus semantics.

docs.title: 13.6. Cumulative Attainment and Dated Period Events
docs.text:
For a fixed named plan target set \(T_{\mathrm{Plan}}\), cumulative plan attainment counts the effectively mastered goals of the plan:

\[ H_{\mathrm{gesamt}} = |T_{\mathrm{Plan}} \cap \Meff|. \]

Forming the union \(\Meff\) prior to intersecting with \(T_{\mathrm{Plan}}\) prevents double-counting across explicit outcomes, implicit sets, and overlapping contracts; any dedicated explicit-only view must label its distinct counter clearly.

By contrast, an active schedule period counts solely dated explicit completion events under its event contract: newly derived application recognition, prior mastery brought into the course, or a widened plan display never fabricates an extra dated completion event inside the current period (Figure 16).

Figure 16 — Total plan progress and dated period completions: Total plan progress and period completions use distinct counters. In the example, 7 of 10 planned goals are effectively mastered (4 explicit and 3 implicit). The current period counts only the 2 dated explicit completions against its quota of 3 goals. The three implicit contributions raise cumulative progress without fabricating dated explicit completion events inside the current period.

The unified learning-plan status contract specifies the user-facing surfaces. Static contract definitions may be cached per revision while derived sets remain computed projections rather than a second stored truth, and invalid or unresolved contracts stay visibly unavailable. Automated checks of these formulas replace neither independent content review nor human learner testing or instructional effectiveness studies.

Sources: Assessment-Gated Completion and Implicit Mastery; Completion Semantics Clarification of 4 November 2026; Unified Learning-Plan Status Contract.

docs.title: 7. Visualisierungen für atomare Lernziele
docs.text: Optionale Begriffsillustrationen unterstützen Lernende dabei, die Kernidee eines atomaren Lernziels visuell zu erfassen, ohne eigenes Nachdenken oder Aufgabenlösen vorwegzunehmen.

docs.title: 7.1. Kanonisches Linkschema und MCP-App-Darstellungsvertrag
docs.text:
Geprüfte Visualisierungen werden über resourceLinks am atomaren Lernziel referenziert:

{
  "type": "goal-visualization",
  "resourceType": "image",
  "role": "primary",
  "skillpilotId": "<exakte-kanonische-goal-id>",
  "url": "/assets/goal-visualizations/<subject>/<id>/<id>.png"
}

In MCP-fähigen Hosts wie OpenAI ChatGPT liefert render_skillpilot_goal_visualization ein oberflächenneutrales text/html;profile=mcp-app-Widget mit einmaliger (goalId, stateVersion)-Autorisierung und dem Schalter showGoalVisualizationsInChat. Das Widget bleibt bis zum erfolgreichen Bildladen eingeklappt, wertet begrenzte MCP-Ergebnisumschläge aus (mit gespeichertem Widget-State nur als Bootstrap-Fallback) und bewahrt alle zuvor veröffentlichten inhaltsadressierten UI-Ressourcen-Hashes unverändert.

docs.title: 7.2. Produktionsbereich, Format und Provider-Priorität
docs.text:
Prompts, Kandidatenerzeugung und QA-Ledger liegen unter curricula/DE/Gymnasium/visualizations/ (prompt.de.md, image-reconstruction-prompt.de.md, Ausspielung per npm run deploy:assets als 16:9-PNG um 1600x900, geprüft auf 360px Mobil- und 680px Desktopbreite, kalibriert am Pilotziel 502ecaa7-cca6-5c51-a1cc-da09a7b2382c).

Gemäß verbindlicher Product-Owner-Entscheidung vom 13. September 2026 gilt:

  • Standard KEEP: Gute bestehende Mathematik- und Physikbilder bleiben unabhängig vom ursprünglichen Generator erhalten; es erfolgt keine rückwirkende Konvertierung zur Provider-Vereinheitlichung.
  • Provider-Priorität bei Neu- oder Korrekturbildern: Bevorzugt wird ChatGPT/Codex-Bildgenerierung in der freundlichen, abstrakten, klaren, comicartigen Raster-Bildsprache von SkillPilot, sofern Fachrichtigkeit und Darstellung passen. Nano Banana Pro (gemini-3-pro-image) ist ohne vorherigen Fehlversuch als reguläre Alternative zulässig, wenn es die fachliche Darstellung besser trifft.
  • Enge SVG-/Plot-Ausnahme: Programmatisch gezeichnete Diagramme/SVGs bleiben eng begrenzte, fachlich begründete Ausnahmen für exakte Geometrie-/Funktionsplots und kein allgemeiner Stilwechsel.

docs.title: 7.3. CLI-Workflow und zweistufige Review-Gates
docs.text:
Die Hilfsskripte unter app/ (visualization:generate:nano-banana, visualization:plan-batch, visualization:check-prompt-appends, visualization:prepare, visualization:import) trennen Generierung strikt von Freigabe:

  1. KI-QA-Ledger (aiApprovedAssetSha256 / Gate V): Speichert strukturierte Prüflabels (accepted_pilot, accepted_pilot_after_regeneration, rejected_regenerate, deferred_provider_limitation, needs_external_review), gebunden an den exakten Datei-SHA-256.
  2. Menschliches Publikationsgate (humanApproved, HR-003): Öffentliche Standalone-Releases und public-Lernzielbücher (8, Menschliche Review-Gates) verlangen eine ausdrückliche menschliche Fach- und Rechtefreigabe (CC-BY-4.0 getrennt von Provenienz); bloße Generierung oder KI-Prüfung ersetzt keine Publikationsfreigabe.

{

docs.title: 7.2. Production Workspace, Format, and Provider Policy
docs.text:
Authoring prompts, candidate generation, and QA ledgers reside under curricula/DE/Gymnasium/visualizations/ (prompt.de.md, image-reconstruction-prompt.de.md, published via npm run deploy:assets at 16:9 1600x900 PNG and inspected at both 360px mobile and 680px desktop widths, calibrated on pilot goal 502ecaa7-cca6-5c51-a1cc-da09a7b2382c).

Under the binding Product Owner decision of 13 September 2026:

  • Default KEEP: Retain good existing Mathematics and Physics images regardless of which provider generated them; never regenerate retro-actively merely to unify providers.
  • Provider priority for new or defective images: Prefer ChatGPT/Codex image generation in SkillPilot's friendly, abstract, clear, comic-like raster style when subject-matter accuracy and representation fit. Nano Banana Pro (gemini-3-pro-image) is an allowed alternative whenever it better serves the didactic representation — no prior failed attempt with the other provider is required.
  • Narrow SVG/programmatic exception: Programmatically plotted diagrams or SVGs remain narrow, explicitly documented exceptions justified by exact geometric/function-plot precision, never a blanket style replacement.

docs.title: 7.3. CLI Workflow and Two-Stage Review Gates
docs.text:
Helper scripts in app/ (visualization:generate:nano-banana, visualization:plan-batch, visualization:check-prompt-appends, visualization:prepare, visualization:import) separate asset generation from approval:

  1. AI QA ledger (aiApprovedAssetSha256 / Gate V): Records structured review labels (accepted_pilot, accepted_pilot_after_regeneration, rejected_regenerate, deferred_provider_limitation, needs_external_review) bound to exact file SHA-256 digests.
  2. Human publication gate (humanApproved, HR-003): Public Standalone releases and public-mode GoalBooks (8, Human Review Gates) require explicit human content and rights clearance (CC-BY-4.0 vs. provenance); generation or AI review alone never grants publication approval.

docs.title: 9. Rollout-Politik für das kanonische Gymnasium
docs.text: Dieses Kapitel legt die dauerhafte Zielarchitektur und Rollout-Politik fest, nach der die deutschen Gymnasiallehrpläne aller 16 Bundesländer ohne bundeslandspezifische Zielduplizierung in je einen kanonischen Skill-Graphen pro Fach zusammengeführt werden (Umsetzungspläne und Migrationsstände liegen unter Implementierungsplan Kanonisches Gymnasium und Migrationsstatus).

docs.title: 9.1. Neun Kernentscheidungen und Scope-Vokabular
docs.text:
1. Kanonische Fachebene zuerst: Eine durchgängige SkillLandscape je Fach unter curricula/DE/Gymnasium/canonical/ von Sekundarstufe I bis zur Abiturreife.
  2. Kontinuität in der Übergangsphase: Abgelöste Landesbäume bleiben als bundeslandgebundene Quellen- und Auditeingaben unter curricula/DE/Gymnasium/input/<STATE>/ erhalten (abgesichert durch die Stilllegungsvalidatoren in Graph- und View-Validierung), während Mappings bestehenden Lernfortschritt überführen.
  3. Schlanke Mapping-Schicht: Explizite legacyGoalId -> canonicalGoalId-Mappings (matchType: "exact" | "partial") statt eines zweiten Inhaltsuniversums.
  4. ISO-3166-2-Ländercodes: Metadaten und Filter nutzen durchgängig DE-HE, DE-BY, …, DE-TH (ALL ist ein reiner Query-Sentinel und wird nie serialisiert).
  5. Stabile Coach-/MCP-Schnittstellen: Backend und Laufzeit kapseln die Übersetzung zwischen Alt- und Kanon-Schicht, sodass KI-Coaches stets genau einen Lernstand, eine Frontier und ein Mastery-Modell sehen.
  6. Kontrollierte fachübergreifende requires: Kanonische Fachlandschaften dürfen fachübergreifende Kanten direkt auf stabile kanonische IDs setzen (z. B. Physikziele mit Mathematik-Voraussetzungen), ohne fremde Teilbäume zu kopieren; die Graphvalidatoren lösen diese Verweise über die geladenen Landschaften auf, und CQR-001 bezieht benötigte fachfremde Ziele samt vererbender Vorfahren in die Prüfung auf atomare Normalform und transitive Minimalität ein.
  7. Gemeinsame Wurzel Gymnasium (DE) & geprüftes Scope-Vokabular: Ein bundesweiter Einstiegsknoten bündelt Fachlandschaften entlang jurisdiction (DE-*), schoolForm (Gymnasium), stage (SekI, SekII), durationModel (G8, G9) und courseProfile (GK, LK, GK+LK ohne doppelte IDs) auf Basis expliziter .view.json-Dateien (3).
  8. G9-Referenzraster für Sek I: Kanonische Sek-I-Landschaften orientieren sich am gemeinsamen Raster Jahrgang 5 bis Jahrgang 10, während G8/G9-Quellwahrheit in Provenienz und Views erhalten bleibt.
  9. Bundeslandgebundene Quell-Assets: Nicht-kanonische Quellenextrakte, Abitur-Blueprints (curricula/DE/Gymnasium/input/HE/abi/) und Auditbelege bleiben strikt ländergetrennt unter input/<STATE>/.

docs.title: 9.2. Teilbaum-Zustandsmodell und Einführungsreihenfolge
docs.text:
Migrationseinheit ist stets ein didaktisch abgeschlossener Teilbaum (kein Big-Bang-Umbau) entlang vier geordneter Zustände:

Zustand Bedeutung & Lernstandsvertrag 1. legacy_frozen Bestehende Landes-JSONs dienen schreibgeschützt als Quelle; Laufzeit-/Mappingkorrekturen ohne Umbau des Altbaums erlaubt. 2. subtree_adopted Abgeschlossener contains-Teilbaum unter canonical/ mit expliziten exact/partial-Mappings und gebundenen Voraussetzungen angelegt. 3. cutover_ready Lernstandskontinuität, Frontier-Stimmigkeit und Mappingabdeckung belegt, sodass der kanonische Pfad Standard werden kann. 4. legacy_view_retained Kanonischer Teilbaum ist primärer Lernpfad; Kompatibilitätssichten bleiben vorübergehend bis zur regulären Stilllegung verfügbar.

Strategische Reihenfolge: hessische Lernstandskontinuität sichern \(\to\) Mathematik über Sek I und Sek II als zentrales Voraussetzungsrückgrat aufbauen \(\to\) Bayern und weitere Länder per Mapping und .view.json-Projektionen einbinden \(\to\) mehrfächige kanonische Navigation und gezielte Fach-zu-Fach-Voraussetzungen ausbauen.

docs.title: 9. Canonical Gymnasium Rollout Policy
docs.text: This chapter specifies the durable target architecture and rollout rules for converging German Gymnasium curricula across all 16 Bundesländer into one shared canonical skill graph per subject without duplicating competencies per state (execution plans and migration ledgers live in Canonical Gymnasium Implementation Plan and Migration Status).

docs.title: 9.1. Nine Core Decisions and Scope Vocabulary
docs.text:
1. Canonical subject layer first: One continuous SkillLandscape per subject under curricula/DE/Gymnasium/canonical/ spanning Sekundarstufe I through Abitur readiness.
  2. Legacy continuity during transition: Retired state trees survive as state-scoped audit/source inputs under curricula/DE/Gymnasium/input/<STATE>/ (enforced by retirement validators in Graph Validation Rules) while compatibility mappings bridge learner progress.
  3. Minimal mapping layer: Explicit legacyGoalId -> canonicalGoalId mapping files (matchType: "exact" | "partial") instead of a second content universe.
  4. ISO 3166-2 state identifiers: Metadata and filters standardize on DE-HE, DE-BY, ..., DE-TH (ALL is a query-only sentinel, never serialized).
  5. Stable coach/MCP APIs: Backend/runtime code hides legacy-vs-canonical translation so AI coaches always see one learner state, one frontier, and one mastery model.
  6. Controlled cross-subject requires: Canonical subject landscapes may author cross-subject edges directly (for example Physics goals requiring Mathematics atoms by their stable IDs) without cloning foreign subtrees; graph validators resolve these references across loaded landscapes, and CQR-001 includes required foreign goals and their inheriting ancestors in its atomic-normal-form and transitive-minimality audit.
  7. Shared Gymnasium (DE) root & reviewed scope vocabulary: One DE-level composition root exposes child subject landscapes governed by jurisdiction (DE-*), schoolForm (Gymnasium), stage (SekI, SekII), durationModel (G8, G9), and courseProfile (GK, LK, GK+LK union without duplicated IDs), backed by explicit state-scoped .view.json files (3).
  8. G9 Sek-I reference grid: Canonical Sek-I authoring normalizes onto the shared Jahrgang 5–Jahrgang 10 grid while preserving G8/G9 source truth in provenance and view bindings.
  9. State-scoped retained inputs: Non-canonical source extracts, Abitur blueprints (curricula/DE/Gymnasium/input/HE/abi/), and audit records remain strictly state-scoped under input/<STATE>/.

docs.title: 9.2. Subtree Migration State Machine and Adoption Sequence
docs.text:
The unit of convergence is a didactically closed subtree (never a forced big-bang rewrite), progressing monotonically through four states:

State Meaning & Learner-State Contract 1. legacy_frozen Existing state curriculum JSON is read-only source input; runtime/mapping fixes allowed without rewriting legacy trees. 2. subtree_adopted Closed contains subtree reconstructed in canonical/ with explicit exact/partial mappings and bound prerequisites. 3. cutover_ready Learner-state continuity, frontier coherence, and mapping coverage verified so canonical navigation can become default. 4. legacy_view_retained Canonical subtree is the primary learner-facing route; compatibility views remain temporarily until formal retirement.

Strategic adoption sequence: preserve Hessen learner continuity \(\to\) establish Mathematics across Sek I and Sek II as the primary prerequisite spine \(\to\) fold Bavaria and remaining states into canonical Mathematics via mappings and .view.json projections \(\to\) widen multi-subject canonical navigation and cross-subject prerequisites.
