docs.title: Appendix B — Implementation Status and Boundaries of Claims
docs.text:
Status of this edition. Current candidate, 13 November 2026: PR #141 brings together the Gymnasium follow-up work on the updated main baseline 2ad03c810c. The 12 HARD / 50 PARTIAL / 55 OPEN / 28 OPT/DOC rows and four required GVR-012 scopes belong to this candidate, which has not been integrated into main. Local gate, negative-case, documentation, and PDF checks are evidenced in the follow-up record. Final remote CI and main acceptance are not recorded here as complete; the earlier CI for PR #131 does not evidence these changes. This appendix records the repository states against which the specification's claims were audited and documents where the inspected implementation diverges from the normative model (GD-D01). This unified Single-Source edition consolidates the 4 November concept correction, the 8 November atomic normal-form mandate and milestone mapping, the 9 November projection contract clarification, the 10 November closed Personal Curriculum learning scope, the 11 November 2026 decisions on non-compilable learning contexts and on learning-unit validity, and the 12 November 2026 decisions on complete current target-state validation and on the representation of learning units across Web and PDF. Since 11 November 2026, CQR-001 also enforces G17 for the canonical Gymnasium catalog. The CQR/GVR hardening delivered in PR #131 is integrated into main and supported by the dated CI evidence below; its exact domains and two remaining gaps are recorded in the rule registry. Both backend and WebGUI now evaluate the fixed atomic prerequisite closure; the closure compiler PersonalCurriculumLearningScope.java reuses canonical normalization. Local regression tests cover learnability, planning, focus, reference errors, and cross-subject prerequisite delivery. Full native, curriculum, and remote-CI acceptance as well as applicability validation of the current state remain separate steps. Global application recognition (\(\Meff\)) is not yet implemented. Readable documentation evidence or a green document build proves neither runtime conformance nor production deployment.

Binding Product Owner decisions.

  • 4 November 2026: Implicit mastery through passed assessments of a valid local contract demonstrates independent application and carries global effect (\(\Meff\)); transitive minimality remains mandatory. Assessment and memory goals remain protected: for memory goals, verified completion recall alone establishes goal completion, and subsequent card due state never revokes it (Sections 3, 8, and 13; GD-D03).
  • 7 November 2026: Every reachable prerequisite of a visible goal requires an explicit projection role (target or prerequisiteOnly) in subject composition views; at the Personal Curriculum compile boundary, the 10 November 2026 closure rule supersedes blanket manual per-atom view entries with derived target roles (Section 7.2).
  • 8 November 2026: Atomic normal form \(R\subseteq A imes A\) as the binding canonical target state without cluster exceptions, mandatory ordered migration sequence, and mapping of all 143 rule groups to validation areas and milestones (Sections 2 and 3, Appendix A). The migration-order and preservation obligations from that decision are superseded by the decision of 12 November 2026.
  • 9 November 2026: Projections preserve full prerequisite closure; a canonical cluster never becomes an atomic runtime goal through a composition view (Sections 5 and 6.3).
  • 10 November 2026: The Level 2 Personal Curriculum learning scope is \(L=\Closure(S)\) on the unpruned canonical skill graph, fixed independently of mastery, assigning derived target roles to all necessary prerequisite atoms (Sections 5 and 7).
  • 11 November 2026 (learning context): Hard closure errors belong to validation, curriculum QA, and native acceptance, not to learner reads. When the canonical graph of a learning context is not strictly compilable, the runtime keeps the reviewed seed scope without derived closure, claims no learning basis, offers no goal with broken demand, and logs the failure once per curriculum and error code; seed-selection errors stay hard (Section 7.2).
  • 11 November 2026 (learning units): The recognition rule of 4 November stays: an own ordinary goal is recognized once no open own assessment or memory goal of its unit still requires it (if assessments \( d{Q_1}\) and \( d{Q_2}\) of the same unit both require \( d{A}\), \( d{A}\) stays open until both are passed). The alternative recorded on the archived branch of pull request #83 as a “6 November 2026 target decision” – immediate recognition from the qualified coverage list of a single passed assessment, including proof by a parent or foreign unit – was reviewed and is not adopted. Recognition is sound only inside units that satisfy rules R1–R5: R1, R3, and R4 as hard validity conditions from the first authored unit, R2 at M5 with the current per-goal binding at M7, and R5 as a runtime precondition before recognition is enabled in production; a unit's purpose is a secure foundation before planned learning builds on it (Sections 11 and 13.3).
  • 12 November 2026 (G17/GD-C17): Complete deterministic validation of the current declared subject inventory is required before every subject and scope milestone pass M1–M7. Historical closure equality and a fixed migration order are no longer acceptance conditions. Historical reduction proofs remain available for dependent review bindings; they determine neither the current catalog inventory nor the G17 result (Section 3.1).
  • 12 November 2026 (learning-unit representation): Learning units are part of the skill landscape and live in its placement layer; a separate catalog file beside the landscape was rejected as a bolt-on in favor of a stable long-term contract with a new curriculum-package contract version (1.2) where one is needed (Section 11.2). The unit work resumes under the working plan Learning Units for Mathematics and Physics.
  • 12 November 2026 (frozen reduction proof): The prerequisite-reduction proof is frozen at its end state. Its registry (contract V9) records per goal the value the reviews are bound to; an unchanged goal keeps its reviews, a changed goal needs a new review, and every other catalog change leaves the reuse untouched. The history is no longer replayed against the current catalog (Section 3.1).
  • 13 November 2026 (GVR-012 from M7): The stronger semantic route check shall become mandatory for every registered QA scope of each subject obligated to meet M7. Today this covers seven scopes of five M7 subjects; four are secured. Activation of the complete M7 obligation waits for evidence-backed closure of the other three M7 scopes. The full inventory remains twelve; the five M6 scopes become mandatory on later promotion to M7. Existing required scopes and pins remain protected even through later status changes. GVR-012 stays PARTIAL until complete technical enforcement; this target decision neither activates the obligation nor supplies pass evidence or lowers any floor.

Audited repository states. The technical findings in this appendix and in the rule registry are anchored to the repository states listed below. CQR/GVR delivery was separately reconciled through the mainline state of 13 November 2026; the remaining historical runtime findings were not re-audited in that work. No earlier run substitutes for fresh full-system acceptance on a later HEAD:

  • 616324e857 – Historical implementation audit underlying the runtime divergence rows in the comparison table below; not a fresh full runtime acceptance run.
  • 3b71ee9370 – Baseline gate-reach audit in Appendix A against main.
  • 68db5bf499 – Dedicated projection audit of 9 November 2026 regarding direct goalEntry references to canonical clusters.
  • cacf323919 – main integration of the Personal Curriculum prerequisite-closure compiler \(L=\Closure(S)\) (10 November 2026 decision) and baseline for the traffic-light (Ampel) reconciliation and this Single-Source edition.
  • 44c5b06b77 – main state of this edition (11 November 2026) with the standard G17 milestone gate (15f74ef564, pull request #119), the repaired protected subject data (pull request #121), and the seed-scope fallback (b511654efb); basis of the 11 November rule reconciliation. The runtime findings in the table below were not re-audited at this state.
  • 39fe19b658 – Verified head of PR #131: all 16 jobs in CI #2299 and the Assessment, Docs, OAuth, and Gemini workflows passed. Squash merge dcf5278881 has the same tree; its direct mainline CI run was cancelled. Isolated local gate run blocks actually reject a cluster prerequisite in an M0 subject with exit 1; this is not a mutated full run of both CI entry points. Details and the separately documented local continuations are in the delivery record.
  • 2129b207f4 – Later integrated mainline state: all 14 jobs in the complete CI #2315 passed. This includes retirement of historical proof replays (#133), the new Mathematics assessment (#134), and the inventory correction (#135). It evidences the CQR/GVR gates in this evolved tree, not an unchanged rerun of the PR head or general runtime acceptance. Frozen per-goal V9 review transfers remain separate from current G17 validation; the historical intermediate frame is not restored.
  • 7d13eb82a5 – Mainline baseline for this targeted documentation reconciliation after #136; its PR head 67d36185 passed Docs #790. The documentation check evidences delivery-record consistency, not additional curriculum or runtime acceptance.
  • 2ad03c810c – Updated main baseline of open PR #141, not evidence that its follow-up work has been integrated. The candidate has local evidence for direct gates and negative cases and consistent Web/PDF documentation. The new GD classifications and four directly required GVR-012 scopes in an inventory of twelve are not attributed to historical main CI at 2129b207f4; final remote CI and main acceptance must be tracked separately in the delivery record.

Dedicated projection finding of 9 November 2026. At audited state 68db5bf499, CompletionCanonicalGraphResolver loads prerequisite chains recursively. However, view projection in LearnerService and the resolver still treat direct goalEntry references to canonical clusters as childless runtime atomic goals. Historical evidence for the package-backed runtime catalog, offerings, and composition views (work package DPK-006c-c) documents that legacy implementation rather than proving preservation of the canonical atomic basis now explicitly required. The code fix and native verification remain open. This targeted read audit does not refresh the remaining historical runtime findings in the table below.

Area Binding specification here Audited repository status Completion traversal (transitivity) Full transitive open demand \(N_U=\operatorname{Reach}_{\Rat}^{*}(P_U\setminus M)\) without stopping at mastered intermediate goals. CompletionEvaluator.evaluateAutomaticGraph stops at mastered intermediate goals: in \( d{Q} o d{B} o d{A}\) with only \( d{B}\) mastered, \( d{A}\) is released there, whereas the new formula keeps \( d{A}\) needed for open assessment \( d{Q}\). The legacy profile path in the same service is a different algorithm and likewise does not implement the new contract. Protected goals and local coverage The protected set \(P_U=Q_U\cup A_{\mathrm{mem},U}\) protects all own assessment and memory goals; every own content goal requires local assessment coverage within \(\Own(U)\), without turning pure aggregates or parent syntheses into artificial contracts over descendants. The existing automatic path starts solely from open assessment goals; joint protection of selected memory goals and own-unit assessment coverage are not yet implemented in runtime evaluation. For the learning units authored in the canonical Gymnasium landscapes, validate:learning-units checks R1, R3, and the uniqueness part of R4 fail-closed in required curriculum CI and verifies claimed R2 evidence (the unit's coverageReviews); R2 as a milestone gate and R5 remain open. Global recognition (\(\Meff\)) Person- and revision-bound global union \(\Meff=M\cup igcup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{valid}}}I_U\) acts durably across downstream frontiers, focus switches, and cumulative progress without writing synthetic Mastery records. Not yet implemented. Context-local legacy exemption is not the durable contract-bound set \(\Meff\); downstream frontier, cumulative progress, contract revision binding, and historical meaning must be implemented and verified together. A reference evaluation of the set equations checks them against the shared conformance cases, including invariants over all learner states; the backend does not use it, and it has no binding to contract states (R5). Atomic normal form and minimality (G17) Complete atomic normal form \(R\subseteq A imes A\) and transitive minimality as mandatory baseline before maturity level M1; complete deterministic validation of the current subject inventory including necessary cross-subject prerequisites and inheriting ancestors. Since 15f74ef564 (on main with pull requests #119 and #121, 11 November 2026), CQR-001 runs the G17 check (atomic normal form, transitive minimality, explicit types, including required cross-subject goals) for every root of the complete canonical Gymnasium catalog and caps a failing subject at M0; hard in CI via the ten protected floors. In the status generated on 11 November 2026, the ten protected subjects plus Italian, Polish, Russian, and Czech pass; Chinese, English, French, Greek, Music, Spanish, and the Gymnasium overview root fail and report M0. Non-canonical roots have no G17 gate. The current catalog is derived and completely validated independently of historical reduction proofs; a missing or invalid historical proof never permits reuse of old review evidence (Appendix A). Cluster satisfaction (\(\Sat\)) The normative core requires all atomic descendants \(\Atoms(g)\subseteq\Meff\). Audited backend paths filter recursively via private helper isCoreForPrereqs: children with no tags or tag GK take precedence over other children when present; otherwise all children count. No boolean core field is read there. That differs from normative full-basis aggregation. Memorization and card due state Verified completion recall (RecallPassed) establishes memory-goal completion; subsequent SRS card due dates never revoke completed mastery, and ordinary goals carry no review-due expiry (GD-D03). Legacy due-date target formulas are superseded; historical derivation from recall flags in useSrsMastery.ts alone does not prove full runtime conformance across all flows. Recursive learning units (LearningUnit) Recursive target and child hierarchy with unique direct ownership \(\Own(U)\), derived completion \(\Complete(U)\), and separate optional calendar/budget planning; technical unit locks and direct assessment entry under them remain undecided. Binding domain-structure specification; not yet a claimed runtime feature. Learning units are declared in the placement layer of their skill landscape and carried by curriculum-package contract 1.2 (Section 11.2). validateLearningUnits.ts and the independent package validator check R1, R3, and the uniqueness part of R4 fail-closed (Section 13.3). Since 13 November 2026 canonical Mathematics contains two units with reviewed coverage (R2): a pilot on the dot product with one assessment written for it, and the unit "Understanding and representing natural numbers" with five goals and two assessments. Canonical Physics contains the unit "Modelling motion with constant acceleration" with two goals and one assessment. Review reuse from the frozen prerequisite-reduction proof is decided per goal and does not depend on the learning-unit layer. Still missing: derived recognition at runtime, pass-through of the new fields by the backend API, and a block-cycle check of a unit sequence. Direct cluster references in views A composition view never turns a canonical cluster into an atom; \(\Atoms(g)\) is preserved (GD-X09). At audited state 68db5bf499, LearnerService and CompletionCanonicalGraphResolver still treat direct goalEntry references to canonical clusters as childless runtime atoms; fix and native verification remain open. Personal Curriculum scope (\(L=\Closure(S)\)) Valid seed targets \(S\) are closed on the unpruned canonical graph (\(L=\Closure(S)\)), fixed independently of mastery, and assigned derived target roles for necessary prerequisite atoms. Implemented in backend (PersonalCurriculumLearningScope.java) and WebGUI (cacf323919) with local regressions; full native, curriculum, and remote-CI acceptance plus applicability validation of the current state remain separate. Since b511654efb (11 November 2026), a learning context whose canonical graph is not strictly compilable keeps its reviewed seed scope without derived closure and claims no learning basis. Focus and filter modes (normal vs. strict) Level 3 focus narrows candidate goals while keeping Level 2 denominator \(L\) fixed; normal mode checks prerequisites inside focus, strict mode checks globally; focus widening is offered only after actual focus completion. Implemented in learner runtime and WebGUI over explicit \(M\); does not yet evaluate \(\Meff\) and remains subject to the isCoreForPrereqs and goalEntry boundaries above. Didactic routes (\(O_k o a o Z_k\)) Every non-exempt atomic goal lies on a direct atomic prerequisite path from an orientation anchor to a terminal autonomy goal within its route profile. CQR-101/102/103 are directly hard-enforced in all twelve configured QA profiles across ten Gymnasium subjects; CQR-102 checks atomic reachability. CQR-104 enforces endpoint visibility only in eight of those twelve scopes. In the follow-up working state, the stronger semantic route check GVR-012 applies to four scopes: Mathematics lower/upper secondary, Biology and Physics upper secondary. Two other scopes have route findings (Physics lower secondary 5, Chemistry 3); six scopes lack complete current ledgers. Curricula without route profiles cap at M2. The earlier mainline state 2129b207f4 evidences the delivered baseline; it is not CI evidence for later changes. The Product Owner decision of 13 November 2026 requires every scope of subjects obligated to meet M7 in future (currently seven), with activation only after evidence-backed gap closure. Current coverage is four of seven M7 scopes, or four of twelve inventory scopes; five M6 scopes become mandatory on later promotion to M7. The twelve-scope diagnostic remains separate from this future promotion check. The Physics lane now also includes reviewed explicit stage targets. Another 43 upper-secondary targets inherited only through subtrees remain separate alignment debt, 42 without terminal routes; this is not complete stage-target coverage. Assessment tasks and application coverage Releasing assessments must require independent application of every recognized essential competence under every passing score combination (GD-A08). CQR-201–CQR-203 directly require passing results for examData presence, non-placeholder readiness, and metadata in all twelve pinned QA scopes, without proving live session grading or non-compensability of every passing rubric combination. CQR-104 checks general endpoint visibility in eight of twelve pinned scopes. Its additional binding of every coveredGoalIds entry to a visible prerequisite path (related to R3) still applies only to terminal assessments of canonical Economics; expanding visibility alone does not close R3 outside this domain. For own assessments of authored learning units, validate:learning-units enforces R3 fail-closed and checks claimed coverage reviews (the unit's coverageReviews) against the current task and rubric hashes; it does not establish R2. Optional acquisition and time planning Optional calendar periods verify structural completion witnesses over \(B_\pi\) and \(\Work+\Reserve\le\Budget\) only under explicitly declared estimation assumptions \(\Theta_\pi\). Optional planning profile (GD-P01–GD-P11); no productive curriculum or runtime budget gate is claimed, and weight never denotes minutes. Cumulative progress vs. period completions Cumulative plan progress counts \(\lvert T_{\mathrm{Plan}}\cap\Meff vert\) (with an optional clearly labelled explicit-only plan counter \(\lvert T_{\mathrm{Plan}}\cap M vert\)), while active periods count only reliably dated explicit completions. Current Cockpit and velocity views count explicit completion events; segmented explicit/implicit accounting awaits implementation of \(\Meff\). Maturity levels M0–M7 and quality floors Automated phase-1 curriculum QA M0–M7 remains strictly separated from human sign-off, learner trials, and runtime conformance. CI protects ten Gymnasium subjects via checkCurriculumMaturityFloors.ts (5 at M7, 5 at M6) plus status-file diffing; unfloored experimental landscapes remain reportable at M0, and docs/**-only changes are exempted in ci.yml.

Inspectable code anchors. PersonalCurriculumLearningScope.java; CompletionEvaluator.java; LearnerService.java; useSrsMastery.ts; validateGraph.ts; validateLearningUnits.ts; learningUnitContracts.ts; learningUnitRecognition.ts; Mastery.java. The linked main branch continues to evolve. The generated build manifest binds the exact input files read during each document build via SHA-256.

Sources: AGENTS.md, §2; completion-semantics-clarification-2026-11-04.md; dual-curriculum-package-implementation-status.md; PersonalCurriculumLearningScope.java; CompletionEvaluator.java.

docs.title: Appendix C — Verification Strategy for Completion Semantics
docs.text:
The accompanying script check-assessment-model.py is a mathematical reference check written with the Python standard library alone. It verifies the formulas from Section 13 across small finite models, reads no learner data, and mutates no runtime state (GD-D04).

  • Finite model checking. Every topologically ordered DAG of up to four vertices under every assignment of explicit mastery and protected sets where local content goals have complete local assessment coverage: \(5\,222\) valid cases. Graph traversal and static transitive closure yield the identical implicit set \(I_U\).
  • Minimality. Transitive reduction is minimal and preserves closure. Redundant edges of the normalized relation do not alter recognition. The older inheritance counterexample diagnoses transitional data; this bounded model test does not replace complete G17 validation of the current catalog (GD-D05).
  • Global monotonicity. Under fixed valid contracts, additional explicit mastery never reopens effectively mastered work. Assessment and memory goals are never implicitly passed (GD-D06).
  • Recursive units. \(128\) state assignments of the Mechanics example verify completion \(\Complete(U)\), own recognition \(I_U\), and explicit child obligations. A pure aggregate requires no own assessment; a pure parent synthesis requires no new content goals.
  • Unit block grouping. \(948\) grouping cases compare the unit-block DAG against a complete block sequence. One counterexample exhibits an acyclic atomic DAG whose coarse block summary forms a cycle; no technical entry-lock policy is derived from it.
  • Concrete counterexamples. No stopping barrier at mastered intermediate goals; local recognition preserved despite an open later assessment; durable union across contracts, future prerequisites, intersection with planned target sets, and external support outside \(\Own(U)\).
  • Invalid inputs. Cycles, unknown references, and uncovered local content goals fail closed as errors rather than defaulting to automatic mastery.

Diagram generation in generate-completion-diagrams.py verifies the concrete sets displayed in each figure and compares freshly rendered PNG bytes in --check mode (GD-D07). These model and diagram checks verify neither real task quality, grading reliability, identity verification, nor pedagogical effectiveness. Required independent subject-matter content review remains a separate step; runtime integration and its security, concurrency, and UI tests remain separate engineering work.

Sources: check-assessment-model.py; generate-completion-diagrams.py.

docs.title: D.1 Terms
docs.text:
The first table defines the terms in the order in which this specification introduces them and gives the corresponding German terms. The second table lists the mathematical symbols. None of these definitions introduces an additional stored outcome kind: only the binary outcome \(m\) is persisted per atomic goal.

Term Meaning goal (Lernziel, Ziel) Node of the skill graph with a stable UUID identity. atomic goal, atom (atomares Ziel, Atom) Goal without contains children. Only atoms carry a stored learner outcome. cluster goal, cluster (Cluster) Goal with contains children; structures and aggregates content rather than being mastered directly. containment (Containment) The hierarchy formed by authored contains edges. requirement, prerequisite (Anforderung, Voraussetzung) The edge \((g,p)\in R\) is a requirement of \(g\); goal \(p\) is a prerequisite of \(g\). authored, derived (verfasst, abgeleitet) Only the stored edges in \(C\) and \(R\) are authored. Everything else is computed from them. inherited, effective requirement (geerbte, effektive Anforderung) An inherited requirement is one that a goal acquires from a contains ancestor. Effective requirements combine a goal's own and inherited requirements. atomic basis (atomare Basis) For an atom, the goal itself; for a cluster, its atomic descendants. atomic demand (atomarer Bedarf) All atoms that a goal directly or transitively requires, independent of learner state. atomic normal form (atomare Normalform) The property \(R\subseteq A\times A\): all authored requirements connect atomic goals. target state, transitional data (Zielzustand, Übergangsbestand) Target state is the intended state of canonical data: atomic normal form and transitive minimality. Transitional data denotes inventories that still carry cluster requirements. transitive minimality (transitive Minimalität) No authored requirement is already reachable through the remaining requirements. motivation anchor, terminal autonomy goal (Orientierungsanker, terminales Autonomieziel) Starting and ending endpoints of a didactic route. explicit mastery, Mastery (Mastery) The stored explicit outcome of an atomic goal: mastered or not yet mastered. implicit mastery (implizite Beherrschung) Mastery derived from passed assessments of a valid local recognition contract; for content goals it demonstrates independent application. effective mastery, effectively mastered (effektiv beherrscht) Explicitly mastered or implicitly mastered. Both carry equivalent global effect. satisfaction (Erfüllung) A goal or cluster is satisfied when its atomic basis is non-empty and effectively mastered. frontier (Frontier) The next available atomic goals: themselves not yet mastered, with all required atoms satisfied. filter, focus (Filter, Fokus) A filter selects a subset of the skill graph. Focus is a learner's temporary working scope (Level 3). normal (optimistic) mode, strict (pessimistic) mode (Normalmodus, strikter Modus) Normal (optimistic) mode checks prerequisites inside the selected scope; strict mode checks all prerequisites globally. level of personalization (Personalisierungsstufe, Level) Four narrowing levels: base curriculum, Personal Curriculum, focus with one active goal, and global mastery. Personal Curriculum (persönlicher Lehrplan) Committed personal goal selection including its necessary atomic prerequisites at Level 2; fixed independently of mastery under a given configuration. Existing valid recognition counts as satisfied. projection, composition view (Projektion, Kompositionssicht) A projection derives the visible tree for a resolved scope. A composition view explicitly defines that scope's reviewed upper tree structure. projection role (Projektionsrolle) target: selectable learning target of the view. prerequisiteOnly: subject-local prerequisite support; necessary atoms still receive an acquisition target in the full Personal Curriculum. applicability (applicability, Anwendbarkeit) Compiled dimensional metadata specifying in which scopes a goal is visible. program unit, goal placement (programUnits, goalPlacements) Organizational container such as a school year or semester; entry attaching an unchanged goal to such a unit. Kind learningUnit declares a learning unit, and relation own assigns it an atomic goal it owns. goal type, node type (Zieltyp) Pedagogical kind of an atomic goal: content goal, orientation goal, memory goal, or assessment goal. content goal, ordinary subject goal (Inhaltsziel) An ordinary subject-matter learning goal; labelled “ordinary” in figures. verified recall, completion recall (verifizierter Abruf, Abschlussabruf) Controlled unaided recall of a card without prompt hints. Verified completion recall across all required cards completes a memory goal. direct assessment access (direkter Prüfungszugang) A deliberately chosen assessment attempt is not blocked by unmastered preparation. learning unit, child unit, required child (Lerneinheit, Kindeinheit, Pflichtkind) Authorized educational unit with a stated learning outcome; its subunits; the mandatory subunits among them. aggregate, synthesis (Aggregat, Synthese) An aggregate bundles child units without adding its own assessment. A synthesis unit additionally assesses their integration. local recognition contract (lokaler Vertrag) Binds a learning unit's own goals, its curriculum revision, and the subject-reviewed application meaning of its assessments; also called an acquisition contract. unit validity rules R1–R5 (Gültigkeitsregeln) The five conditions of 11 November 2026 without which implicit recognition is unsound: an assessment path for every own ordinary goal (R1), reviewed coverage evidence (R2), coverage only within the assessment's prerequisites (R3), exactly one directly owning unit (R4), and a versioned contract (R5). protected goal (geschütztes Ziel) Assessment or memory goal; never implicitly passed. open demand (offene Nachfrage) A learning unit's still-open protected goals together with their full transitive atomic demand. consumer (Verbraucher) A goal that requires another goal, viewed from that prerequisite. whole-unit prerequisite, entry lock (Einheitsvoraussetzung, Einheitssperre) Explicitly authorized prerequisite between whole learning units; a hard technical access lock derived from it. Whether such locks exist remains undecided. planning period, entry basis, completion witness (Planungsstufe, Eintrittsbasis, Abschlusszeuge) Calendar interval of an optional schedule; competencies assumed present at entry; ordering that proves a period's targets can be acquired step by step. planned target, actual count, cumulative progress (Plan-Soll, IST, Gesamt-IST) Planned target is the scheduled progress of a named scope; actual count is achieved progress. Cumulative actual progress (Gesamt-IST) counts a plan's effectively mastered goals. profile (Profil) Named set of additional constraints that applies only where explicitly selected, such as a route, validator, or planning profile. scope, QA scope (Scope, QA-Scope) The named validation scope of a rule or route profile. gate (Gate) Automated check whose failure blocks a milestone or build. maturity level, milestone (Reifegrad, Meilenstein) Level M0 to M7 of automated curriculum QA; Appendix A refers to them as milestones. M7 is not human effectiveness proof.

docs.title: D.2 Symbols
docs.text:
The following table summarizes all mathematical symbols across the specification (graph core in Sections 1 to 3, learner state and filters in Sections 4 and 5, Personal Curriculum in Section 7, goal types in Section 8, learning units and implicit mastery in Sections 11 and 13, planning in Section 12).

Note on unified notation. Earlier standalone English Markdown drafts used \(D(g)\) for atomic demand, \(U(T)\) for the prerequisite closure of a subset, \(M_A\) for the explicit mastery set, \(M_k\) and \(T_k\) (or \(M\) and \(T\)) for orientation anchors and terminal autonomy goals of a route profile, and \(K\) for memory goals. The unified Single-Source specification standardizes these symbols across both Web and PDF to \(\ReqAtoms(g)\), \(\Closure(T)\), \(M\), \(O_k\) and \(Z_k\) (or \(O\) and \(Z\)), and \(A_{\mathrm{mem}}\), keeping \(K=G\setminus A\) unambiguous for structural clusters and \(M\) unambiguous for explicit mastery. The unchanged static original illustration 06-available-next-goals.png (Figure 8) still shows the historical label \(M_A\), as noted in its caption.

Symbol Meaning \(G\), \(A\), \(K\) Goals, structural atoms, clusters; \(K=G\setminus A\). \(C\), \(R\) Authored edges: containment (contains) and direct requirements (requires). \(X^+\), \(X^{-1}\) Non-empty transitive closure and inverse relation of a relation \(X\). \(\Anc(g)\), \(\Desc(g)\) Ancestors and descendants along contains. \(\Atoms(g)\) Atomic basis; the singleton \(\{g\}\) if \(g\) is atomic, otherwise its atomic descendants. \(\Reff\), \(R_{\mathrm{inherited}}\) Effective requirements and their inherited subset; \(\Pre_{\mathrm{eff}}(g)\) denotes the effective prerequisites of \(g\). \(\Rat\) Fully atomically expanded effective requirement relation, also used in the completion formulas. \(R_A\) Directly authored atomic requirements \(R\cap(A\times A)\). \(B(g)\), \(\ReqAtoms(g)\) Atomic basis of the effective prerequisites of \(g\) and full atomic demand (written \(D(g)\) in earlier standalone English drafts). \(O\), \(Z\), \(E_{\mathrm{route}}\) (\(O_k\), \(Z_k\)) Orientation (motivation) anchors, terminal autonomy goals, and exempt support goals (or per route profile \(k\); written \(M\) and \(T\) or \(M_k\) and \(T_k\) in earlier standalone drafts). \(m\), \(M\) Stored binary state per atomic goal and the set of its explicit successes. \(m(a)=0\) does not rule out implicit mastery. Earlier standalone drafts and static Figures 8 and 9 write \(M_A\). \(\Meff\) Global union of explicit mastery and validly derived implicit mastery. \(\Sat(g,\Meff)\) Satisfaction of an atomic goal or cluster. \(\Frontier\), \(\Frontier_K\) Next available atomic goals; derived cluster availability. \(P(S)\), \(w(a)\) Weighted progress across a goal set \(S\); progress weight of an atomic goal \(a\). \(F\), \(G_F\), \(A_F\) Filter predicate, selected goals, selected atomic goals. \(\Applicability\), \(D\), \(V_d\) Applicability mapping, set of filter dimensions, and value vocabulary of dimension \(d\). In Section 5, \(Q\) denotes the active query selection. \(\Closure(T)\) Selected atomic goals \(T\) together with their full atomic prerequisite demand (written \(U(T)\) in earlier standalone drafts). \(S\), \(L\) Union of valid atomic seed targets across the selected reviewed subject scopes and the resulting closed Personal Curriculum learning scope \(L=\Closure(S)\) at Level 2. \(\Frontier_{\mathrm{opt}}\), \(\Frontier_{\mathrm{strict}}\) Frontier in normal (optimistic) mode and in strict mode. \(\Missing\), \(\MissingAtoms\) Unsatisfied effective prerequisite nodes; missing atomic goals of the demand. \(\operatorname{Cards}(g)\) Fully resolved valid set of required cards of memory goal \(g\). \(\operatorname{RecallPassed}(g)\) Explicitly verified successful completion recall across \(\operatorname{Cards}(g)\). \(\Score\), \(\Passed\) Score and pass result of an assessment goal; \(\MaxPoints\) and \(\PassingPoints\) come from the scoring rubric. \(U\), \(\Own(U)\), \(T(U)\) Learning unit, directly owned atomic acquisition targets, and total recursive scope including child units; \(\Children(U)\) denotes its required child units. \(\Complete(U)\) Recursively derived unit completion; never an additionally persisted unit-mastery state. \(Q\), \(A_{\mathrm{mem}}\) In Section 13, the sets of atomic assessment goals and atomic memory goals (written \(K\) for memory goals in earlier standalone drafts). \(Q_U\), \(A_{\mathrm{mem},U}\), \(P_U\) Directly owned assessment, memory, and combined protected goal sets; \(A_{\mathrm{mem},U}=\Own(U)\cap A_{\mathrm{mem}}\). \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\Rat}^{*}(X)\) The set \(X\) together with all atomic goals its elements directly or transitively require. \(N_U\) Open demand: full transitive demand of the unit's still-open own protected goals, without stopping at mastered intermediate goals. \(I_U\) Implicit set: directly owned unprotected goals outside \(M\) and \(N_U\). For content goals, it witnesses locally derived independent application. Not an additional stored outcome kind. \(\operatorname{Cov}(q)\) Reviewed coverage claim of an assessment \(q\): the goals whose independent application its tasks and normal grading test; under rule R3 never larger than \(\{b\in A\mid(q,b)\in\Rat^+\}\). Grants no recognition by itself. \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{valid}}\) Person- and revision-bound, durably applicable authoritative local recognition contracts; not merely currently visible units or their latest revisions. \(T_{\mathrm{Plan}}\), \(H_{\mathrm{gesamt}}\) Planned target goal set and count of its effectively mastered goals. \(T_\pi\), \(B_\pi\), \(\ell_\pi\) Planned acquisition targets, entry basis, and optional calendar-bound planning periods; \(n_\pi\) is the number of periods and \(S_i\) is the target set of period \(i\). \(\Rat^{\pi}\), \(\Frontier_\pi\), \(\ReqAtoms_\pi\) Plan requirement relation excluding outgoing requirements of the entry basis; corresponding frontier and atomic demand. \(W^{(r)}\) Hypothetical mastery state of the witness verification algorithm after \(r\) steps. \(\Theta_\pi\), \(\widehat t_h(\Theta_\pi)\) Declared estimation assumptions of the plan and the non-negative duration of activity \(h\) estimated under them; \(\mathcal H_i\) denotes the activities of period \(i\). \(\Work\), \(\Reserve\), \(\Budget\) Scheduled workload, protected reserve, and available time budget of a planning period.

docs.title: Appendix F — Building and Verifying the Specification
docs.text:
All bilingual web pages and PDF editions are compiled from the sole authored source under docs/concept/skill-graph/source/ (source/README.md, spec-manifest.json). The compiler docs/concept/skill-graph/build_spec.py verifies 1:1 structural parity between German (DE) and English (EN), translates chapters and structured JSON datasets into MkDocs Markdown and LuaLaTeX sources, and embeds both the static original illustrations (01–07) and the deterministically generated bilingual bitmap PNGs (00, 08–16) from docs/concept/skill-graph/assets/graph-definition/. From the repository root:

  • python3 docs/concept/skill-graph/build_spec.py --web-and-tex – uses only the Python standard library to verify DE/EN AST parity and generate all bilingual MkDocs web pages plus intermediate LaTeX files under tmp/skill-graph-document/.
  • python3 docs/concept/skill-graph/latex/check-assessment-model.py – runs the finite mathematical reference checks for Section 13.
  • python3 docs/concept/skill-graph/latex/generate-completion-diagrams.py --check – verifies deterministic bilingual PNG diagram rendering without modifying files.
  • python3 docs/concept/skill-graph/build_spec.py --all – runs the parity check, formula model verification, bilingual PNG rendering, Web Markdown emission, and multi-pass LuaLaTeX builds for both the German (skillpilot-graph-definition.pdf, skillpilot-graph-definition.de.pdf) and English (skillpilot-graph-definition.en.pdf) PDFs together with .build.json manifests (GD-D11).

Python 3 alone suffices for --web-and-tex and the formula verifier; full --all runs additionally require Matplotlib and LuaLaTeX with German (ngerman) and English (english) Babel support plus preamble packages. Multi-pass LaTeX compilation resolves cross-references, and generated .build.json manifests bind input files, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, tool versions, and output PDF digests via SHA-256. Byte-for-byte PDF identity across different TeX Live versions is not guaranteed. All generated Web Markdown pages, generated diagram PNGs (00, 08–16), intermediate .tex files, PDFs, and build manifests are .gitignored build artifacts and must never be edited by hand or committed to Git.

Complete document verification requires an error-free build, resolved cross-references, inspection for overfull or underfull boxes, and visual inspection of both generated PDFs (GD-D12). Technical specification prose, schemas, and build scripts are licensed under Apache-2.0 (LICENSE); own didactic illustrations are licensed under CC-BY-4.0 (LICENSES/CC-BY-4.0.txt, LICENSING.md). Build and formula checks complement document QA and replace neither runtime tests nor independent subject-matter and empirical validation.

Sources: source/README.md; spec-manifest.json; check-assessment-model.py; LICENSING.md.

docs.title: Produktentscheidung: Beherrschung durch Verständnis und selbständige Anwendung
docs.text: 4. November 2026. Dieser Beschluss ersetzt die bisherige Deutung impliziter Erledigung als bloßen Entfall von Vorbereitung. Er gilt für die Konzepte; die bisherige Implementierung ist noch nicht entsprechend korrigiert.

docs.title: Verbindliche Bedeutung
docs.text:
• Transitive Minimalität bleibt erforderlich. Die am 31. Oktober dokumentierte Aufhebung wird zurückgenommen. Die Rechnung muss indirekte Voraussetzungen verstehen, ohne redundante Direktkanten zu verlangen.
  • Direkt erledigt bezeichnet den unmittelbaren Nachweis eines Lernziels, bei gewöhnlichen Kompetenzzielen auf Verständnisebene.
  • Implizit erledigt bezeichnet die durch selbständige Anwendung in den zugehörigen Prüfungen nachgewiesene Beherrschung. Es ist keine Freistellung und kein schwächerer Abschluss.
  • Erledigt ist erledigt: Beide Nachweiswege erfüllen spätere Voraussetzungen und zählen zum Gesamtfortschritt. Eine spätere offene Prüfung, ein Fokuswechsel oder ein anderer ausgewählter Lehrplan nimmt die Anerkennung nicht zurück.
  • Gespeichert bleibt pro atomarem Ziel ausschließlich das binäre Ergebnis. Effektive Beherrschung wird aus expliziten Ergebnissen und festen fachlichen Abschlussverträgen abgeleitet. Es gibt keine zusätzlichen Mastery-Stufen, Freistellungsdatensätze oder qualifizierenden Prüfbelege.
  • Prüfungs- und Lernkartenziele bleiben selbst explizit zu erledigen. Für sie gelten die normalen Bewertungs- beziehungsweise Recall-Regeln.

docs.title: Lokale Begründung, globale Wirkung
docs.text:
Eine autoritativ bestimmte Lerneinheit hat ein Lernversprechen, einen motivierenden Auftakt und einen überprüfbaren Abschluss. Sie enthält eigene Ziele und kann weitere Lerneinheiten bündeln. Der Begriff ersetzt das zuvor verwendete curriculare „Level“; Personalisierungsstufen, Schwierigkeitsgrad und QA-Reife bleiben eigenständige Begriffe.

Jedes Erwerbsziel ist innerhalb des aufgelösten Kurses genau einer Einheit direkt zugeordnet. Deren Anerkennungsvertrag umfasst die eigenen Ziele und sämtliche eigenen Prüfungs- und Lernkartenpflichten. Er berücksichtigt volle transitive Anforderungen, auch über bereits gemeisterte Zwischenziele hinweg. Ein beliebiger Baum- oder Fokusfilter definiert keinen solchen Vertrag.

Einheit U: Prüfung Q1 ──requires──▶ B ──requires──▶ A
Einheit V: Prüfung Q2 ──requires──▶ C ──requires──▶ A

Ist nur das gewöhnliche B gemeistert, bleibt A für die offene Q1 erforderlich. Besteht die Person Q1 und sind damit sämtliche für A und B relevanten eigenen Pflichten erfüllt, gelten A und B als durch Anwendung gemeistert. Die offene Q2 verhindert dies nicht. Beim späteren Lernen von C ist A bereits erfüllt. Es wird weder erneut als offen verlangt noch als zweites Ziel gezählt.

Eine weitere offene Prüfung derselben direkt zugeordneten Einheit kann die Anerkennung von A hingegen noch verhindern. Eine unabhängige offene Kartenpflicht hält den vollständigen Einheitsabschluss offen, aber nicht automatisch jede bereits belegte Kompetenz. Ausgewählte Prüfungs- und Kartenpflichten dürfen nicht aus der Rechnung herausgefiltert werden.

docs.title: Rekursive Einheiten und größere Abschlüsse
docs.text:
Eine größere Einheit ist abgeschlossen, wenn ihre verpflichtenden Untereinheiten und eigenen Zielpflichten erfüllt sind. Der Abschluss wird abgeleitet; es gibt keinen zusätzlichen gespeicherten Modul-Mastery-Zustand. Eine übergeordnete Prüfung kann das selbständige Zusammenspiel bereits erworbener Kompetenzen prüfen. Reine Bündelung braucht keine zusätzliche Prüfung.

Eine offene übergeordnete Prüfung öffnet abgeschlossene Untereinheiten nicht wieder. Umgekehrt besteht sie weder deren Prüfungen noch deren Karten implizit. Eltern bündeln die Zielmengen ihrer Kinder, erhalten dadurch aber keinen neuen Anerkennungsvertrag über alle Nachkommen. Eigene neue Kompetenzen brauchen einen eigenen gültigen Anwendungsnachweis. Gemeinsame Voraussetzungen behalten ihre Identität und werden nicht mehrfach erworben.

Das gilt auch für den motivationalen Auftakt: Er erklärt Zweck und Lernversprechen, belegt aber selbst keine Fachkompetenz. Ein abgeleiteter Orientierungsabschluss behauptet keine tatsächlich stattgefundene motivierende Interaktion.

Eine ausdrücklich gesetzte Abhängigkeit zwischen ganzen Einheiten kann deren Ablauf strukturieren. Eine einzelne atomare Voraussetzung erzeugt diese stärkere Pflicht nicht automatisch. Ob solche Abhängigkeiten Empfehlungen oder technische Startblockaden sind und ob direkte Prüfungsversuche davon betroffen sind, bleibt bewusst offen. Die Einteilung muss einen möglichen Ablauf zulassen; atomare Zyklenfreiheit allein garantiert noch keine zyklusfreie Folge ganzer Einheiten.

Die normative Abschlussrechnung definiert die Mengen und die Verbindung zur Graph-Definition. Lerneinheiten beschreiben die rekursive Struktur; Abhängigkeiten und Lernweg erläutern die separate Entscheidung über Zugang und Reihenfolge. Die Umsetzung folgt später.

docs.title: Verbindliche Anforderung an Prüfungen
docs.text:
Die Aufgaben und normalen Bewertungsregeln müssen gemeinsam die selbständige Anwendung aller dadurch anerkannten Kompetenzen absichern. Ein Voraussetzungspfad, die Erwähnung einer Kompetenz oder ein angeleiteter Rechenschritt genügt nicht. Der unabhängige fachliche Review fragt:

Kann die relevante Prüfungsmenge bestanden werden, obwohl eine wesentliche dadurch anerkannte Kompetenz nicht selbständig angewandt wurde?

Wenn ja, muss Aufgabe, normale Bestehensregel oder Einheitszuschnitt korrigiert werden. Ein völlig fehlender wesentlicher Bestandteil darf nicht durch Punkte aus anderen Bereichen ausgeglichen werden, während dieser Bestandteil als beherrscht anerkannt wird. Nicht jede einzelne Prüfung muss alles doppelt prüfen; maßgeblich ist die für die Anerkennung erforderliche Prüfungsmenge. Dies ist eine Autorenpflicht, kein zweites Laufzeit-Bestehensverfahren.

Bestehende Prüfungen und frühere M7-Freigaben belegen diesen stärkeren Vertrag nicht automatisch. Eine Prüfungsziel-ID muss eine stabile Anerkennungsbedeutung behalten. Spätere Kanten oder Programmvarianten dürfen alten Ergebnissen keine zusätzlichen Kompetenzen zuschreiben. Gleichwertige Aufgabenformen können denselben Vertrag erfüllen; eine veränderte Anerkennungsbedeutung benötigt eine eigene Prüfungsidentität oder eine ausdrücklich geprüfte Migration. Die technische Ausgestaltung gehört in die spätere Umsetzungsplanung.

docs.title: Darstellung und Planung
docs.text:
Grüne und blaue Symbole dürfen den Nachweisweg unterscheiden; beide stehen für erledigte Ziele. Ein Tooltip erklärt den direkten Nachweis beziehungsweise den Nachweis selbständiger Anwendung. Wiederholen bleibt freiwillig möglich.

Gesamtfortschritt zählt eindeutige effektiv beherrschte Ziele innerhalb seines Zielumfangs. „Nur explizit erreichte Lernziele zählen“ ändert allein die Plananrechnung. Tages- und Wochenpensum zählen weiterhin nur tatsächliche explizite Abschlussereignisse. Anerkennung erzeugt keine künstlichen Ereignisse oder Datumsangaben. Siehe Lernplanstatus.

docs.title: Vereinbarte Reihenfolge
docs.text:
1. Konzepte einschließlich LaTeX, Abbildungen und PDF auf frischer main-Basis konsolidieren und unabhängig prüfen.
  2. Anschließend die Umsetzung neu planen.
  3. Erst danach wiederverwendbare Teile des bisherigen PR prüfen. Die alte Curriculum- und Runtimearbeit wird nicht einfach fortgesetzt.

Dieser Stand ändert keine Produktionsdaten und behauptet weder einen passenden produktiven Runtime noch eine bereits erfolgte Neuprüfung der Curricula.

docs.title: Bestätigung vom 11. November 2026
docs.text:
Der Product Owner hat die hier beschriebene Anerkennungsregel am 11. November 2026 bestätigt: Ein eigenes gewöhnliches Ziel gilt als anerkannt, sobald keine offene eigene Prüfung und kein offenes eigenes Memorierziel seiner direkt zuständigen Einheit es noch benötigt. Gehören Q1 und Q2 zur selben Einheit und setzen beide A voraus, bleibt A nach bestandener Q1 offen, bis auch Q2 bestanden ist.

Die auf dem archivierten Branch von Pull Request #83 als „Zielentscheidung vom 6. November 2026“ geführte Alternative wurde geprüft und nicht übernommen: sofortige Anerkennung aus der qualifizierten Deckungsliste einer einzelnen bestandenen Prüfung, auch als Nachweis durch eine Eltern- oder Fremdeinheit.

Tragfähig ist die Regel nur in Einheiten, die die Gültigkeitsregeln R1–R5 erfüllen: Prüfungspfad für jedes eigene gewöhnliche Ziel, geprüfter Deckungsnachweis, Deckung nur innerhalb der Voraussetzungen der Prüfung, genau eine direkt zuständige Einheit und versionierter Vertrag. Wortlaut und Verortung der Regeln stehen in Graph-Definition §13.3.

docs.title: Hinweis vom 12. November 2026
docs.text: Dieser Beschluss bleibt unverändert. Die technische Darstellung ist inzwischen festgelegt: Lerneinheiten liegen in der Platzierungsschicht ihrer Skill-Landschaft (Graph-Definition §11.2), der Curriculum-Paketvertrag 1.2 trägt sie, und der Arbeitsplan ist Lerneinheiten für Mathematik und Physik. Die Completion-Profile und -Scopes des Paketvertrags 1.1 setzen noch die hier abgelöste Freistellungsdeutung um und bleiben nur bis zur Umstellung der Runtime in Betrieb.

docs.title: 5. Content Integration: Architectural Framework
docs.text: This chapter establishes the binding v1.1 architectural framework (Product Owner decision of 21 September 2026, GitHub Issue #50; PoC details in Physik-Libre PoC, PoC Operations, and Issue #54 Content Packages).

docs.title: 5.1. Three-Layer Separation and Personal Selection
docs.text:
Canonical Skill Graph (provider-neutral goalIds)
        ^
        |  referenced from outside via content/ packages
Optional Content-Link Packages (textbooks, simulations, tasks)
        ^
        |  activated per learner via ordinary SkillPilot ID
Personal Material Selection (Cockpit & Coach, default opt-in/off)

Core architectural invariants:

  • Provider-neutral canonical core: Canonical landscapes never hardcode or privilege external textbook, video, or publisher URLs; content packages under content/ point inward to stable canonical goalIds.
  • Ordinary SkillPilot-ID personalization: Learners select or deselect optional content packages directly in their ordinary Cockpit profile without special activation keys, teacher accounts, or third-party logins.
  • Operational kill-switch & privacy: Every external content package can be disabled centrally via an operational kill-switch without touching canonical landscapes or learner mastery. Outbound links remain plain, parameter-free URLs without SkillPilot IDs or tracking tokens; SkillPilot relicenses no third-party content.

docs.title: 5.2. Physics Pilot and Four Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
The initial reference pilot binds open-licensed physics textbook sections (https://physikbuch.schule/) after Physics M7 stabilization and expands to Mathematics and LEIFIphysik under Issue #54. Every content-package integration is judged against four binding acceptance criteria:

Criterion Required Proof 1. Unchanged core Disabling or removing all content/ packages leaves canonical graphs, views, frontier logic, and mastery 100% intact. 2. Personal selection Learners control package visibility through their ordinary SkillPilot profile without special keys or accounts. 3. Concrete utility Active links resolve to goal-specific reading or practice sections and appear cleanly in Cockpit and Coach contexts without fabricated page summaries. 4. General viability Adding a second provider or subject requires only a declarative content/ package and validation pass, zero core schema changes.

docs.text: Dieses Kapitel definiert den verbindlichen Architekturrahmen v1.1 (Product-Owner-Entscheidung vom 21. September 2026, GitHub Issue #50; PoC- und Ausbaudetails unter Physik-Libre-PoC, PoC-Betrieb und Content-Pakete zu Issue #54).

docs.title: 5.1. Dreischichtige Entkopplung und persönliche Auswahl
docs.text:
Kanonischer Skill-Graph (anbieterneutrale goalIds)

        |  von aussen referenziert ueber content/-Pakete

Persoenliche Materialauswahl (Cockpit & Coach, jederzeit abschaltbar)

Verbindliche Architekturprinzipien:

  • Anbieterneutraler Kern: Kanonische Landschaften enthalten und bevorzugen keine externen Lehrbuch-, Video- oder Verlags-URLs; Contentpakete unter content/ verweisen von außen auf stabile kanonische goalIds.
  • Personalisierung über die normale SkillPilot-ID: Lernende aktivieren oder deaktivieren optionale Materialpakete im regulären Cockpit-Profil ohne Sonder-Keys, Lehrer-Accounts oder Drittanbieter-Logins.
  • Betriebsschalter (Kill-Switch) & Datenschutz: Jedes externe Contentpaket lässt sich zentral per Betriebsschalter deaktivieren, ohne kanonische Graphen oder Lernstände zu verändern. Ausgespielte Links sind parameterfreie Plain-URLs ohne SkillPilot-ID oder Tracking-Token; Drittinhalte werden nicht umlizenziert.

docs.title: 5.2. Physik-Pilot und vier Abnahmekriterien
docs.text:
Der erste Referenzpilot bindet offen lizenzierte Physikbuch-Abschnitte (https://physikbuch.schule/) nach der Physik-M7-Stabilisierung an und wird in Issue #54 auf Mathematik und LEIFIphysik erweitert. Jede Contentanbindung wird an vier verbindlichen Kriterien gemessen:

Kriterium Geforderter Nachweis 1. Unveränderter Kern Das Abschalten oder Entfernen aller content/-Pakete lässt kanonische Graphen, Views, Frontier-Logik und Mastery zu 100 % unberührt. 2. Persönliche Auswahl Lernende steuern die Sichtbarkeit über ihr normales SkillPilot-Profil ohne Sonder-Keys oder Zusatzkonten. 3. Konkrete Funktion Aktive Links führen zielgenau auf passende Kapitel/Aufgaben und erscheinen sauber in Cockpit und Coach ohne erfundene Seiteninhalte. 4. Allgemeine Tragfähigkeit Ein zweiter Anbieter oder ein weiteres Fach benötigt nur ein deklaratives content/-Paket samt Validierung, keine Kernschema-Änderung.
