Bei abgewiesener OpenAI-Clientauthentifizierung zeigt client_auth_method ausschließlich eine feste Klasse der empfangenen Authentifizierung: NONE, SECRET_BASIC, SECRET_POST, JWT_ASSERTION, OTHER oder UNKNOWN. JWT_ASSERTION besagt nur, dass Spring einen JWT-Assertion-Versuch erkannt hat; es bestätigt weder eine gültige Signatur noch eine akzeptierte Anmeldemethode. Ohne klassifizierten Ablehnungsversuch bleibt das Feld UNKNOWN. CLIENT_METHOD_REJECTED unterscheidet eine unzulässige Methode von fehlender Clientregistrierung (CLIENT_REGISTRATION_NOT_FOUND), fehlenden Zugangsdaten (CLIENT_CREDENTIALS_MISSING), abgewiesenem Secret (CLIENT_SECRET_REJECTED), Code-Ablehnung (AUTHORIZATION_CODE_REJECTED) und PKCE-Ablehnung (PKCE_REJECTED). Diese Zuordnung verwendet nur exakt bekannte Spring-Fehler; unbekannte Fehler bleiben CLIENT_AUTHENTICATION_REJECTED. Spezifische JWT-/Policy-Diagnosen behalten Vorrang. Niemals freie Exception-Texte, Client-IDs, Secrets, Assertions, Codes oder PKCE-Verifier protokollieren. Eine Methodenabweichung anhand der App-Konfiguration und dieses Nachweises beheben; ein abgewiesenes vertrauliches Profil darf nicht auf none ausweichen.

Die gemeinsame Readiness-Gruppe umfasst readinessState,db; die getrennte Gruppe openaiReadiness zusätzlich openAiDeCoach. Damit darf ein ausschließlich gestörtes OpenAI-JWT-Profil nicht die gesamte Anwendung samt Claude oder dem konfigurierten Basic-Übergang aus dem gemeinsamen Traffic nehmen. Betreiber müssen unterscheiden, welche Probe sie für welchen Eingang verwenden: /actuator/health/readiness für die gemeinsame Instanz, /actuator/health/openaiReadiness als zusätzliche OpenAI-Bereitschaftsdiagnose. Eine grüne gemeinsame Probe ist keine OpenAI-Freigabe; eine gestörte OpenAI-Probe darf nicht als globales Claude-Abschaltsignal verdrahtet werden. Diese internen Betriebsproben nicht ungeschützt ins Internet stellen.

docs.title: Störungen und sichere Wiederherstellung
docs.text:
Beobachtung Gezielte Diagnose Sichere Reaktion Nur JWT nicht verfügbar / clientMetadataReady=false Zugelassene CIMD-/JWKS-Quelle, DNS/TLS, begrenzter Abruf, Metadatenpins und Uhr prüfen JWT geschlossen lassen; Hintergrundprüfung beobachten; kein none-Fallback; andere aktive Profile unabhängig prüfen invalid_client Wirkliches Profil, exakt verwendete Methode, Client-/Callbackkonfiguration und Credential-Hinterlegung prüfen Keine fremde Registrierung übernehmen; Secret nie in Logs kopieren; nur betroffene vertrauliche Lane koordiniert reparieren invalid_grant nach Migration Profilrevision, erwartetes Reconnectfenster, Ablauf/PKCE und Replay unterscheiden Neuen regulären Verbindungsflow starten; keinen alten Grant nachmarkieren oder retired-Datensatz löschen REFRESH_REUSED Betroffene synthetisch/operativ identifizierte Verbindung und Korrelationskennungen prüfen; Token selbst nicht exportieren Familie bleibt widerrufen; Hostverbindung neu aufbauen; bei Leck zusätzlich Credential-/Lernsession-Umfang klären Datenbankfehler oder Lock-Timeout DB-Erreichbarkeit, Migration, Transaktionsdauer und betroffene Instanzen prüfen Fail-closed erhalten; keine In-Memory-Ersatzpolicy; betroffene Route nötigenfalls drainen und DB-Ursache beheben MCP-401/403 trotz „verbunden“ Access-Ablauf, Provider/Audience/Scope und danach getrennt Lernsession/State prüfen OAuth-Reconnect und neue Lernsession nur jeweils bei deren tatsächlichem Fehler; keine Scope-/Sessionprüfung abschalten Secret oder Zugang kompromittiert Betroffene Clientregistrierung bzw. Verbindung begrenzen; Betriebsverantwortlichen einbeziehen Clientzugang sperren/rotieren und bei nötiger Gesamtinvalidierung neue betroffene Profilrevision setzen; andere Profile nicht pauschal zurückstufen

Incident-Reihenfolge: (1) Zeitpunkt, Build, Profil und bereinigte Fehlerbelege sichern; (2) nur betroffenen Zugang begrenzen, bei unklarer Providerreichweite alle zugehörigen Routen/Instanzen schließen; (3) Ursache und Credentialumfang klären; (4) vorher akzeptierte Konfiguration mit erforderlicher neuer Revision koordiniert bereitstellen; (5) neue Verbindung, negativen Altzugang, unveränderte andere Profile und Lernbetrieb nachprüfen; (6) tatsächliche Ergebnisse im Release-/Incidentbeleg festhalten. Keine automatischen Produktionsänderungen aus einem Diagnosecheck ableiten.

docs.title: Profilbezogener Rollback
docs.text:
Rollback heißt gezielte Sperrung oder vorher akzeptierte Konfiguration mit neuer Profilrevision, wenn die alte stillgelegt wurde. Alte Grants dürfen nicht wieder gültig werden; betroffene Nutzer ggf. neu verbinden. Andere Profile bleiben verfügbar. Keine JWT-/PKCE-/Token-/Sessionprüfung abschalten, um einen Fehler zu umgehen.

Das Entfernen eines Profils aus einer ausdrücklich geladenen Provider- Konfiguration stilllegt seine Revision. Ein auf einem neuen Prozess überhaupt nicht geladener Provider wird dagegen nicht automatisch in der gemeinsamen Datenbank stillgelegt: Andere dedizierte Prozesse dürfen ihn weiterhin betreiben. Für eine vollständige Provider-Sperre deshalb dessen gesamte Zugangsroute und alte Instanzen gezielt sperren/drainen; nicht annehmen, ein lokales Feature-Flag widerrufe bereits alle anderen Verbindungen.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
OpenAI mit zwei JWKS-Sätzen testen: neue kid nach begrenzter Aktualisierung erkannt, entfernte Schlüssel nach Cache-/Überlappungszeit abgelehnt. Abruffehler erlauben keinen Public-Fallback. Keine sofortige Revokation behaupten, solange ein gültiger Cache den alten Schlüssel enthält.

Claude-Secrets auf allen Instanzen koordiniert wechseln. Jede Instanz bindet sich an den bei Registrierung gespeicherten bcrypt-Wert; veraltete Knoten müssen ablehnen. Bei Kompromittierung zusätzlich Profilrevision erhöhen und Grants invalidieren. Bei Routine-Rotation Grants nur erhalten, wenn die Policy das ausdrücklich zulässt. Custom-Rotation koordiniert der Betreiber; Anthropic-held benötigt die tatsächliche Übergabe an Anthropic.

docs.title: ChatGPT-mTLS bleibt getrennt
docs.text: Die bestehende V1-Edge gesondert prüfen: nur dedizierter OpenAI-Zugang, vertrauenswürdige Zertifikatsprüfung, keine ungeprüften Identitätsheader. observe beweist kein enforce. Vor Aktivierung akzeptierten/abgelehnten Transport und ungestörten Claude-Zugriff nachweisen. Kein globaler OpenAI-Zertifikatszwang auf dem Claude-Zugang. OpenAI: Authentication

docs.title: 6. Reproduzierbare automatisierte Nachweise
docs.text:
Der Workflow OAuth client authentication läuft bei relevanten Pushes/PRs, täglich und manuell. Er nutzt synthetische Clients und wegwerfbares PostgreSQL 15; keine Produktionssecrets, realen Lernprofile oder bezahlten Modellaufrufe.

Ebene Nachweis Provider Exakte Methoden/Clients, Discovery/Redirects, Code/PKCE, Refresh, JWT, MCP-/Providergrenzen Policy Unabhängige Profile, keine Grant-Aufwertung, persistierte Revision, kein Downgrade Replay/Refresh Einmalverbrauch, Rotation, Wiederverwendung, betroffener Familienwiderruf/Isolation PostgreSQL Echte Migration, konkurrierender Verbrauch, mehrere Instanzen/Neustart, persistierte Policy CI-Gatter Pflichtsuiten tatsächlich ausgeführt; fehlende/leere/übersprungene/fehlerhafte Berichte sind kein Pass Release-Gatter Gewähltes Profil, exakter Commit/Revision, unveränderte Artefakte, separate Host-Abnahme

Mit Corretto aus .java-version/.corretto-version und Node aus .nvmrc:

node --test scripts/oauth_client_auth_ci.test.mjs scripts/check_oauth_profile_release.test.mjs
node --test scripts/validate_openai_v1_runtime_config.test.mjs
node scripts/check_oauth_profile_release.mjs

Backend-Testfilter stehen im Workflow. Für ausschließlich lokales wegwerfbares PostgreSQL SKILLPILOT_OAUTH_POSTGRES_TEST_ENABLED=true sowie SKILLPILOT_OAUTH_TEST_POSTGRES_URL, ..._USER und ..._PASSWORD konfigurieren. Nie Produktions-DSNs verwenden. Das Fixture erstellt/entfernt nur sein eigenes neues Schema. XML-/HTML-Berichte bleiben 30 Tage mit Commit-/Run-ID erhalten. Lokales PostgreSQL 18.1 und CI-PostgreSQL 15 sind getrennte Nachweise. Eine Backend-Suite beweist keine echte Herstellerintegration.

docs.title: Code- und Testanker für Review und Wartung
docs.text:
Die Links zeigen den Entwicklungszweig. Für eine Freigabe dieselben Pfade im belegten Commit prüfen. Die benannten Klassen sind ausführbare Regressionsnachweise, nicht ein Ersatz für das Lesen ihrer Assertions.

Sicherheitsvertrag Implementierung Automatisierter Nachweis Unabhängige Revisionen, Migration, unveränderliche Grantidentität/-codes AuthenticatedClientPolicy IndependentClientProfilePolicyTest Einmaliger Codeaustausch und Sperrreihenfolge OAuthAuthorizationCodeExchangeGuard OAuthAuthorizationCodeExchangeGuardTest Widerruf umfasst Tokens, nicht Code oder State OAuthTokenRevocationBoundary OAuthTokenRevocationBoundaryTest Assertionverbrauch bleibt nach Fehler/Neustart gesperrt JdbcOAuthClientAssertionReplayStore JdbcOAuthClientAssertionReplayStoreTest Mehrere Instanzen, echte DB-Migration/-Sperren Dieselben JDBC-Dienste; keine lokale Ersatzimplementierung OAuthClientSecurityPostgresIntegrationTest JWT und ausdrücklicher Basic-Übergang ohne Methodenfallback OpenAiDeOAuthConfiguration und OpenAiDeClientProfiles OpenAiDeClientProfilesTest, OpenAiDePrivateKeyJwtFlowIntegrationTest JWT-Signatur/Claims/Audience/Zeiten/Schlüssel OpenAiDeJwtClientAssertionValidator OpenAiDeJwtClientAssertionValidatorTest Begrenzte CIMD-Bereitschaft ohne globalen Ausfall OpenAiDeCimdMetadataGate, application.yml OpenAiDeCimdMetadataGateTest, OpenAiDeCoachHealthIndicatorTest Claude-Profile und exakte Konfiguration ClaudeV1ClientPolicy, ClaudeV1Properties, ClaudeV1OAuthConfiguration ClaudeV1ConfidentialOAuthIntegrationTest, ClaudeV1ConfidentialPostOAuthIntegrationTest Public-Claude-Rotation und Familienwiderruf ClaudeV1RefreshTokenFamilies, ClaudeV1FamilyAuthorizationService ClaudeV1PublicRefreshFamilyIntegrationTest, ClaudeV1RefreshTokenFamiliesTest Providertrennung in gemeinsamen OAuth-Tabellen ProviderScopedOAuth2AuthorizationService plus providergebundene Client-Repositories/Introspektoren CombinedProviderOAuthIsolationIntegrationTest Geheimnisfreie, zuordenbare Diagnostik OAuthProfileDiagnostics und OAuthProfileDiagnosticsFilter OAuthProfileDiagnosticsFilterTest

Die App-only-Principals sind direkt in OpenAiDeBindingAuthenticationFilter und ClaudeV1AppAuthenticationFilter nachlesbar. Die danach weiterhin erforderliche Claude-Lernsessiongrenze steht in ClaudeV1SessionCoordinator mit ClaudeV1SessionCoordinatorTest. Änderungen an OAuth dürfen diese fachlich unabhängige Grenze nicht entfernen.

Bei Änderungen dieses Runbooks zusätzlich vom Repository-Wurzelverzeichnis:

npm --prefix app run check:docs-links
npm --prefix app run check:docs-indexes
git diff --check

Schema-/Linktests prüfen Konsistenz. Sie beweisen weder die Sicherheits- korrektheit eines neuen Algorithmus noch einen echten Herstellerflow.

docs.title: Maschinenlesbare Release-Belege
docs.text:
contracts/oauth/client-profile-release.json führt jede Stufe separat. null bedeutet kein an einen Release-Commit gebundener Beleg, nicht zwangsläufig fehlender Quellcode. Der Initialstand behauptet keine neue Produktionsabnahme. Nur tatsächlich erhobene Belege eintragen; bestehende Produktionszustände nicht nachträglich erfinden.

Zuerst den unveränderlichen Code-Kandidaten committen. Für die anschließende Abnahme eine operative Kopie der Vorlage, etwa tmp/oauth-profile-release-evidence.json, verwenden und mit --ledger auswählen. Dadurch erfordert das Erfassen neuer Nachweise keinen neuen Code-Commit, der die vorher geprüfte Build-ID wieder ändern würde. Die bereinigten Belege anschließend mit dem freigegebenen Release archivieren.

Jede belegte Stufe enthält commit, policyRevision, recordedAt (UTC), result: "passed", ausgeführte checks und evidence mit repository-relativem path plus SHA-256. Artefakte müssen bereinigt tatsächlich vorliegen. JUnit/HTTP-Berichte tragen technical; ein echtes Abnahmeprotokoll trägt realHost. Pflichtprüfungen stehen in requiredHostChecks() im Prüfer.

node scripts/check_oauth_profile_release.mjs \
  --ledger tmp/oauth-profile-release-evidence.json \
  --profile claude-cimd-public \
  --commit GEPRUEFTER_40_STELLIGER_COMMIT \
  --revision GEPRUEFTE_PROFILREVISION

Platzhalter vor Ausführung ersetzen. Nur das gewählte Profil wird auf Bereitschaft geprüft; ausstehendes Anthropic-held ist kein Blocker. Das Gatter führt keinen Deploy oder Produktionskonfigurationswechsel aus. Ein Schema-/Hash-Check belegt unveränderte erfasste Beweise, nicht deren ehrliche Erhebung: Der Verantwortliche muss Simulator und echten Host unterscheiden. production erst nach tatsächlicher Aktivierung und Produktionsprüfung belegen.

docs.title: 7. Herstellerabhängige Restpunkte
docs.text: Die Hersteller-Arbeitspakete führen konkrete Frage, Status und ausschließlich betroffene Funktion. Allgemeine Erlaubnis- fragen zu dokumentierten Verfahren und testbare Callback-/Methodenfragen gehören nicht in langwierige Supportanfragen. Vorbereitete Entwürfe sind nicht versandt; beantwortete Fragen sind noch keine erfolgreiche Integration.

docs.title: OAuth: getrennte Hersteller-Arbeitspakete
docs.text: Stand: 11. September 2026. Diese Arbeitspakete blockieren ausschließlich ihre Erweiterung, nicht die unabhängigen OAuth-Profile. Die Entwürfe wurden nicht versandt. Sie enthalten keine Zugangsdaten.

docs.title: ANTHROPIC-HELD: zentrale Credential-Hinterlegung
docs.text:
Status: Entwurf; extern nicht aktiviert. Kein Directory-Organisationszugang nachgewiesen: Der Betreiber verwendet bisher ein persönliches Pro-/Max-Konto.

Abhängige Funktion: Nur claude-anthropic-held. Öffentliche CIMD-Beta und ein verfügbarer eigener vertraulicher Custom Connector benötigen die Antwort nicht.

Eigener Stand: Backend und synthetische Tests sind separat vorbereitet; noch kein tatsächlicher Anthropic-held-Hosttest. Basic/Post, PKCE, Redirects und Refresh werden mit dem dedizierten Custom-Client selbst geprüft, nicht als allgemeine Herstellerfragen gestellt.

Anthropic ordnet zentral verwahrte Credentials einem Directory-Eintrag zu, nicht einem beliebigen Custom Connector. Anthropic-Dokumentation, Directory/Custom

Versandfertiger Entwurf

To: mcp-review@anthropic.com Subject: SkillPilot — onboarding for Anthropic-held OAuth credentials

Hello MCP Review Team,

We would like to set up Anthropic-held OAuth client credentials for SkillPilot, our learning coach. Its remote MCP endpoint is https://mcp-claude-v1.skillpilot.com/mcp; our Git-distributed SkillPilot Coach plugin references that endpoint. Learners use their own Claude accounts.

We currently have a personal Pro/Max account, not a Team/Enterprise Directory organization. Which onboarding route should we use for Directory submission and credential provisioning in this situation?

Please point us to the provisioning process, including the approved channel for credential handover and subsequent rotation. We also need the configured Directory association to apply when the same endpoint is connected through our plugin by users in their own Claude accounts.

Our independent public-CIMD beta remains separate from this request; the Anthropic-held integration has not yet been activated or host-tested.

Thank you, SkillPilot — https://skillpilot.com

Abschlusskriterium: Zugang/Hinterlegung tatsächlich erfolgt, sichere Betriebsübergabe festgehalten und Installation, Code-Austausch, Refresh, Widerruf sowie Lernbetrieb mit dem zentral hinterlegten Client nachgewiesen. Eine Antwort allein erfüllt die Abnahme nicht.

docs.title: ANTHROPIC-ATTESTATION: optionale stärkere Integrationsbindung
docs.text:
Status: Separater optionaler Entwurf, nicht Teil der ersten Freigabe.

Abhängige Funktion: Zusätzlicher serverprüfbarer Plugin-Herkunftsnachweis beziehungsweise eine andere stärkere Clientbindung. Nicht auf Basis einer vermuteten Schnittstelle implementieren.

Frage für ein späteres getrenntes Ticket: Is there a documented, self-service asymmetric OAuth client-authentication mechanism for hosted Claude connectors, or a server-verifiable attestation binding an MCP request to a specific publisher-controlled plugin/version? If so, please provide the verification contract and registration route.

Eigener Befund: Die dokumentierten CIMD-/Secret-Verfahren liefern keinen Nachweis unveränderter Skill-Dateien. Die erste Ausbaustufe verspricht das nicht. Erst nach dokumentiertem Vertrag und eigenem Test als Funktion einplanen.

docs.title: OPENAI-IDENTITY: optionale Bindung an die konkrete Integration
docs.text:
Status: Entwurf zurückgestellt, bis reale JWT-/Installationsbelege vorliegen. Keine allgemeine Genehmigungsanfrage für dokumentiertes private_key_jwt.

Abhängige Funktion: Nur stärkere Zuordnung zur konkreten SkillPilot- Verteilung/Version, nicht das unabhängig abnehmbare chatgpt-cimd-jwt. Noch kein realer Hosttest des neuen JWT-Profils dokumentiert.

OpenAI dokumentiert eine stabile CIMD-Clientidentität. Das beweist nicht die Identität eines SkillPilot-Plugins. Die exakte ID, Callbacks, Audience, JWKS-Rotation und der externe Beta-Installationsweg werden zunächst selbst geprüft. OpenAI: Client registration

Entwurf für den verfügbaren OpenAI-Entwicklersupportkanal

Subject: SkillPilot — optional server-verifiable binding to a plugin integration

Hello,

We are integrating SkillPilot with ChatGPT using CIMD and mandatory private_key_jwt. Our authorization server independently checks the allowed client identity and published signing keys. We understand this authenticates the OAuth client, not the contents of our plugin.

Is there a documented mechanism that binds a server-verifiable assertion to our specific published integration or plugin version, rather than only to the shared ChatGPT OAuth client identity? If available, please point us to its verification contract and publisher registration requirements.

This is an optional strengthening request, separate from our implementation and acceptance of the documented CIMD/JWT flow.

Thank you, SkillPilot — https://skillpilot.com

Vor Versand: Tatsächlichen Host-Teststatus ergänzen, ohne Tokens, Assertions, Sitzungskennungen oder private Lerntranskripte. Zeigt der eigene Test eine undokumentierte Verteilungsabweichung, diese mit bereinigtem reproduzierbarem Befund als eigenes Problem beschreiben.

docs.title: ChatGPT beta distribution: historical assessment
docs.text:
Superseded work plan: the Product Owner subsequently set Claude beta → stable candidate → focused ChatGPT acceptance → submission on 12 September 2026. There is no parallel ChatGPT beta distribution project, further workaround search, or speculative ChatGPT extension work. The findings and unsent drafts below are retained as history, not active follow-up tasks.

Assessment date: 12 September 2026. Status: no complete qualifying pre-review beta route established. This is not an official OpenAI rejection of that capability or proof that no such route can exist. The messages below are drafts, not sent requests or published forum posts.

docs.title: Former required outcome and observed boundary
docs.text:
The intended beta user has an independent personal ChatGPT account and no existing SkillPilot integration. Installation must start from the Git marketplace, use normal connection/consent, and receive Git-delivered Skill updates. The same SkillPilot production endpoint must continue enforcing OpenAI-managed mTLS, OAuth client authentication and independent learning-session authorization. No shared ChatGPT workspace, per-tester developer configuration, distributed client secret, or authentication downgrade qualifies.

The marketplace runbook records the direct-MCP attempt: Windows ChatGPT 26.901.51231 requests reached the edge without a client certificate and received 403 / certificate_required before OAuth. This proves the failure of those requests, not every possible host route.

The subsequent paired user screenshots from the requested account comparison show the selected personal registration loading in the creator account with version 1.0.0 and an install button, while the second account receives the generic plugin-load failure. This supports an account-dependent availability boundary; the exact policy and underlying HTTP error were not captured. Neither screenshot proves installation, OAuth success or a working tool call. The old registration is not the current beta candidate.

docs.title: Alternatives checked
docs.text:
Route Finding under the required outcome Git plugin with direct remote MCP The observed route failed enforced mTLS. A manifest does not provision the OpenAI-managed certificate. Git plugin referencing a registered app Separates Git updates from hosted transport, but a reference creates neither an app nor access rights. Cross-account availability remains unresolved. CIMD with private_key_jwt A documented confidential-client flow without a shared tester secret. Personal developer-mode registration is still a prerequisite; it does not establish marketplace-driven provisioning. Production must not be assumed to use JWT merely because the backend implements it. Secure MCP Tunnel Supports personal Platform organizations, but needs tunnel associations, permissions, a running tunnel client and developer-app setup. It does not establish the required installation path or the same OpenAI-Connectors certificate at our edge. Shared managed ChatGPT workspace Documented app/role and Git distribution mechanisms, but expressly declined by the Product Owner; not equivalent to independent personal accounts. Custom GPT, alternate chat host or SkillPilot model-API proxy Different distribution/runtime contracts, not this plugin installation. An inference proxy additionally conflicts with the direct provider-billing boundary.

Official sources checked for this assessment:

  • Plugin packaging and developer-mode registration
  • Registered-app references and permissions
  • Personal developer mode and CIMD/JWT
  • OpenAI-managed MCP mTLS
  • Secure MCP Tunnel
  • Public review and publication

Tunnel control-plane mTLS and tunnel-client-to-MCP mTLS are separate TLS legs; neither automatically supplies OpenAI's Connectors certificate to SkillPilot. Forwarding through a local operator route would test a different security path. No tunnel was installed and no production security setting was changed.

docs.title: Current decision
docs.text:
Follow the binding beta and publication strategy. Claude is the actual beta platform. Only after stabilization is the shared candidate tested through the real ChatGPT integration and prepared for official submission; that focused acceptance is not another full beta.

The submission dossier, current-candidate demo, security checks and truthful host evidence remain required. The historical marketplace acceptance matrix is unresolved but is not a prerequisite for that submission. Neither support silence nor this assessment establishes that a distribution route is globally impossible. The former parallel support/forum and post-publication Git-beta follow-up plan is superseded, not an automatic future work item.

docs.title: Archived support draft — not an active sending task
docs.text:
Subject: Pre-review beta distribution of a ChatGPT MCP plugin with enforced mTLS

We are preparing a new submission of SkillPilot Coach. We need a beta route for independent personal ChatGPT accounts before public approval, with the plugin and Skill updates distributed through a Git marketplace.

Our production MCP endpoint requires OpenAI-managed client-certificate authentication and authenticated OAuth clients. In Windows ChatGPT 26.901.51231, the installed Git plugin's direct HTTP MCP connection was rejected by our edge with 403 / certificate_required before OAuth. A separate personal registration loads in its creator account, but its link returns a generic plugin-load error in a second personal account. We have not established the exact access policy behind that error.

Is there a supported pre-review registration/distribution flow that lets these users install from Git, complete normal connection/consent, and use the hosted OpenAI MCP transport with its managed client certificate? If so, which setup makes the integration accessible across independent personal accounts?

We are looking for the intended provisioning flow, without shared-workspace membership or separate developer setup for every tester.

docs.title: Archived public forum draft — not an active posting task
docs.text:
Title: Git-distributed ChatGPT MCP plugin: secure beta testing in personal accounts before review?

Has anyone completed this installation flow using supported OpenAI features?

  • A fresh personal ChatGPT account adds a Git marketplace and installs a plugin.
  • The user completes ordinary connection/consent, without creating a developer integration first.
  • Calls reach the MCP server with OpenAI-managed mTLS and authenticated OAuth.
  • Plugin/Skill updates continue through Git.

In our Windows ChatGPT 26.901.51231 test, the direct remote-MCP declaration made requests without a client certificate, so our enforced edge rejected them before OAuth. A personal app link loads for its creator but fails to load in a second personal account. The latter is a generic error, not a confirmed diagnosis of a specific access rule.

The documentation explains existing-app references, but those references do not create the integration or grant access. CIMD/JWT addresses client authentication, while Secure MCP Tunnel describes private/developer access; neither has established the complete installation flow above for us.

Is a pre-review provisioning/sharing route documented for this combination, or does the hosted integration first need public approval and publication? A reproducible supported setup or an authoritative clarification would help.

Relevant references: app references, MCP mTLS, Secure MCP Tunnel.

docs.title: Before sending or posting
docs.text: Use the authenticated support/forum interface and review the final text and destination first. Do not attach old learner-chat screenshots, personal app links, credentials, session capabilities or raw request logs. The sanitized error class, host version, reproduction steps and public documentation are sufficient for these drafts. A support reply or forum report is evidence to evaluate, not automatic production acceptance.

docs.title: Neue SkillPilot Custom GPTs als befristeter Übergangskanal
docs.text:
Stand: 18. August 2026

Status: Clean-Slate-Builder-Paket vorbereitet; noch kein GPT erstellt und keine Produktions-WebGUI geändert

OpenAI-App: skillpilot-coach-v1 Version 1.0.0 bleibt unverändert im Review

docs.title: Entscheidung
docs.text:
Für den Übergang werden zwei neue, klar von der App unterscheidbare Custom GPTs angelegt:

  • SkillPilot GPT Coach (de)
  • SkillPilot GPT Coach (en)

Es wird kein früherer GPT aktualisiert, geklont oder wiederhergestellt. Alte GPT- IDs, URLs, Screenshots, Instructions, Knowledge-Dateien und Actions werden nicht übernommen. Die neuen IDs und URLs entstehen erst bei der privaten Erstellung im GPT Builder.

Das vollständige Builder-Paket liegt unter:

  • ai/openai custom gpt/de/
  • ai/openai custom gpt/en/

ai/openai custom gpt/action-regression/ bleibt ausschließlich Testinfrastruktur für Providerregressionen und wird nie in einen der beiden GPTs hochgeladen.

docs.title: Architektur ohne zusätzlichen Dienst
docs.text:
Der Übergang nutzt deployte Backendgrenzen im vorhandenen Spring-Boot-Prozess und benötigt weder eine neue Route noch einen eigenen JVM-Prozess:

separater Custom-GPT-Launcher in der WebGUI
  -> POST /api/ui/learners/{skillpilotId}/chat-start
  -> sichtbarer, 5 Minuten gültiger Einmalcode SP-....-....
  -> neuer locale-fester SkillPilot GPT Coach
  -> redeemStartCode
  -> internes 24-Stunden-chatSessionToken
  -> neun /visible/...-Coach-Actions
  -> CoachToolFacade / LearnerService / vorhandene Datenbank

Startcode-Einlösung und /visible/...-Adapter akzeptieren dasselbe vom ChatSessionService erzeugte sps_...-Token. Die dauerhafte SkillPilot-ID bleibt im Browser und Backend.

docs.title: Warum Retention ein Rollout-Gate bleibt
docs.text:
Die offizielle OpenAI-Dokumentation zu GPT Actions beschreibt REST-Actions und ihre Authentisierung, garantiert aber nicht, dass ein geheimes Action-Ergebnis in jedem späteren User-Turn als Modellkontext erhalten bleibt.

Der öffentliche reproduzierbare Fehlerbericht dokumentiert den früheren Ausfall. Neue positive Tests sind deshalb belastbare aktuelle Laufzeitevidenz, aber keine dauerhafte Providerzusage.

Jeder neue Sprach-GPT muss privat in einem neuen Chat bestehen:

  1. Einmalcode wird genau einmal durch redeemStartCode eingelöst.
  2. Token, relayFooter, Auswahlreferenzen und interne IDs bleiben unsichtbar.
  3. Ein neuer User-Turn löst erfolgreich getVisibleState mit dem intern behaltenen Token aus.
  4. Eine spätere Nummernantwort verwendet die intern behaltene selectionReference erfolgreich.
  5. Der Test wird nach mehreren normalen Turns wiederholt.

Scheitert einer dieser Punkte, wird die betreffende Sprache nicht freigeschaltet. Der GPT darf technische Werte weder erfinden noch vom Benutzer erfragen.

docs.title: Funktionsumfang gegenüber der OpenAI App V1
docs.text:
Bereich neue Custom-GPT-Übergangslösung OpenAI App V1 Providerprodukt zwei getrennte GPTs (de) und (en) ein mehrsprachiges Plugin skillpilot-coach-v1 Zugang neuer geteilter GPT-Link; ChatGPT-Anmeldung und dortige Verfügbarkeit erforderlich Plugin-Veröffentlichung und dortige Verfügbarkeit erforderlich SkillPilot-Identität 5-Minuten-Einmalcode, danach internes 24h-Sessiontoken OAuth-Appbindung plus getrennte 24h-Lernsession Fachzustand kompakter zehnteiliger Action-Vertrag eingefrorener V1-MCP-Vertrag Personal Curriculum ausschließlich WebGUI; im GPT nicht ändern ausschließlich WebGUI; im Coach nicht ändern Fokus, aktives Ziel, Coaching, Mastery, Progress enthalten enthalten Orientierung aktuelle nicht prüfende Semantik Bestandteil des eingefrorenen V1-Vertrags Lernzielbilder Cockpit-Link; kein MCP-Apps-Widget gebundene MCP-Apps-Bildressource normales Karteikartenüben Cockpit-Link interaktive MCP-Apps-Kartenressource Verified Recall kompatibler Action-Ablauf mit geschützten Antwort-/Write-Schritten serverseitig stärker gebündelter V1-Ablauf Prüfung Aufgabe im State, Lösung erst über geschützte Evaluation nach sichtbarer Abgabe V1-Prüfungswerkzeuge und -Semantik Cross-Turn-Abhängigkeit Action-Retention muss als Provider-Canary bestehen Lernsession wird explizit an V1-Tools übergeben Abschaltung eigener WebGUI-Einstieg wird deaktiviert keine Änderung am Review-Kandidaten

Der Übergangskanal ist fachlich nutzbar, aber kein Ersatzvertrag für die App. Insbesondere werden MCP-Apps-UIs, OAuth-Clientbindung, V1-Capabilities und der stärker gebündelte V1-Recall-Ablauf nicht nachgebaut.

docs.title: Während des aktiven Reviews unverändert lassen
docs.text:
Der eingereichte Pfad

WebGUI-Konfiguration -> Lernen starten -> OpenAI App / vorbereitete Nachricht

bleibt byte- und verhaltensgleich. Insbesondere keine Änderung an:

  • app/src/components/SessionSetup.tsx
  • app/src/coachVariants/coachLaunch.ts
  • app/src/coachVariants/versionSelector.ts
  • app/src/coachVariants/openAiMcp/
  • Plugin-, MCP-, OAuth-, Edge-, Portal- oder Reviewartefakten
  • VITE_SKILLPILOT_COACH_VARIANT im Produktionsbuild

docs.title: Separater Übergangs-Launcher
docs.text:
Nach einer ausdrücklichen, eng begrenzten Product-Owner-Freigabe wird eine eigene WebGUI-Route vorgeschlagen, beispielsweise /custom-gpt. Sie ist kein Providerumschalter und ersetzt keinen vorhandenen Button.

Die Route verwendet den im Browser geladenen Lernenden und prüft, dass das Personal Curriculum vollständig konfiguriert ist. Andernfalls führt sie zur normalen WebGUI-Konfiguration zurück. Sie zeigt deutlich:

  • SkillPilot GPT Coach (de) beziehungsweise (en);
  • „befristete Custom-GPT-Übergangslösung“, nicht „SkillPilot App“;
  • ChatGPT als externen Anbieter und dessen Zugangsvoraussetzungen;
  • Start einer neuen, höchstens 24 Stunden gültigen Lernsitzung;
  • Datenschutzlink und Cockpit-Fallback;
  • keine Behauptung, die im Review befindliche App sei veröffentlicht.

Beim Klick:

  1. Browserfenster synchron leer öffnen, damit Popup-Blocker den späteren Wechsel nicht verhindern.
  2. requestChatStart aus app/src/utils/chatStart.ts mit Sprache und einem eigenen Clientkennzeichen wie custom-gpt-interim aufrufen. Keine Curriculum-Mutation senden.
  3. Die vorbereitete Nachricht mit der neuen, locale-festen URL öffnen.
  4. Bei blockiertem Prompt-Deep-Link nur die Einmalnachricht als Copy-Fallback anbieten; niemals SkillPilot-ID oder Sessiontoken kopieren.
  5. Bei Fehler das leere Fenster schließen und keinen erfolgreichen Start behaupten.

Die neuen URLs werden erst nach Builder-Erstellung und Acceptance gesetzt, etwa über dedizierte Buildwerte:

VITE_CUSTOM_GPT_URL_DE
VITE_CUSTOM_GPT_URL_EN
VITE_CUSTOM_GPT_INTERIM_ENABLED

Die gelöschten GPT-URLs, die während des Review-Freezes noch in altem Frontendcode stehen können, sind keine gültige Quelle. Der neue Launcher darf weder app/src/utils/skillpilotGpt.ts noch die URL-Defaults der alten visibleSession-Variante übernehmen. Eine spätere Implementierung braucht eine neue kleine, sprachspezifische Konfiguration und Tests gegen fehlende Werte.

Backend, Datenbank und JVM bleiben unverändert.

docs.title: Sichtbarkeit und Aktivierung
docs.text:
Die risikoärmste Variante während des Reviews ist:

  1. Builder-Paket und Konzept vorbereiten;
  2. beide GPTs privat erstellen und testen;
  3. Produktions-WebGUI bis zum Reviewende unverändert lassen;
  4. danach den separaten Einstieg aktivieren.

Muss der Übergang schon während des Reviews öffentlich werden, braucht die Aktivierung vorab eine explizite Freeze-Ausnahme. Ein anderer Dateipfad allein beweist wegen des wirkungsbezogenen Freezes keine Unabhängigkeit.

docs.title: Erforderliche Freeze-Ausnahme vor einem Rollout im Review
docs.text:
Die Product-Owner-Entscheidung muss mindestens festhalten:

  1. Grund: einziger öffentlich nutzbarer Interimskanal bis zur App-Freigabe;
  2. Umfang: nur separat benannte Custom-GPT-Route, Copy, neue URL-Konfiguration, Featureflag und Tests; der App-Start bleibt unverändert;
  3. Ziel: Produktions-Webfrontend, nicht skillpilot-coach-v1 Version 1.0.0;
  4. Portalentscheidung: ausdrücklich bestätigen, ob kein Withdraw/Resubmit nötig ist; andernfalls nicht ausrollen;
  5. Hashanker: jede unvermeidbar berührte geschützte Datei exakt benennen und als eng begrenzte Ausnahme in Freeze-Metadaten und Checker aufnehmen.

Ohne diese Entscheidung bleibt es bei Paket, privaten Builder-Tests und Konzept; es gibt keine Produktions-WebGUI-Änderung.

docs.title: Erstellung, Rollout und Rückfall
docs.text:
1. npm test --prefix "ai/openai custom gpt".
  2. SkillPilot GPT Coach (de) neu und privat erstellen; Canary und vollständige deutsche Acceptance ausführen.
  3. SkillPilot GPT Coach (en) getrennt neu und privat erstellen; denselben Test auf Englisch ausführen.
  4. Erst danach die neu vergebenen URLs in die freigegebene Deployment- Konfiguration übernehmen.
  5. Nur mit zulässiger Freeze-Entscheidung den separaten Launcher aktivieren.
  6. Monitoring auf Redeem-Erfolg, anonymisierte Sessionfehler 401/409/410 und Abbruchrate begrenzen; keine Codes oder Token loggen.

Rückfall bedeutet ausschließlich: separaten Launcher deaktivieren. Das berührt weder die OpenAI App V1 noch den Cockpitbetrieb. Der sichtbare Relay-Modus darf nur nach bewusster Produkt-/Datenschutzentscheidung als Notfallstart angeboten werden, weil er das temporäre Sessiongeheimnis absichtlich in den Chat schreibt.

docs.title: ChatGPT App "SkillPilot Coach v1": Deployment and Cutover
docs.text:
As of: 5 October 2026

OAuth cutover, 11 September 2026: For the approved new client authentication, follow the profile-specific activation runbook. The target profile uses CIMD with private_key_jwt; existing securely configured Basic connections remain a separate transitional profile. The Basic examples below are not a method fallback for JWT clients. The Claude beta and vendor inquiries do not block this authorization. Implementation alone does not activate a production connection.

Native desktop integration, 24 September 2026: The uploaded plugin uses the same MCP endpoint and OAuth issuer. An additional chatgpt-native-cimd-public profile supports native CIMD with S256 PKCE; mTLS observe is explicitly authorized for this trial. See configuration and test launch. The enforce acceptance gates below apply to hosted certificate transport.

Status: Submission 1.0.0 was rejected (REJECTED). The Product Owner has explicitly lifted the ChatGPT development freezes. The current successor 1.1.1 is published via the Git marketplace for the desktop beta; the official OpenAI submission remains DRAFT and the OpenAI directory remains unpublished. Installation and starting a learning session in Windows ChatGPT Desktop have been confirmed by the Product Owner. See unfreeze and review history. The scoped authorizations of 24 September for archive/native CIMD and of 5 October for the existing Git/desktop beta including ordinary GUI launch supplement the original Claude-first sequence. The Product Owner performs the GUI/server rollout; local changes do not constitute a resubmission. The V1 contract continues to use the dedicated mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com origin with server-authenticated HTTPS, OpenAI connector mTLS, and OAuth/PKCE. Actual production state and the required enforce mode for hosted certificate transport must be re-verified before any submission. The separately authorized native desktop beta using observe remains distinct from that path. Permanent ID, provider notice, and Level 2 configuration remain exclusively inside the first-party WebGUI.

This runbook activates the multilingual, chat-first MCP learning coach with two separately bound MCP Apps UIs: the read-only learning-goal image viewer and interactive flashcard practice. The MCP server, OAuth authorization server, UI resource delivery, and SkillPilot domain logic run inside the existing Spring Boot process. The Node MCP server under ai/openai app/ remains a local regression testbed; it also hosts the verified source implementation of the UI components whose self-contained build artifacts are copied into Spring Boot resources.

The canonical responsibility boundary between chat client and backend is defined in the communication contract. Product and provider architecture are documented in the SkillPilot-owned coach architecture. The binding identity and session flow is documented separately in openai-mcp-oauth-learner-session-architecture.md. Package, contract, and lifecycle versions follow the versioning and lifecycle plan; release, rollback, and retirement follow the V1 release runbook. In particular, ChatGPT manages OAuth access and refresh tokens automatically; users never enter OAuth tokens, an OAuth client secret, or a permanent SkillPilot ID in chat. However, every explicit authorized launch via the first-party web interface creates an independent learningSessionId with an absolute 24-hour lifetime. During an ordinary desktop beta launch, the prepared message is copied into a fresh chat with the plugin selected. Dedicated Recall/exam launches retain their browser-launch contracts. SkillPilot inserts this reference automatically into the short start message; ChatGPT passes it unchanged to every domain MCP tool.

docs.title: 1. Public Contract
docs.text:
Purpose URL Plugin identity skillpilot-coach-v1 MCP Server URL https://mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com/mcp OAuth Resource / Audience https://mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com/mcp Declared widget origin https://mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com Observed ChatGPT Web origin https://mcp-coach-v1-skillpilot-com.web-sandbox.oaiusercontent.com Goal visualization resource ui://skillpilot/coach/v1/sha256-c890cf271307d815256450a2b20b27d57015a84e9f4e39c97532eaefc4e30c26/goal-visualization.html Flashcard practice resource ui://skillpilot/coach/v1/sha256-8524ee20837971227c35f1e16518d2b5bdbd60637fbec6beede9f2f4b29e4852/memory-card-practice.html Protected Resource Metadata https://mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp Domain challenge https://mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com/.well-known/openai-apps-challenge OAuth Issuer https://skillpilot.com/api/openai/v1 Authorization Server Metadata https://skillpilot.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/openai/v1 Issuer-relative OAuth compatibility route https://skillpilot.com/api/openai/v1/.well-known/openid-configuration Authorization Endpoint https://skillpilot.com/api/openai/v1/oauth2/authorize Token Endpoint https://skillpilot.com/api/openai/v1/oauth2/token Revocation Endpoint https://skillpilot.com/api/openai/v1/oauth2/revoke

Both discovery URLs serve the exact same OAuth metadata document. The canonical RFC 8414 route remains authoritative. The issuer-relative compatibility alias is additionally required because ChatGPT fetches it during MCP re-initialization; it activates neither OpenID scopes nor ID tokens.

The draft inventory contains one active content-addressed resource each for goal visualizations and flashcard practice, plus previously shipped launch and image hash URIs retained as byte-identical passive resources. render_skillpilot_goal_visualization and start_skillpilot_memory_practice each reference only their own active URI via ui.resourceUri and openai/outputTemplate. The app-only tool review_skillpilot_memory_practice_card, ordinary tools, and all retained predecessors remain unbound. After updating, refresh the plugin metadata and verify fresh chats against both active URIs.

The additive V1 vHost forwards exclusively the public /mcp path to the loopback-bound Spring transport /internal/openai/v1/mcp. There is no public compatibility alias. The production app entry uses exclusively this V1 Server URL, never the development tunnel and never a path on skillpilot.com.

docs.title: 2. Discovery Bootstrap and OAuth Values of the Legacy Compatibility Profile
docs.text:
The production contract uses Authorization Code with PKCE S256 and exactly one pre-registered confidential OAuth client for the SkillPilot Coach v1 line. Its fixed client ID, long random client secret, exact callback allowlist, fixed MCP resource, and fixed scopes are configured on both sides by the app author. ChatGPT authenticates at the token endpoint using client_secret_basic; SkillPilot accepts neither none nor open Dynamic Client Registration, CIMD, or private_key_jwt in this active legacy production profile.

The secret is protected configuration exclusively in ChatGPT and SkillPilot. It must never appear in the repository, browser, start message, tool arguments, or logs. PKCE additionally binds the authorization code to the verifier generated by ChatGPT. Standard server-authenticated HTTPS remains mandatory. At the dedicated MCP edge, ChatGPT additionally presents an OpenAI-managed client certificate; SkillPilot does not need to request its own certificate for this.

ChatGPT administration probes the MCP URL before revealing its advanced OAuth settings. At the same time, the full SkillPilot authorization server requires the app-specific callback URL. An explicit, stateless bootstrap mode exists for this purpose:

  1. Leave full operation disabled and set exclusively SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_BOOTSTRAP_ENABLED=true.
  2. After restart, verify the four discovery URLs and the constant MCP 401. Bootstrap registers neither tools nor OAuth client, token endpoints, learner services, or a coach health contributor.
  3. In ChatGPT app administration, select Server URL, the production MCP URL, and OAuth.
  4. Generate a fixed client ID dedicated solely to this app and a long random client secret. Configure the exact same values in ChatGPT and SkillPilot; never copy the secret into documentation or tickets.
  5. Copy the app-specific production callback URL shown there, formatted as https://chatgpt.com/connector/oauth/{callback_id}, unchanged.
  6. Configure multiple real callback URLs as a comma-separated list. Do not add any example or legacy URL that does not appear in app administration.
  7. Select client_secret_basic as token-endpoint authentication in ChatGPT. Disable bootstrap and atomically enable full operation with client ID, secret, callback, OAuth, MCP, and write operations enabled. A read-only canary is an intentionally non-production diagnostic state.

The bootstrap MCP endpoint rejects every method and any arbitrary Bearer values with 401 plus WWW-Authenticate. Authorization, token, revocation, and introspection endpoints remain 404 during bootstrap. OpenAI documentation defines this challenge/metadata contract as the discovery mechanism; whether a specific ChatGPT UI build unlocks its advanced settings with it is still verified in practice. If a UI issue occurs, the security contract is not relaxed. Local rate limiting and data-minimized status telemetry already protect this public bootstrap edge; across multiple instances, a shared gateway rate limit remains required in addition.

Without a client ID or callback list, Spring startup intentionally aborts when OpenAI V1 OAuth is enabled. Bootstrap and full operation must also never be enabled simultaneously; that misconfiguration aborts startup.

docs.title: 3. Runtime Configuration
docs.text:
For a safe cutover, code and additive Liquibase migrations can first be verified in a separate read-only canary. Full production operation, by contrast, requires write operations to be enabled and uses server-authenticated HTTPS on the dedicated V1 vHost, OpenAI connector mTLS, and mandatory OAuth/PKCE with exact resource/audience and scope checks. The separate host isolates domain verification, plugin lifecycle, and client-certificate verification. The existing skillpilot.com vHost is not fundamentally restructured; it only receives the narrow 404 block against MCP/internal path aliases described below.

The reproducible additive vHost configuration resides at deploy/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf. It MUST be included inside the existing Nginx http {} block. Including it at the global top level outside http {} triggers server directive is not allowed here and is invalid. After the switch, the associated Certbot lineage skillpilot-mcp-coaches covers exact major hosts V1 through V9 already provisioned:

mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com
mcp-coach-v2.skillpilot.com
mcp-coach-v3.skillpilot.com
mcp-coach-v4.skillpilot.com
mcp-coach-v5.skillpilot.com
mcp-coach-v6.skillpilot.com
mcp-coach-v7.skillpilot.com
mcp-coach-v8.skillpilot.com
mcp-coach-v9.skillpilot.com

The previously locally prepared names mcp-coach-de-v* and mcp-coach-en-v* were never part of any release. They are neither proxied in Nginx nor retained as compatibility routes. Remaining DNS records or old certificate SANs may be removed after the V1 cutover.

Only V1 is proxied to Spring. The remaining eight HTTPS vHosts are reserved and return 404 for every path; their DNS and TLS readiness does not constitute a release. Changes are always tested first with nginx -t and activated via reload only afterward. Existing vHosts are neither replaced nor fundamentally reworked.

In addition, deploy/nginx/skillpilot-main-vhost-openai-deny-locations.conf is included exclusively inside the existing HTTPS server {} block for skillpilot.com, placed before its general location /. This narrow location snippet blocks the retired public path, the internal Spring transport, and the internal protected-resource metadata target on the main origin with 404. It must be included neither at the global level nor directly in the http {} block. That leaves the existing main vHost otherwise unchanged while only the dedicated V1 vHost exposes the MCP contract.

Before installation, back up the existing main Nginx file and any target snippets already present under unique names. Compare any existing working MCP vHost file against the repository template first rather than blindly overwriting it:

Beforehand, the production checkout must verifiably already contain the language-neutral cutover. This check is mandatory: an outdated script would keep testing the DE host, and an old vHost could mistakenly route unknown new hostnames to V1 as the default vHost. All five commands must succeed and the last one must produce no output:

grep -F 'server_name mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com;' \
  deploy/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf
grep -F 'mcp-coach-v9.skillpilot.com' \
  deploy/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf
grep -F 'proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787/internal/openai/v1/mcp;' \
  deploy/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf
grep -F 'MCP_ORIGIN="https://mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com"' \
  scripts/verify_openai_v1_public_edge.sh
! grep -E 'mcp-coach-(de|en)-v[1-9]' \
  deploy/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf

If any check fails, nothing is installed into /etc/nginx. Pull the approved commit first. A passing run of an outdated smoke script is no substitute for this content check.

sudo cp -a -n /etc/nginx/nginx.conf \
  /etc/nginx/nginx.conf.before-mcp-subdomain-includes

if sudo test -e /etc/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf; then
  sudo cp -a -n /etc/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf \
    /etc/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf.before-repository-sync
  sudo diff -u /etc/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf \
    deploy/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf || true
fi

if sudo test -e /etc/nginx/skillpilot-main-vhost-openai-deny-locations.conf; then
  sudo cp -a -n \
    /etc/nginx/skillpilot-main-vhost-openai-deny-locations.conf \
    /etc/nginx/skillpilot-main-vhost-openai-deny-locations.conf.before-repository-sync
  sudo diff -u \
    /etc/nginx/skillpilot-main-vhost-openai-deny-locations.conf \
    deploy/nginx/skillpilot-main-vhost-openai-deny-locations.conf || true
fi

The two files are not installed or activated at this stage yet. During the first mTLS cutover, backend mode, CA bundle, root-owned mode file, and loopback verifier are prepared first. Only afterward are the Nginx templates installed in the coordinated sequence below, ensuring that the new V1 configuration never references missing mTLS artifacts during a full Nginx test.

The two includes intentionally belong in different contexts:

http {
    # bestehende globale Einstellungen bleiben unverändert
    include /etc/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf;

    server {
        server_name skillpilot.com skillpilot.org skillpilot.mobi;

        # vor dem bestehenden allgemeinen `location /`
        include /etc/nginx/skillpilot-main-vhost-openai-deny-locations.conf;

        location / {
            # bestehende SkillPilot-Proxykonfiguration
        }
    }
}

This snippet is a placement guide, not a replacement for the existing main vHost. Add the second include specifically inside that existing server {} block while leaving all other entries untouched. Installation alone activates nothing yet. Before every reload, run the root-only mTLS preflight and an explicit nginx -t in the coordinated sequence further below.

Before installing the new TLS vHost template, the existing Let's Encrypt lineage must already be switched to the nine language-neutral major hosts. First, all existing DNS A/AAAA records must point to the same server; an absent AAAA record is acceptable, whereas a stale AAAA record is not. The certbot --nginx commands below assume that the previously verified, working V1 vHost without the new mTLS file reference is still active. On a genuinely fresh installation with no existing lineage, first use solely a separately verified port-80 challenge configuration; activate the full repository vHost template only after certificate issuance and then in the sequence established below: EnvironmentFile → mTLS artifacts → Nginx template → preflight. The existing main vHost is never replaced during this step.

sudo certbot certonly --nginx --dry-run \
  --preferred-challenges http \
  --key-type ecdsa \
  --cert-name skillpilot-mcp-coaches \
  -d mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v2.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v3.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v4.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v5.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v6.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v7.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v8.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v9.skillpilot.com

sudo certbot certonly --nginx \
  --preferred-challenges http \
  --key-type ecdsa \
  --cert-name skillpilot-mcp-coaches \
  --force-renewal \
  -d mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v2.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v3.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v4.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v5.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v6.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v7.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v8.skillpilot.com \
  -d mcp-coach-v9.skillpilot.com

sudo certbot certificates
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
sudo systemctl is-active nginx

The second invocation replaces the domain set of the same lineage; it does not create a parallel language lineage. Before confirming, verify that the domain list displayed by Certbot matches V1 through V9 exactly. Afterward, V1 must serve its protected contract and V2 through V9 must serve 404 for every path over valid TLS; ./scripts/verify_openai_v1_public_edge.sh verifies both. --force-renewal is set deliberately here because the successfully validated new SAN set must be written immediately into that same lineage. --expand is unsuitable because it would retain the old unpublished DE/EN SANs instead of replacing the domain set exactly.

SERVER_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1

SKILLPILOT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://skillpilot.com
# Unabhängig vom OAuth-Client-Secret erzeugen, z. B.: openssl rand -hex 32
SKILLPILOT_SIGNING_SECRET=<mindestens-32-hochentropische-zeichen>

SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_ENABLED=true
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_BOOTSTRAP_ENABLED=false
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_OAUTH_ENABLED=true
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_MCP_ENABLED=true
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_WRITES_ENABLED=true
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_MTLS_EDGE_MODE=observe

SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_CHATGPT_URL=https://chatgpt.com/

SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_OAUTH_CLIENT_AUTHENTICATION_METHOD=client_secret_basic
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=<exakte-feste-client-id-dieser-app>
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=<langes-zufälliges-client-secret>
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URIS=<exakte-callback-url-oder-kommaliste>

# Nur bei einem tatsächlichen Client-ID-Wechsel, einmalig und danach entfernen:
# SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_OAUTH_LEGACY_CLIENT_IDS=<exakte-alte-client-id-oder-kommaliste>

SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_LEARNING_SESSION_TTL=PT24H
# Standardmäßig false; nur für einen kontrollierten First-Party-Live-Test kurz aktivieren:
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_TTL_ENABLED=false
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS=3600000
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL=PT1H
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL=P30D

SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW=PT1M
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_RATE_LIMIT_MCP_REQUESTS=120
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_RATE_LIMIT_OAUTH_REQUESTS=60
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_RATE_LIMIT_UI_REQUESTS=60
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_RATE_LIMIT_METADATA_REQUESTS=120
SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_CLIENT_BUCKETS=10000

MTLS_EDGE_MODE=disabled is only the rollback-capable initial state prior to the separate edge installation. observe validates presented OpenAI certificates while still allowing requests without a certificate to reach OAuth, providing live-traffic proof without breaking the existing operator smoke test. An invalid certificate presented during observe is still rejected. Once live ChatGPT proof succeeds, switch both the root-owned Nginx mode and the backend mode together to enforce. Publication is permitted only in enforce.

The initial cutover to observe is an ordered, fail-closed activation. First, stage SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_MTLS_EDGE_MODE=observe in the root-protected systemd EnvironmentFile without restarting the backend service yet. Then follow this exact sequence:

cd /home/enpasos/skillpilot

# 1. Repositoryvertrag und CA-Pins prüfen.
./scripts/verify_openai_v1_mtls_edge.sh --static

# 2. CA-Bundle, Modusdatei und Loopback-Verifier staged installieren.
sudo ./scripts/install_openai_v1_mtls_edge.sh --mode observe
sudo systemctl is-active skillpilot-openai-v1-mtls-verifier

# 3. Erst jetzt die bereits gesicherten und geprüften Nginx-Vorlagen installieren.
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0644 \
  deploy/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf \
  /etc/nginx/skillpilot-mcp-coaches.conf
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0644 \
  deploy/nginx/skillpilot-main-vhost-openai-deny-locations.conf \
  /etc/nginx/skillpilot-main-vhost-openai-deny-locations.conf

# 4. Geschützte Backend-Konfiguration, installierte Artefakte und Nginx-Diskstand prüfen.
sudo ./scripts/verify_openai_v1_mtls_edge.sh \
  --preflight --expected-mode observe
sudo nginx -t

# 5. Backend zuerst, danach den bereits geprüften Nginx-Stand aktivieren.
sudo systemctl restart skillpilot
sudo systemctl is-active skillpilot
sudo systemctl reload nginx
sudo systemctl is-active nginx

# 6. Laufzeitvertrag prüfen; danach folgt der reale ChatGPT-Nachweis.
./scripts/verify_openai_v1_mtls_edge.sh --runtime --expected-mode observe

The runtime smoke intentionally runs without sudo and reads neither the root-protected mode.conf nor the backend EnvironmentFile. It detects the active mode solely through the public no-certificate/invalid-certificate matrix while simultaneously confirming over the loopback operator lane that the running backend filter accepts the same mode. The separate root-only gates --staged, --preflight, and --installed remain responsible for artifact parity, file permissions, systemd, listeners, and the on-disk Nginx contract.

The installer does not fetch CA files live from the network; instead, it verifies the reviewed OpenAI files, their SHA-256 digests, X.509 fingerprints, and the intermediate chain. The systemd unit supplies those exact two CA files to the isolated DynamicUser via read-only service credentials, so the service requires no read permission on the protected parent directory /etc/skillpilot. This requires systemd 247 or newer; the unit deliberately uses ${CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY} rather than the %d specifier introduced later. The static gate validates the unit before installation using systemd-analyze verify. The installer binds the verifier exclusively on 127.0.0.1:8792 and writes the explicitly chosen root-owned Nginx mode atomically to /etc/skillpilot/openai-mtls/mode.conf. It never edits, tests, or reloads the active Nginx configuration. Before every reload, the separate root-only --preflight must prove that the installed mode matches SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_MTLS_EDGE_MODE in the protected systemd EnvironmentFile and that both installed files and on-disk Nginx configuration match the repository contract. Neither the EnvironmentFile nor any secret is printed in the process.

Even during the initial transition from disabled to observe, restart the backend service before reloading Nginx. Between backend restart and Nginx reload, contradictory or not-yet-present edge headers are intentionally rejected with 403. This brief fail-closed window is never bypassed via a public diagnostic override.

The cutover from observe to enforce follows this sequence:

  1. Prove at least one real ChatGPT tool invocation in observe. The privacy-bounded counter with event="mtls_edge_verified" must increment for that call, while event="mtls_edge_observed_no_cert" must not increment. Certificate, token, and session ID must never be logged.
  2. Start a maintenance window and set the value in the backend EnvironmentFile to enforce, without restarting the service yet. The running backend/edge contract thus remains completely on observe for the moment.
  3. Run sudo ./scripts/install_openai_v1_mtls_edge.sh --mode enforce, followed by the separate sudo ./scripts/verify_openai_v1_mtls_edge.sh --preflight --expected-mode enforce and an explicit sudo nginx -t. Only these checks confirm that backend EnvironmentFile, installed edge mode, artifacts, and on-disk Nginx state are consistent. The installer still neither edits nor reloads Nginx.
  4. Now restart the backend service, immediately run sudo systemctl reload nginx, and then run ./scripts/verify_openai_v1_mtls_edge.sh --runtime --expected-mode enforce. The public request without a certificate must return 403, while metadata and challenge remain reachable. The positive OAuth smoke test without a certificate runs exclusively over the genuine loopback socket peer. Between backend restart and Nginx reload, the backend filter intentionally rejects the contradictory classification still arriving from the running observe edge with 403. That brief fail-closed transition is expected and must not be bridged with a public bypass.
  5. Refresh/connect the app in a fresh chat and perform a real ChatGPT tool call. Only when event="mtls_edge_verified" increments again, the verifier journal contains no rejection for that call, no backend assertion rejection increments, and the protected openAiDeCoach health detail reports mtlsEdgeMode="enforce" is the cutover ready for publication.

If steps 3 through 5 fail, the edge stays fail-closed. Rolling back to observe is likewise executed as a coordinated backend-plus-root-owned-edge change with preflight, nginx -t, reload, and runtime smoke; it is not a publishable final state.

CA trust is never updated over the network during startup or deployment. At least every 90 days, compare the two official OpenAI CA files against the pinned repository files, SHA-256 digests, X.509 fingerprints, validity periods, and intermediate chain, recording the outcome and review date in operational evidence. Re-verify unchanged files with ./scripts/verify_openai_v1_mtls_edge.sh --static. Any discrepancy triggers not an automatic update, but a review-gated CA rotation under CA provenance, including an overlapping trust cutover whenever OpenAI temporarily publishes both chains, followed by a renewed positive ChatGPT test. In addition, monitor mtls_edge_verified, mtls_edge_observed_no_cert, and the backend assertion counter mtls_edge_rejected. Certificate and no-certificate rejections upstream of Spring are derived from the bounded verifier journal and public 403 edge status codes. An absence of verified ChatGPT calls or an unexpected spike in rejection signals triggers an operational review. At least 90 days before any pinned CA expires, a confirmed successor or renewal strategy must be in place.

Removed direct-start variables SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_SECURE_COOKIE, SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_BINDING_TTL, SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_LAUNCH_TTL, and all SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_RATE_LIMIT_BOOTSTRAP_* entries must not remain in the service environment. Both the server and the deployment validator reject these retired names fail-closed.

The three public V1 URLs are not configured via environment variables. They are immutable parts of the V1 contract:

  • MCP and OAuth resource: https://mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com/mcp
  • Protected Resource Metadata: https://mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp

Setting SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_UI_ORIGIN is likewise disallowed: the widget origin is fixed in the V1 contract as https://mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com and delivered identically via _meta.ui.domain and _meta["openai/widgetDomain"]. Legacy URL variables and same-named override attempts abort startup fail-closed so a stale or misspelled route can never silently replace the versioned V1 contract.

ChatGPT Web currently materializes this declared domain as an isolated browser origin under *.web-sandbox.oaiusercontent.com. Both active UI resources communicate exclusively via their narrowly bound MCP tools; there is no provider-side permanent-ID or setup HTTPS path.

Before the first subdomain deployment, remove in particular any legacy entries for SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_DE_UI_ORIGIN, SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_DE_V1_ORIGIN, SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_DE_MTLS_EDGE_ENABLED, SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_DE_MTLS_EDGE_TRUSTED_PROXIES, and mTLS smoke certificates from the EnvironmentFile. Do not replace them with new locale-bound names; the sole current backend switch is SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_MTLS_EDGE_MODE. Likewise, completely remove SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_DE_MCP_URL, SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_DE_OAUTH_RESOURCE, and SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_DE_RESOURCE_METADATA.

Prior to copying assets, building, and restarting the service, ./deploy_skillpilot.sh inspects the EnvironmentFile actually referenced by the systemd unit. The production contract permits exactly one such file, defaulting to /etc/skillpilot/skillpilot.env; set SKILLPILOT_SERVICE_ENV_FILE explicitly if a different path is used. Only the names of removed OpenAI V1 variables are detected from the file; their values and all OAuth, database, or other secrets are neither logged nor printed. Those same legacy names must not be injected via Environment=, PassEnvironment=, or the global systemd environment either. If the single EnvironmentFile is marked optional in systemd (ignore_errors=yes) and is absent, preflight accepts the canonical V1 defaults after checking the remaining environment channels. A missing mandatory file (ignore_errors=no) remains an error. An EnvironmentFile containing OAuth or database secrets remains root:root with mode 0600 by default. The sole explicitly supported group-read exception is admin file access on the canonical /etc/skillpilot/skillpilot.env; it does not authorize broad group access to other secrets or configuration directories. If the deploy user cannot read the root-protected file or traverse a parent directory, preflight visibly reports this content check as SKIP; the exact Spring startup validation remains the final fail-closed boundary. Blanket sudo cat permissions or world-readable secret files are strictly prohibited.

The migration is intentionally fail-closed: legacy SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_DE_* and SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_DE_V1_* names are not silently mapped as V1 aliases. All V1-specific settings carry SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_*; shared policies of the single Spring process carry SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_* without a language or version segment. Remove legacy names completely rather than setting them to empty strings.

The nine Nginx origins are not nine Spring processes and are not toggled via a shared URL environment variable. Each public host is mapped statically in Nginx to the internal path of its contract line. Only V1 is currently implemented; the remaining reserved hosts intentionally return 404. Future contract lines already follow this unambiguous naming convention:

Public host Spring configuration group Line-scoped environment names Current status mcp-coach-v1.skillpilot.com skillpilot.openai.coach.v1 SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_* active, internal /internal/openai/v1/* mcp-coach-v2.skillpilot.com skillpilot.openai.coach.v2 SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V2_* reserved, 404 mcp-coach-v3.skillpilot.com skillpilot.openai.coach.v3 SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V3_* reserved, 404 mcp-coach-v4.skillpilot.com skillpilot.openai.coach.v4 SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V4_* reserved, 404 mcp-coach-v5.skillpilot.com skillpilot.openai.coach.v5 SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V5_* reserved, 404 mcp-coach-v6.skillpilot.com skillpilot.openai.coach.v6 SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V6_* reserved, 404 mcp-coach-v7.skillpilot.com skillpilot.openai.coach.v7 SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V7_* reserved, 404 mcp-coach-v8.skillpilot.com skillpilot.openai.coach.v8 SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V8_* reserved, 404 mcp-coach-v9.skillpilot.com skillpilot.openai.coach.v9 SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V9_* reserved, 404

The reserved names are a convention, not yet an accepted runtime configuration. The current server aborts startup if an unimplemented line or an unknown line-scoped variable is set rather than silently ignoring the entry. A line is activated only with its own contract, internal route, Spring configuration group, and test suite. Process-wide settings such as cookie hardening, session TTLs, and rate limits remain defined once under SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_*.

Likewise, SKILLPILOT_SERVER_BUILD is not maintained in /etc/skillpilot/skillpilot.env. Gradle builds exactly one skillpilot-server artifact and embeds the full lowercase HEAD commit hash into skillpilot.openai.coach.v1.server-build and skillpilot.openai.coach.v1.mcp.server-version during backend resource processing. scripts/deploy.sh verifies both values against the checked-out commit before restarting the service, ensuring that telemetry and health output describe the shipped artifact rather than a manually maintained environment variable.

SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_WRITES_ENABLED=true is mandatory for a functional production coach. Personalization, navigation, task progress, and mastery are domain write operations. When set to false, discovery, OAuth, and read-only tools keep working, but the coach aborts on the first required state transition with 503 Service Unavailable. That setting is therefore suitable exclusively for a deliberately isolated read-only canary. Operational write disablement must not trigger an OAuth reconnect flow.

The ordinary enabled provider starts exclusively in secure client mode; there is no production secure-mode=false switch. Client proof and callback are verified per explicit profile: Basic with secret, hosted CIMD with private_key_jwt, and optionally native CIMD with none and loopback callback. Resource, scopes, and PKCE S256 remain mandatory. Each authentication method may be used only by its configured client identity; DCR and silent profile fallback remain excluded.

SKILLPILOT_SIGNING_SECRET is also mandatory when the OpenAI V1 provider is enabled. Startup aborts if the value is missing, matches the insecure placeholder, contains fewer than 32 non-whitespace characters, or exhibits insufficient structural entropy. Neither the value itself nor any excerpt is logged or echoed in error messages during this check. It is an independent HMAC operational secret and must never match the OAuth client secret.

Manage the client secret as an operational secret: restrictive file permissions, no shell history, no request/health detail exposure, and no client output. When rotating, first update ChatGPT and SkillPilot in coordination, then revoke all tokens issued under the previous client contract.

The legacy client allowlist is not part of the baseline profile; use it only during an actual client-ID change. SkillPilot then deletes OAuth authorizations, consents, registered client rows, and access and refresh tokens exclusively for the exact legacy client IDs listed. Historical connection, binding-grant, and pending-launch legacy artifacts may additionally be purged during that one-time cutover. Current openai_de_learning_session rows, however, are not deleted by a pure OAuth client rotation. Afterward, only the newly configured client may remain readable; otherwise startup aborts.

A database backup is mandatory prior to this cutover. Although the setting is idempotent for already-removed IDs, remove it from the environment again once production startup succeeds. Old access and refresh tokens and authorizations are intentionally and irrevocably invalidated; an application-only rollback will not restore them. Users re-authorize the SkillPilot app once afterward.

The current additive migration provisions openai_de_learning_session as an independent launch authorization record. Each row stores at least the hash of the random learningSessionId, the internal learner reference, started_at, and expires_at. Neither the permanent SkillPilot ID nor the plaintext session ID is duplicated there. Legacy session rows addressed solely via an OAuth subject are never used as a fallback and are removed or migrated in a controlled manner during cutover.

The historical physical table prefix openai_de_ intentionally remains in place as an internal migration anchor during this additive switch. It is no longer a language or contract marker; the binding communication language is stored per session in communication_locale. Renaming existing tables and internal Java types would be a separate, higher-risk database migration with zero benefit to the public V1 contract and does not belong in this cutover.

The start intent is a short-lived command to the domain backend. On every click on Start learning (Lernen starten), SkillPilot applies the narrowly typed intent to authoritative state under the learner lock and immediately generates a fresh cryptographically random learningSessionId. Even two launches by the same learner produce distinct IDs. The absolute lifetime is governed by SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_LEARNING_SESSION_TTL (PT24H in production). MCP calls, access-token refreshes, browser reloads, and new or parallel chats never extend it.

Before every session-bound read, write, or replay response, the V1 adapter additionally enforces the action horizon expiresAt >= now + PT1H. Exactly one hour of remaining lifetime is valid; less than one hour returns SESSION_RENEWAL_REQUIRED before any domain operation executes or any stored result is returned. A previously committed write with the exact same tool name, canonically identical arguments, and the same clientRequestId may replay—while its pinned workflow/curriculum version remains available—only if its completedStateVersion still matches the current canonical learner revision. Neither the operation nor the mutation is re-executed during replay. Every new session is always an independent record and does not revoke earlier sessions.

The session ID is inserted once automatically into the URL-encoded start prompt and subsequently passed unchanged by ChatGPT as a required argument to every learner-scoped tool. SkillPilot resolves exclusively the session-ID hash to the learner. OAuth alone neither creates nor selects a learning session, and a session ID alone never authorizes an MCP call. If either credential is missing, the domain contract returns SESSION_REQUIRED or an OAuth error respectively. SESSION_REQUIRED, SESSION_RENEWAL_REQUIRED, and SESSION_VERSION_UNAVAILABLE do not trigger a new OAuth connection: the coach outputs instruction verbatim; if absent, it uses the matching exact entry from instructions, appending the exact startUrl only if not already present in the instruction. No domain answer and no retry with the stale session follow. The learner uses Start learning (Lernen starten) in the first-party WebGUI and uses the fresh session via the prepared message in a new chat. During an ordinary desktop beta launch, the learner copies this message manually. Falling back from an OAuth subject to a learner is prohibited.

Every OpenAI launch uses exclusively POST /api/ui/learners/{skillpilotId}/openai/v1/launch. A successful request applies the typed start intent and creates exactly one new learning session plus start prompt. Every subsequent call creates a fresh session regardless of browser, existing app authorization, or prior launches. The /launch call is self-contained and requires neither a preceding connection-status check nor ephemeral intermediate browser state.

docs.title: Request-Local Diagnostic TTL
docs.text:
For a controlled live test of the one-hour action horizon, exclusively the first-party endpoint POST /api/ui/learners/{skillpilotId}/openai/v1/launch may receive the optional JSON field diagnosticSessionTtlSeconds. The server accepts it solely when SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_DIAGNOSTIC_SESSION_TTL_ENABLED=true is set. The integer value must lie between 3601 and 86400 seconds inclusive and must not exceed the normal learning-session lifetime still configured at PT24H.

The override applies solely to the single independent session created by that request; it alters neither configuration nor any other or subsequent session. The very next /launch request omitting the field automatically produces a normal PT24H session again, even while the diagnostic gate remains enabled. No other launch path accepts this field.

Recommended values:

  • 3660 seconds: roughly one minute until crossing below the PT1H action horizon;
  • 5400 seconds: 90-minute soak with roughly 30 minutes until crossing the horizon.

Do not lower SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_LEARNING_SESSION_TTL globally for this test. Returning immediately to normal runtime behavior requires only a request without the diagnostic field—neither a deployment nor a configuration change. Verify its expiresAt against startedAt + PT24H. Keep the separate diagnostic gate active only during the controlled test window, then reset it to false through the regular configuration path.

Expired or revoked learning-session records are rejected and purged independently of the OAuth lifecycle. Authorization codes, access and refresh tokens, and consents follow solely their own OAuth lifecycle. In particular, token issuance or token refresh neither creates a learning session nor extends an existing one. Technical cleanup cadence is controlled by SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS, defaulting to one hour.

Every /launch call must explicitly send providerEligibilityConfirmed=true; if missing or false, the backend rejects the launch with 403. The Cockpit prompts for this once per browser session: the learner confirms being at least 13 years old, meeting any higher minimum age applicable in their place of residence, and—if under 18—having permission from a parent or legal guardian. SkillPilot does not infer age from grade level or curriculum and stores neither date of birth nor an age profile for this check. This is an explicit self-confirmation, not identity or age verification and not OAuth client or learner identity.

The coach path requires no OpenAI model API key. Model execution and chat UI are provided by the learner's own ChatGPT account; SkillPilot provides only the MCP, OAuth, and domain backend.

The configured MCP resource is security-critical and is intentionally matched exactly. Neither leading/trailing whitespace nor an extra trailing / is accepted. Authorization requests persist this exact value, and token introspection re-verifies it as the audience on every MCP call. The same protection applies across refresh-token rotation.

docs.title: 3.1 Health, Readiness, and Metric Names
docs.text:
When SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_ENABLED=true, Spring registers the health contributor openAiDeCoach, which feeds into the separate Actuator group openaiReadiness. The contributor reports UP only when MCP and OAuth are enabled, required client and callback values are configured, public MCP/metadata targets use valid HTTPS, selected client profiles are active, and the current contract with all 14 tools is loaded. Under the JWT profile, the verified CIMD metadata cache must additionally be valid. The OpenAI readiness group also includes readinessState and the database health check db, ensuring an unreachable persistence layer can never be reported as a ready coach.

The shared readiness group contains exclusively readinessState,db. A failure isolated to JWT metadata retrieval therefore marks openaiReadiness as DOWN without blocking shared readiness or available Claude/Basic profiles. Shared readiness explicitly does not constitute OpenAI acceptance; separate provider verification and profile-specific host/release acceptance remain mandatory. SKILLPILOT_OPENAI_COACH_V1_WRITES_ENABLED=false is a permitted read-only canary state and does not set openaiReadiness to DOWN either. Whether the full coach is operationally writable in production must therefore be verified additionally via the runtime environment or a dedicated deployment preflight.
