Quellsnapshots und alte veröffentlichte Pakete bleiben unveränderte Geschichte. Die kanonischen Physiklinks dürfen erst zusammen mit der expliziten, inhaltlich begrenzten Kompatibilitätsmigration entfernt werden: Der bisherige ChampionPracticeFingerprint berücksichtigt Nicht-Curriculum-Ressourcen. Historische Praxisnachweise dürfen weder wegen einer reinen Auslagerung verloren gehen noch durch beliebige Hash-Neubindungen fälschlich gültig werden. Der lokale Migrationsnachweis liegt unter content/migrations/physik-libre-links-2026-09-20.json: Er bewahrt die elf ursprünglichen Bindungen vollständig außerhalb des Curriculums. Die inaktive historische Zuordnungsliste ist kein aktiviertes Lernmaterialpaket.

docs.title: 4. Verbraucher und Abnahmekriterien
docs.text:
Vor dem PoC lesen GoalCard und LearnerService.toFrontierGoal Ressourcen direkt aus dem kanonischen Ziel. OpenAI projiziert diese als Ressourcen; Claude gibt in formatGoal dagegen keine allgemeinen Materiallinks aus. Im Package-Modus verlangt resolveGoalResourceHref bisher einen Curriculum-Katalogeintrag. Die separate Contentauflösung muss deshalb ausdrücklich bis in UI und Claude-Kontext reichen und darf nicht nur neue JSON-Dateien bereitstellen.

Die Abnahme umfasst:

  1. Zwei getrennte Lernprofile, gleiches Curriculum: aktivierte Zuordnung nur für das Profil mit gespeicherter Auswahl, unabhängig vom KI-Host. Auswählen und Speichern funktioniert mit dem normalen Profilzugang ohne Zusatzschlüssel.
  2. Aktivieren, Deaktivieren und Paket-/Materialrücknahme verändern weder Mastery noch Frontier, Prerequisites oder aktives Lernziel.
  3. Fehlende Zuordnung, deaktivierter Dienst und nicht verfügbare externe Seite lassen normales Lernen funktionieren. Kein synchroner Websiteabruf im Coach.
  4. Fehlende oder nicht aktive Profile, nicht schreibbare Sitzungen, ungültige Paketauswahl und veraltete Revision werden weiterhin abgewiesen. Ein Profilwechsel vermischt keine Auswahlzustände; keine Freitexte oder privaten Daten in Contentpaketen.
  5. Claude erhält nur passende öffentliche Links und behauptet keinen gelesenen Volltext. Keine neuen Personalisierungstools im Coach.
  6. Ein synthetischer zweiter Anbieter und ein anderes Fach bestehen dieselben Strukturtests, ohne Sonderlogik oder zweite produktive Anbindung.
  7. Quellen, Bilder, Kernsemantik, aktuelle QS-Nachweise und M7 bleiben erhalten.

docs.title: 5. Nachweise und offene Schritte
docs.text:
Ausgeführt am 20. September 2026:

  • node --test scripts/validate_content_packages.test.mjs: neun Tests bestanden.
  • node scripts/validate_content_packages.mjs --check-links: drei öffentliche HTML-Seiten und sämtliche vier verwendeten Anker erreichbar/geprüft.
  • Fachliche Prüfung der oben benannten Abschnitte und Zuordnungsgrenzen; kurze KI-Prüfbegründungen liegen direkt beim Material. Keine Volltexte kopiert.

Backend-/UI-/Coach-Regressionsnachweise und die konkreten Sicherheits- und Betriebsschritte stehen getrennt im PoC-Betriebs- und Abnahmebericht. Lokale Tests sind keine Produktionsbereitstellung oder Realhost-Abnahme. Vor einer bestätigten Realhost-Abnahme ist ein echter Claude-Ablauf mit ausgewählter und wieder abgewählter Anbindung nachzuweisen. Ein früher ausdrücklich gesetztes SKILLPILOT_CONTENT_ENABLED=false muss bei der Bereitstellung aufgehoben werden, damit die normale Cockpit-Auswahl verfügbar ist. Die übrigen Bestandszuordnungen, insbesondere GeoGebra, bleiben eine sichtbare Folgeaufgabe; der PoC behauptet keine vollständige Bereinigung aller Curricula.

docs.title: External-content PoC: Physik Libre
docs.text: Status: updated local implementation candidate, 21 September 2026; this revision is not a deployment or real-Claude acceptance claim. Architecture: content integration.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
One separately authored public-link package for Physics goals across topics; explicit per-learner opt-in, Cockpit selection and optional Claude material hints. No provider content is downloaded at runtime. Neither a link nor a click proves reading, understanding or mastery. No new coach mutation tools, entitlement system, provider partnership or general-purpose package standard is claimed.

The eleven former Physik Libre references have been removed from canonical resourceLinks. Their exact original and retained arrays live in content/migrations/physik-libre-links-2026-09-20.json as migration evidence, not active teaching content. The deployed four-goal pilot remains as version 1.0.0. The catalog selects its expanded 1.1.0 successor with explicit AI mapping reviews and documented coverage and limits. Existing selections use the same package ID and need not be saved again after deployment. Historical references were re-examined, not automatically approved. GeoGebra is inventoried for a subsequent migration; this PoC is not a claim that all repository materials have been externalized.

HistoricalContentLinkBindings preserves historical practice fingerprints only when the current retained link array equals the migration's exact after-array. Every other goal field and actual image bytes are still fingerprinted live. No practice receipt is rewritten, no new approval is manufactured. A later substantive change uses the ordinary review process; the snapshot is not a new curriculum development freeze. --verify-relocation is a one-time check of the unchanged semantic fields at the migration checkpoint.

docs.title: Cockpit selection and deployment
docs.text:
Material selection uses the ordinary SkillPilot-ID profile access. The Product Owner explicitly confirmed on 21 September 2026 that the system should not distinguish the learner from another holder of the same ID. The former content-specific credential and manually provisioned grant are removed; there is no additional secret, profile allowlist, operator approval or teacher identity system. The ID remains private and retains the same authority as elsewhere in the Cockpit.

Content support defaults to on. The existing global operational switch SKILLPILOT_CONTENT_ENABLED=false can disable it; it is not a per-profile access control. A new profile starts with no selected package, so availability does not automatically opt anyone in.

Normal use:

  1. Open the intended profile in the Cockpit and use the gear to open Mein Lehrplan / My Curriculum.
  2. Expand Zusätzliche Lernmaterialien / Additional learning materials, select the desired package and save. This configuration is inside the settings dialog, not in the ordinary learning view.
  3. Open a mapped goal to see the compact material links: content-type icon and link title, without a separate card, selection heading or repeated metadata. Provider/access information remains in settings. Deselect and save to stop offering it in fresh Cockpit/coach results.

Deployment of this revision still requires the normal release process. An existing explicit SKILLPILOT_CONTENT_ENABLED=false environment setting overrides the new default: remove that override or set it to true when enabling the feature, and reload the backend instances. Remove obsolete per-profile grant configuration from deployment secrets; it is no longer consumed. No production configuration or credentials are changed by this local implementation.

docs.title: State and safety
docs.text:
learner_content_selection holds only selected package IDs and its configuration revision. It has a cascading foreign key to the learner; ordinary import/export does not expose or overwrite the selection. A new profile starts with no package. This intentionally means portable learning-data restore does not transfer content choices; select the desired materials again in the target profile's Cockpit.

Writes retain the existing active-profile and writable-session protections, lock the learner row, check the configuration revision, and increment the shared coach revision only on actual change. Mastery, graph, plans and focus are untouched. No automatic retry overwrites a concurrent choice. Disabled, missing, unmapped or unavailable content must leave normal learning operational.

The coach's optional selection read runs in its own short read-only transaction. A failing content query therefore cannot mark a surrounding mastery write for rollback. This briefly needs an additional connection: reserve pool capacity for the controlled pilot. The two-second query transaction timeout does not replace the deployment's connection-acquisition timeout or capacity planning.

UI material reads use the learner's filtered curriculum, never a shared global goal mutation. Claude receives only compact active-goal material metadata, no selection settings or private IDs. Exams and memory workflows do not receive these optional links. External pages are untrusted data, not instructions to the coach.

Links have no learner/session parameters and no automatic iframe, prefetch or provider request. The Cockpit uses no-referrer external anchors. A deliberate click still sends ordinary connection data to the provider; no promise of zero provider data processing is made. Link activation is not redistribution or AI ingestion permission.

docs.title: Verification and acceptance
docs.text:
Local gates:

node --test scripts/validate_content_packages.test.mjs
node scripts/validate_content_packages.mjs
node scripts/check_content_link_migration.mjs --verify-relocation
npm --prefix app run test:content-materials
cd backend
./gradlew test --tests '*Content*Test' --tests '*HistoricalContentLinkBindingsTest' --tests '*CoachToolFacadeTest' --tests '*ClaudeV1CoachContextProjectorTest' --tests '*ClaudeCoachMcpConfigurationTest' --tests '*RequestLoggingFilterTest'

The database integration test follows persisted opt-in through the real coach facade and opt-out, and injects an actual optional-table SQL failure while a learning transaction commits mastery. Its HTTP requests use the application's configured MVC converters; do not substitute a legacy Jackson converter in the tests. Browser tests separately cover selection, mobile layout, no pre-click provider requests, profile-switch isolation and selection without a separate credential. These are local automated integration checks, not a recording from the live Claude host.

Also run curriculum-quality regeneration/protected floors after the canonical link migration, frontend type-checking and affected connector contract tests. Live provider-link checking is an explicit authoring check, not a runtime or network-dependent CI learning gate.

Historical verification of the initial PoC on 20 September 2026, before removal of its additional configuration credential:

  • Package validation and nine authoring tests; four live material anchors on three provider pages; eleven exact link-relocation checks.
  • 113 focused backend tests, including real database persistence, deletion, import isolation, SQL-failure isolation, coach projection and private logging.
  • Full ./gradlew check: 217 suites, 1,956 tests passed, nine skipped, zero failures or errors (1,965 tests reported in total). The skips are the eight separately provisioned PostgreSQL OAuth tests and the external package-store conformance test; none of the new content tests was skipped.
  • Material API and browser tests, session-setup tests, existing Cockpit/Trainer regressions, full frontend lint and the complete build:application build.
  • All four locally built goal books passed publication validation; Physics rendered 478 pages.
  • Curriculum-quality regeneration, protected maturity floors and deep-review gates passed: Physics remains M7 with 478/478 strict completions.
  • Documentation link/index/terminology checks and MkDocs build passed.
  • Claude connector/plugin structural checks and all 41 checker tests passed; published Claude archive bytes and the OpenAI draft verification are unchanged. Only mutable candidate bindings were refreshed; external release gates remain pending and no earlier acceptance was transferred.

These are dated test results, not verification of the 21 September access-model change, fixed future curriculum totals or external release approvals. Rerun the affected current gates above for that change.

Verified locally on 21 September 2026 for the ordinary Cockpit selection:

  • 109 backend tests passed across content availability/catalog/resolution, selection HTTP/persistence, request logging, the coach facade and Claude context projection. Normal ID-based selection, deselection, profile isolation, revision conflicts and unavailable/read-only profiles are covered.
  • Material API/browser regressions passed without any configuration key, including persisted choices, delayed profile-switch responses, conflict reload, mobile DE/EN presentation and no provider request before a link click.
  • App type-check, affected-file lint, frontend bundle build, nine content authoring tests, catalog/migration checks, documentation links/indexes and the historical OpenAI review-integrity check passed. No learner data or production configuration was changed; no full repository CI or live-host acceptance is claimed by these targeted local checks.

Production follow-up on 21 September 2026: the supplied server log identified a Jackson-version mismatch at the selection PUT boundary. Boot's Jackson 3 HTTP converter could not deserialize the controller's Jackson 2 JsonNode, so saving failed before persistence. Both earlier content HTTP test setups had forced a Jackson 2 converter and therefore missed this fault. With the actual MVC context, the existing save test reproduced the same exception before the fix.

The controller now uses the Jackson 3 request tree, preserving strict validation, ordinary profile guards and revision checks. The updated MVC/database tests cover selection, re-read, deselection, conflicts and invalid input without changing stored selection, activity or coach revision. All 110 focused backend tests and the material API/browser tests passed locally. This is not a full CI or live-host acceptance claim. Deploy the corrected backend; no frontend change, database migration or additional content access permission is needed for this repair.

Real-host release acceptance remains separate:

  1. Open an existing active profile in the intended environment and select a package through its normal Cockpit settings, with no separate access key.
  2. Open one mapped, reachable goal; verify the same material in Cockpit and a real Claude context/tool response without transmitting private credentials.
  3. Continue the actual learning conversation; material is optional, not a task completion signal. Capture sanitized evidence, not private chat text in Core.
  4. Disable, reload and continue in the existing session. Fresh context must stop offering the material. Already returned provider conversation text cannot be retracted by disabling a package.
  5. Check a second profile, an unmapped goal and a broken/unavailable provider page; normal learning and mastery persistence must continue in every case.

Rollback: disable the content flag; selections remain inert and may be re-enabled later. Do not drop tables or roll back curriculum/review history to disable an optional material offer. Subsequent ChatGPT acceptance reuses this backend path; no parallel ChatGPT beta distribution is part of this PoC.

docs.title: Issue #54: Ausbau optionaler Content-Pakete
docs.text: Stand: 30. September 2026. Issue #54 verlangt konkrete, kostenlos für den vorgesehenen Lernzweck erreichbare Materialien, präzise Zielzuordnung und getrennte Nachweise für lokale Prüfung, CI und Produktion. Der priorisierte LEIFI-Gleichstromlink wurde nach einem geschlossenen Touch-Stromkreis lokal aktiviert; CI- und Produktionsnachweise fehlen weiterhin.

docs.title: Umgesetzter Umfang
docs.text:
Der Katalog enthält die 1.1.0-Nachfolger für Mathematik, PhET-Physik, LabXchange und oPhysics sowie Physik Libre. Die 1.0.0-Piloten dieser Pakete bleiben unverändert. Die Nachfolger enthalten direkte Einzelaktivitäten: Mathe mit GeoGebra, Desmos und PhET; Physik mit regulären PhET-Simulationen; LabXchange mit fünf englischen OpenStax-Artikeln (Anbieterzielgruppe 13+); oPhysics mit acht englischen Aktivitäten von Tom Walsh. Fachlicher Nutzen, Modellgrenzen, Sprachen, Anbieter und begründet ausgeschiedene Kandidaten stehen in den jeweiligen Paket-READMEs. Für eigenes SkillPilot-Mapping ist enpasos Kurator; die verlinkten Dienste und Urheber bleiben getrennt ausgewiesen. Alle aktiven Materialien verwenden public-link und link-only.

Das zuvor unveröffentlichte LEIFIphysik-Paket ist jetzt mit zwei aktiven Materialien katalogisiert: der Zentripetalkraft-Simulation und der priorisierten Gleichstromseite mit LEIFI-Arbeitsaufträgen. Deren PhET-Einbettung wird nicht als zusätzliche Simulation gezählt. Diese Auswahl ist optional; fehlende Auswahl oder ein Ausfall ändert weder Mastery noch Voraussetzungen oder Lernplan.

docs.title: LEIFI-Browserbeleg und Grenze
docs.text:
Beide konkreten Direkt-URLs wurden am 30. September in frischen anonymen Playwright-Chromium-Kontexten geprüft. 390 × 844 war ein emulierter Touch-Viewport, kein physisches Smartphone:

Test Gleichstrom mit PhET Zentripetalkraft Regulärer Desktop-UA, 1365 × 900, wiederholt HTTP 403, Cloudflare-Sicherheitsprüfung HTTP 403, Cloudflare-Sicherheitsprüfung Mobiler UA, 390 × 844, Touch HTTP 200; Aufgaben und PhET-Iframe mit Intro/Labor und Komponenten geladen HTTP 200; Aufgaben, Canvas, Startknopf und drei Regler geladen Touch-Ereignisse im emulierten Viewport Direkter Touch startete PhET-Intro; Touch-Drags verbanden Batterie und Lampe über zwei Drähte. PhET-Accessibility meldete Current is flowing in 1 of 1 groups und Light Bulb 1 of 1,brightness 21%. Start änderte Canvas-Bild; Masse-Regler änderte sichtbaren Wert von 1,1 auf 1,8 kg und Canvas-Bild erneut Mobiler UA bei Desktop-Breite HTTP 200, Seite geladen HTTP 200, Seite geladen

Der mobile Test belegt einen geschlossenen Stromkreis mit Stromfluss und sichtbarer Lampenreaktion. Die LEIFI-Aufträge waren ohne Konto lesbar, wurden jedoch nicht vollständig bearbeitet. Der normale Desktop-Zugang ist aus dieser Prüfungsumgebung weiterhin nicht bestätigt. Die wiederholten 403-Antworten sind eine umgebungsabhängige Zugangsgrenze, kein Beleg für allgemeine Unverfügbarkeit. Physische Smartphone-Bedienung und umfassende Barrierefreiheit wurden nicht geprüft.

docs.title: Lokale Prüfungen
docs.text:
• node scripts/validate_content_packages.mjs: erfolgreich; nach LEIFI-Katalogisierung 6 Pakete mit insgesamt 252 deklarierten Materialien, beide LEIFI-Materialien aktiv.
  • node --test scripts/validate_content_packages.test.mjs: 17/17 erfolgreich. Der Test prüft aktuelle Ziel-IDs, Kurator/Anbieter, Status beider LEIFI-Materialien und die kombinierte Grenze von vier aktiven Links je Ziel.
  • npm --prefix app run test:content-materials: erfolgreich; API- und UI-Prüfungen für die optionale Materialanzeige.
  • cd backend && ./gradlew test --tests 'com.skillpilot.backend.content.ContentCatalogTest' --tests 'com.skillpilot.backend.content.ContentMaterialResolverTest' --tests 'com.skillpilot.backend.content.ContentSelectionIntegrationTest' --tests 'com.skillpilot.backend.content.ContentSelectionControllerHttpTest': erfolgreich. Der Resolver-Test prüft den LEIFI-Katalogeintrag mit materialCount=2 und die fünf aktiven Zuordnungen.

Alle fünf LEIFI-Ziel-IDs sind im aktuellen kanonischen Inventar vorhanden und als curricularAtomic eingestuft. Die kombinierte Zahl aktiver Materiallinks überschreitet an keinem Ziel vier; bei 01bebdfc-5819-4610-a03e-ea5e794fc954 sind es mit LEIFI genau vier. Die Testläufe belegen den lokalen Arbeitsbaum; sie ersetzen weder CI noch Produktzugang.

docs.title: CI und Produktion
docs.text:
Der bisherige Ausbau-Commit 8ef49014fc627a3ef55995c9408cf3318f0b89e2 liegt auf origin/main. Eine read-only GitHub-Abfrage zeigte für diesen Commit keine Check-Runs, Actions-Runs oder Commit-Statusmeldungen; ein CI-Erfolg für diesen Stand wurde daher nicht verifiziert. Die hier dokumentierte LEIFI-Änderung ist lokal und hat ebenfalls keinen CI-Nachweis.

https://skillpilot.com/ antwortete mit HTTP 200. Das belegt nur die Erreichbarkeit der Startseite. Der Materialkatalog ist lernendenbezogen; der versuchte Pfad /api/ui/content/catalog antwortete 404 und ist kein gültiger Produktionsnachweis. Ob die neuen Pakete in Produktion angeboten werden, ist nicht bestätigt. Es erfolgten weder Deployment noch GitHub-Schreibaktionen. Issue #54 war bei der read-only Prüfung offen.

docs.title: Offene Abnahme
docs.text:
1. Den regulären Desktop-Zugang aus einer anderen Umgebung prüfen; den 390 × 844-Touch-Test bei Bedarf auf einem physischen Smartphone ergänzen.
  2. Für den geänderten Arbeitsbaum CI mit terminalen Ergebnissen prüfen und danach die tatsächliche Produktionsauswahl in einer autorisierten Lernendensitzung bestätigen.
  3. Issue #54 erst nach diesen getrennten Belegen als vollständig abgeschlossen bewerten.

docs.title: CQR-104: current endpoint visibility findings
docs.text: Candidate evidence for the F5 work in the hard-gate plan, based on main 2ad03c810c896d0bab96cd69d1cd96f45973d8e2. This is not main or production acceptance. The existing eight required visibility scopes remain required; the four upper-secondary gaps are not promoted by this report.

docs.title: Reproduce the measurement
docs.text:
npm --prefix app run report:route-endpoint-visibility -- \
  --output ../docs/qa-ci/status/route-endpoint-visibility-audit.json

The command exits 1 while any measured obligation fails. It invokes the actual CQR-104 evaluator, first with the missing SekII configuration and then with the existing compiled-jurisdiction mode. It does not change the registered profiles, pins, applicability, assessment contracts or reviews. The JSON report contains every finding and 381 raw input hashes: the measured canonical documents, all view files read to determine membership, and the shared selector/evaluator inputs. Its applicability-report hash binds derived compiler output, not new source evidence or a complete provenance receipt.

docs.title: Implemented corrections
docs.text:
The evaluator now uses each authored view's course and duration filters for both the actual projection and the independently expected endpoints, in every subject. Previously this was complete only for Economics. For example, an LK-only ENG/ECG assessment cannot be required in the national Biology GK view. Country applicability alone does not establish course or duration applicability.

The national Biology view already referenced eight assessment collections, but used shallow goalEntry nodes. Those references displayed the folders without their tasks. They now use canonicalSubtree, retaining the same identities, labels, roles and canonical contents. Of their 26 existing assessments, 21 belong in the GK projection; five LK-only tasks remain filtered out. No task, prerequisite, source claim, assessment coverage or review was authored by this projection correction.

testBiologyAssessmentProjection.ts, invoked by test:graph-gate-contracts, reproduces the old shallow-folder failure, checks the exact restored GK task set independently from the view, retains all previous canonical atomic targets, and checks the LK exclusion. It also runs the actual evaluator over all eight pinned scopes and verifies that the remaining Biology gaps still fail. This is a partial repair, not twelve-scope acceptance.

docs.title: Remaining findings after the correction
docs.text:
Counts below are view/jurisdiction projections, not additional QA scopes. Each subject is still one unpinned upper-secondary QA scope.

Scope Relevant views Compiled projections Projections missing expected endpoints Other findings Mathematics Sek II 80 140 140 State/course/stage placement and assessment obligations need reconciliation. Physics Sek II 68 128 64 60 projections also expose unexpected terminals under this prospective configuration. Chemistry Sek II 41 101 101 Two configured terminals have no compiled jurisdiction applicability. Biology Sek II 3 18 2 Five national-view jurisdictions have no applicable configured terminal.

The simpler, non-jurisdiction-expanded configuration still fails in 80/80 Mathematics, 64/68 Physics, 41/41 Chemistry and 2/3 Biology views. It is not a substitute for the scoped applicability check.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
The current evaluator expects the Insulin/Plasmid assessment (1d0c84df-8040-5cab-8a7c-359366937e44) and colour-vision assessment (7c7f147c-2b64-5b0c-90c1-ea9a9bf4b03a) in both Sachsen-Anhalt Sek-II views from their existing applicability metadata. Both views omit them. A separate author analysis and independent task-contract review on 13 November examined the actual tasks, solutions, rubrics, atomic goal descriptions and official curriculum. They found a concrete ST eAN/LK subject basis, together with contract gaps that prevent accepting an unchanged placement repair.

The official Sachsen-Anhalt Biology curriculum, 1 August 2022 explicitly includes photoreceptors and colour/contrast perception at eAN (printed/PDF pp. 57–59), and genetically modified organisms, restriction enzymes, vectors and gel electrophoresis at eAN (pp. 60–61). The gAN pages 46–49 support broader perception, protein-biosynthesis and material-based genetic-test work. They do not establish the same specific prior knowledge for both unchanged tasks. A sufficiently supported transfer task could suit gAN, but that requires its own task/material and course decision. Global GK/LK tags inherited from Hessen do not decide ST applicability and must not be narrowed globally merely to repair ST.

Existing assessment Actual task and rubric Contract mismatch Insulin Explain cDNA suitability for a bacterial host; match supplied fragment lengths to samples; explain DNA → mRNA → protein; distinguish DNA presence from functional expression. 22 direct prerequisites include drift, Hardy–Weinberg, SNP analysis, epigenetics and other unneeded contracts. The two coveredGoalIds clusters expand to 36 ordinary atoms, far beyond the four assessed tasks. Colour vision Use a supplied cone model to interpret a possible effect of M-cone dysfunction and explain redundant signal design using contrast, position and other information. 16 direct prerequisites include hearing, pain, Hebbian learning, ENG/ECG and other unneeded contracts. The two coverage clusters expand to 28 ordinary atoms; organ anatomy, complete visual pathways and detailed neural transduction are not tested.

For Insulin, the existing atom 374e6de5-0747-57cb-99e3-e50ccb371124 (compatible conditions for recombinant protein expression) is a close contract candidate, with protein biosynthesis already among its transitive prerequisites. The cDNA/intron knowledge required by task 1 is not supplied in the material; the existing alternative-splicing goal also demands protein diversity and evolutionary interpretation and is too broad a substitute. Restriction and gel goals are possible preparation candidates, not automatically assessed coverage: expected fragment lengths are supplied, with no independent recognition-sequence or size-marker task. Their complete atomic promises therefore cannot be copied into the coverage list. The expression atom's current raw applicability is only DE-HE, with an explicit mapping-inheritance boundary; an ST mapping needs its own evidence.

For colour vision, 9499943f-89b7-54e3-9fe2-e90404beaa4a (structure and function of selected sense organs) is a possible preparation candidate, but its full promise is not tested. No exact existing atom for the narrow qualitative cone/contrast performance was established. The listed sensitivity maxima do not determine response curves or unique responses to the two wavelengths. The present task supports a qualitative possible loss of information, not a quantitative discrimination claim. A revised task must state the intended inference and provide the necessary model/data; extra prerequisite edges cannot supply missing task evidence.

Both tasks use a total of 30 points and a passing threshold of 18. Insulin can pass with tasks 1–3 scoring 22 points and task 4 scoring zero; colour vision can pass with tasks 1, 3 and 4 scoring 22 and the dysfunction analysis in task 2 scoring zero. Thus passing alone does not demonstrate every claimed atomic competence. Preparation, assessed coverage and globally recognized mastery remain separate; neither requires nor visible placement writes mastery. These counterexamples do not claim that existing learners have already received an incorrect result.

The next subject-authoring step is a reviewed narrow Insulin eAN contract that closes the cDNA preparation/material gap, followed by a precise colour- vision target and matching task/rubric. The review must bind actual atomic coverage, course-specific applicability, necessary preparation and the meaning of a passing result. Both released identities also carry a separate assessmentApplicabilityBasis referencing the old clusters; changing only coveredGoalIds would leave that basis untouched. Before changing an existing identity, check result/history and selection semantics explicitly and decide whether a reviewed correction/migration or a distinct successor identity is needed. No effect on existing learner records is asserted without that check. Do not rewrite the frozen V9 evidence or silently reuse it for a changed goal.

Consequently this is F5's documented evidence-gap outcome, not an approved replacement prerequisite list, new review pass or permission to place both tasks in both ST courses. New assessment, coverage, applicability and result contracts remain subject-authoring follow-up work. The availability of the official PDF proves a source basis, not a finished atomic task contract.

The inspected inputs are reproducible without the exploratory drafts:

  • Canonical Biology, the two goal IDs above, including examData, requires, assessmentApplicabilityBasis and the referenced ordinary goals. Raw SHA-256: 0de1cfc92fd15d6633575f6f1da9aa78027feec4383e45f50ca738744977fe5e.
  • Retained official PDF at curricula/DE/Gymnasium/input/ST/FLP_Biologie_Gym_01082022_swd.pdf, pp. 46–49 and 57–61, with official provenance recorded in the source registry. Raw SHA-256: 58b106c65a71478a096f31cf8e9743a238a59aec085414ac472ee0ab5da10c38.
  • The preparation/coverage distinction and released-assessment identity boundary in AGENTS.md, sections 2 and 6.3. This audit changes none of those contracts or any curriculum/view bytes.

In the national GK view, BW, NI, HB, HH and SL still have no applicable configured terminal. Exposing another folder cannot create the missing applicability/assessment evidence. Review existing suitable assessments and their actual coverage first; if none applies, author and independently review an appropriate assessment. Do not broaden an applicability override just to remove these findings.

docs.title: Chemistry
docs.text: The two endpoints without compiled applicability are eed5eda3-2daf-5d48-b935-23dadd622d9b (chemical knowledge development, with course assignment explicitly unresolved) and d7abdeb3-5b69-5744-b7fd-8149fd92b0d5 (Grignard alcohol synthesis). Source, course and assessment evidence must settle these cases before pinning the whole scope. The report separately lists missing placements in all 101 compiled projections; hiding these two endpoints would not resolve them.

docs.title: Physics and Mathematics
docs.text: The report names every missing/unexpected endpoint by view, jurisdiction and goal ID. Physics already has deliberate stage-specific and prerequisite-only assessment placements. These cannot be converted wholesale into target endpoints. Mathematics likewise needs its state/course-specific assessment collections checked against authoritative target scope and actual tasks. Restoring Biology's already authored national collections does not authorize adding every canonical examination to every state view.

docs.title: Decision after the Biology package
docs.text: Matching course/duration filters is a shared evaluator correction. The remaining curriculum gaps have different causes and do not support one bulk repair across all four subjects. Keep compositionVisibilityRequired unchanged until a complete subject scope passes with independent applicability and assessment evidence. CQR-104 therefore remains PARTIAL at eight of twelve scopes. Even twelve passing scopes would not by itself prove the additional semantic route obligation of GD-C22 or the broader assessment/runtime obligations of GD-A18.

docs.title: Gymnasium retained-source boundary (F3)
docs.text: The follow-up programme classifies the 45 Bavarian files in curricula/DE/Gymnasium/input/BY/gymnasium/ as frozen source material. Their original bytes, IDs, relationships, mappings and provenance bindings remain intact. Their old root-to-orientation prerequisite constructs are source history and do not enter the current G17 inventory.

docs.title: Measured consumers
docs.text:
The 45 files contain 8,413 goals, between 4 and 893 per file. The source landscape IDs occur in 47 mapping documents (21 distinct source IDs), four provenance documents (21 IDs) and four canonical documents (five IDs). The canonical occurrences are provenance references: no canonical requires or contains edge depends on a retained Bavarian goal or landscape ID.

Consumer Original behavior Boundary in this change app/scripts/lib/graphValidationInventory.ts Recursively discovered the 45 files as live graphs Discovers exactly the registered current canonical catalog inside Gymnasium; retained inputs and authoring metadata are excluded. Unexpected live Gymnasium graphs and incomplete/additional canonical inventory fail closed. app/scripts/validateGraph.ts Included source goals in the global validation universe Keeps sources outside that universe. An explicit source-reference resolver preserves existing references from consumers outside curricula/DE/Gymnasium/; canonical consumers cannot use it. Backend LandscapeService Discovered the 45 raw files and also added registered archived/source-extraction landscapes to getAll, getById and the global goal index Separates retained source maps from active discovery and lookup. getRetainedSourceLandscape reads source evidence explicitly, including a localized source view. Source membership and atomic-closure APIs retain their evidence behavior. Backend legacy closure Resolved legacy references through the same active/source index Existing noncanonical roots can traverse explicit retained-source references. Entering any canonical graph disables this fallback, including when the traversal started outside Gymnasium. Active definitions retain precedence when IDs collide. Backend GoalMappingService, canonical provenance and applicability Read mapping files and source/jurisdiction registries independently of runtime landscape discovery These inputs and APIs remain in use. CurriculaService obtains source atomic closure through resolveSourceAtomicGoalIds; the source API can derive local atomic descendants from the frozen source when no closure entry exists. app/scripts/applicabilityCompiler.ts Uses the source registry first, with a source-path index as fallback Continues to read source evidence independently; the live validation inventory is not its source index. Source extraction and authoring tools Explicitly read frozen Bavarian source JSON Paths remain unchanged. Consumers include generateByPhysicsSourceExtraction.ts, generateByChemistrySourceExtraction.ts, generateByEconomicsSourceExtraction.ts, the Bavarian Mathematics course-projection audits, Physics adjudication scripts and goal-book source tests. Deck deployment Canonical deployment uses registered files in memory-decks/; legacy deployment uses deck filenames in directories named json Neither deployment enumerates these 45 files as decks or as live graphs. Backend DeckResourceService Indexes deck filename patterns under json and memory-decks Does not depend on landscape graph discovery. Its retained deck behavior stays available. Schema checking and repository revision Validate source JSON syntax and bind repository input bytes Retained evidence still participates in syntax/provenance integrity and revision binding. This does not make it a live G17 graph.

The shared source-landscape registry has 302 entries, 298 with an archiveSourcePath; 21 refer to these Bavarian source identities. Some paths use the historical DE-BY spelling, resolved by the existing retained-path normalization. No registry or frozen proof is rewritten.

docs.title: Existing outside references
docs.text:
curricula/DE/BY/DE_BY_Gymnasium_Overview.json is outside the current canonical Gymnasium domain and is not a manifest root. Its 45 contains references point to retained Bavarian subject-root goal IDs. Removing source lookup without an explicit compatibility route produced exactly 45 missing-ID errors in validate:graph. The source-only resolver preserves those references without adding the source graphs to validation or the canonical runtime universe.

Twenty-five retained source landscape IDs also occur in other Bavarian school forms. Separating the source maps preserves the active school-form definition for ordinary landscape and goal lookup. Explicit source evidence remains addressable by its source identity. Compatibility traversal likewise keeps the existing active-owner deduplication; it does not add source-only goals under a colliding active landscape ID. The other 20 Bavarian source owners have no goal ID overlap with active definitions. No outside curriculum JSON is changed.

The resulting validator inventory is 548 files: 21 canonical Gymnasium catalog entries and the same 527 files outside Gymnasium. The canonical catalog remains the G17 gate domain. Explicit historical source reads and noncanonical compatibility closures are separate from that live inventory.

docs.title: Regression and verification contract
docs.text:
testGraphValidationRetirement.ts checks exact registered-catalog membership, unchanged discovery behavior for outside input directories, reserved evidence exclusion, rejected extra or missing canonical files, rejected live Gymnasium graphs outside the catalog, and source-reference acceptance only outside Gymnasium.

LandscapeServiceSourceRegistryTest checks active/source index separation, source membership and atomic closure, preserved noncanonical closure, canonical source rejection and active-first collision handling. The backend directory-scan fixtures retain their existing outside-Gymnasium behavior. The CLI and CI reject unexpected live graphs in Gymnasium; the backend excludes those files with a diagnostic while keeping the other graphs and learner reads available, following the 11 November runtime-readability decision. Repository source-extraction probes use the explicit retained-source accessor instead of asserting runtime availability. Existing retired-learner selection, read-only state, projection and export tests remain required; rewriting source-reader expectations alone does not establish runtime compatibility.

The reload fingerprint keeps the prior JSON input membership, including retained inputs, while the loader skips their live parsing. It performs no extra complete fingerprint scan on reload. At this checkout the fingerprint membership is 8,223 JSON files, including 446 Gymnasium input files. Archived snapshots retain the existing explicit source-reader behavior.

For a reproducible raw-byte preservation check, sort the 45 graph paths, then hash each repository-relative UTF-8 path followed by NUL, the raw file bytes, and NUL with SHA-256. The audit value before and after this change is 2aa5f3bd5df7608585092294eb0669bc9f818c552b912d3b89f59d7ae6a3ffa5. No source graph is normalized and no historical proof is replayed or rebound.

docs.title: Local verification
docs.text:
• npm --prefix app run validate:graph: 548 landscapes passed.
  • npx tsx --test scripts/testGraphValidationRetirement.ts in app/: 8 tests passed.
  • python3 scripts/validate_bavaria_gymnasium_archive_paths.py: no violations.
  • python3 scripts/validate_bavaria_gymnasium_legacy_refs.py: no violations.

docs.title: CQR and GVR Gates: Work Plan to HARD
docs.text:
Snapshot: 12 November 2026; delivery record updated 13 November. Status: bounded implementation delivered in PR #131, head 39fe19b658, based on 38b1080130, subsequently merged as dcf5278881. Its complete PR CI passed; subsequent main 2129b207f4 passed complete CI #2315. Section 9 records the exact verification scope and later main changes. The bounded main delivery is complete; the two broader target gaps remain open. The owner authorized plan review, necessary adjustments, autonomous implementation and PR creation. The execution choices in section 4 apply; merge and publication are separate operations.

This document retains the original work packages and their delivery evidence. The implementation replaced indirect enforcement with direct gates in the declared domains and retired two redundant codes. The delivered legend has 22 HARD and 2 PARTIAL codes. The remaining evidence gaps (CQR-104, GVR-012) require broader curriculum work; they are not part of the completed bounded hardening.

Current state and next steps: section 11. Section 10 records the owner decision of 13 November 2026 and the follow-up packages F1–F5, delivered in PR #141. Sections 1–9 are the record of the first delivery and are not reopened.

Related material:

  • Register source: docs/concept/skill-graph/source/rules-and-gates.json (gatesOverview.rows is the code legend; ampelSection defines the traffic-light states). Rendered as Rule-to-Milestone Matrix.
  • Predecessor work: Transitive Minimalität: Lieferplan nach main.
  • Standing rules: AGENTS.md (authoritative), CLAUDE.md.

docs.title: 1. Outcome
docs.text:
The initial code legend listed 8 GVR and 18 CQR codes. At that baseline, 5 GVR codes were HARD; GVR-006, GVR-012, GVR-013 and all 18 CQR codes were PARTIAL.

The bounded implementation is complete: the executable portions of the work packages were delivered in a PR with terminal green remote CI and integrated into main, with subsequent green integration CI. Unfulfilled target items remain explicit, and the register states exactly which domain each gate covers. The full HARD target still requires genuine endpoint visibility evidence for the four remaining scopes in WP5, and independently evidenced semantic route coverage as described in WP6. A measured missing prerequisite remains an explicit open item; neither a narrower validator nor invented curriculum evidence may be presented as completing the stronger target.

A main acceptance claim requires the gate to be merged to main and green in remote CI. The implementation PR may update the register together with the code it describes, but must distinguish candidate enforcement from accepted main evidence. Assigning a rule to a validation area is not a pass.

docs.title: 2. Baseline (measured 12 November 2026)
docs.text:
This section records the initial pre-implementation snapshot, not the current delivered results. Re-measure for verification; do not overwrite this baseline or rely on its findings as current after implementation changes.

# Catalog-wide G17 report without failing (about one minute)
(cd app && npx tsx scripts/auditTransitiveMinimality.ts --report-only)
# Current status snapshot and floor check
npm --prefix app run quality:curriculum-status:check

docs.title: 2.1 Why the 18 CQR codes are only PARTIAL
docs.text:
At the initial baseline, CQR results did not fail CI directly. generateCurriculumQualityStatus.ts computes a maturity per curriculum, and checkCurriculumMaturityFloors.ts fails only when one of ten protected subjects drops below its floor.

The catalog (curricula/DE/Gymnasium/canonical/, 21 landscapes) splits as follows in docs/qa-ci/status/curriculum-quality-status.json (curriculum-quality-v5):

Group Curricula Floor M7 Biologie, Chemie, Mathematik, Physik, Wirtschaftswissenschaften M7 M6 Deutsch, Geschichte, Informatik, Latein, Politik und Wirtschaft M6 M0 Chinesisch, Englisch, Französisch, Griechisch, Italienisch, Musik, Polnisch, Russisch, Spanisch, Tschechisch, overview root none

So 11 of 21 catalog entries have no CI protection at all, and for the other ten the protection is indirect.

Rule results across the 21 curricula and the 12 registered QA scopes:

Rule pass Other CQR-000 10 7 warn, 4 fail CQR-001 14 7 fail CQR-002 21 – CQR-003 10 11 warn CQR-004 16 5 not_configured CQR-005 20 1 not_configured (overview root) CQR-301, CQR-302 10 11 not_configured CQR-303 5 16 not_configured CQR-401 11 10 not_configured CQR-501 21 – CQR-101, 102, 103, 201, 202, 203 12 of 12 scopes – CQR-104 8 of 12 scopes absent in 4 scopes

All 12 QA scopes belong to the ten protected subjects. No M0 curriculum has a QA scope, a review configuration or a route profile.

docs.title: 2.2 CQR-001 (G17) failures
docs.text:
Complete-catalog auditor run: 14 roots pass, 7 do not.

Root Result Englisch fail: 66 minimality findings, 45 non-atomic requires Spanisch fail: 32 minimality findings, 61 non-atomic requires Musik fail: 10 minimality findings, 43 non-atomic requires Chinesisch, Französisch, Griechisch invalid-input: effective requires self-cycle; the auditor stops there. A raw count shows 29, 22 and 20 authored requires on clusters. Overview root invalid-input: inherits the Griechisch cycle

The self-cycle is one construct per file: the subject root requires its own direct child (the "Warum …" motivation node), so that child inherits a requirement on itself.

docs.title: 2.3 Why three GVR codes are only PARTIAL
docs.text:
Code Finding GVR-006 Scoped to 17 Hessen rollout landscape IDs (noDirectChildRequireRuleLandscapeIds in app/scripts/validateGraph.ts). None of these IDs is a loaded landscape any more; they exist only in archive and provenance registries. The rule currently checks nothing. The same holds for GVR-004 and GVR-005. GVR-013 Scoped to canonical Mathematics. Since 11 November 2026 CQR-001 requires atomic endpoints on every authored requires in the whole catalog, which is strictly stronger. GVR-012 Scoped to canonical Mathematics Sek I and Sek II through a profile list in validateGraph.ts. The status generator keeps routeProfiles with all 12 QA scopes for the weaker reachability invariant CQR-102; these checks are not equivalent.

Applied to all 593 loaded landscape files, the GVR-006 condition would report 567 violations: 3 inside the catalog (the three self-cycles above) and 564 in landscapes outside the catalog, where the root-requires-"Warum"-child construct is the standard legacy pattern.

docs.title: 2.4 Wiring gaps
docs.text:
• npm run check:transitive-minimality already is a complete-catalog, fail-closed G17 check. It is called neither by run_ci.sh nor by .github/workflows/ci.yml.
  • run_ci.sh regenerates and diffs the status but does not call check:curriculum-maturity-floors; only remote CI does.

docs.title: 3. What HARD means in this plan
docs.text:
A legend row may be graded HARD when all four hold:

  • H1 – Derived or pinned domain. The set of landscapes or scopes the gate covers is computed from the complete catalog or pinned in a committed register whose coverage is itself checked. It cannot shrink silently.
  • H2 – Direct failure. CI fails on any violation inside that domain. It does not depend on a floor happening to cover the affected subject.
  • H3 – No bypass. No environment switch, not_configured result or optionally attached rule lets a violation through.
  • H4 – Main acceptance. The claim is true for the whole domain on main, with terminal green CI for the merged head. Before merge, a candidate may document H1–H3 enforcement and passing candidate evidence, but must not claim H4 or main acceptance. Candidate HARD legend entries describe the code under review, not an authorized merge or an accepted-main result.

Two classes of rule follow from this:

  • Class I – catalog invariants. Must be pass for all 21 catalog curricula at all times: CQR-001, CQR-002, CQR-501.
  • Class II – milestone and scope obligations. Bind a curriculum or QA scope from the milestone at which it is pinned: CQR-000, 003, 004, 005, 101–104, 201–203, 301–303, 401. The CQR-104 obligation applies only to its eight explicitly pinned visibility scopes; the four remaining route profiles carry documented unmet visibility obligations, not silently skipped required results.

docs.title: 4. Execution choices within the authorization
docs.text:
These are implementation choices made under the owner's autonomous-work instruction, not newly attributed dated Product Owner policy decisions.

ID Choice Boundary D1 Use direct milestone-bound enforcement over a complete pin register; retain M0 as a legitimate starting state. State the covered domain and count for each gate. Require every applicable rule to pass directly; check pins against an independent inventory and the Git base policy. A maturity label alone is insufficient. D2 Retire empty legacy GVR-006 and Mathematics-only GVR-013 together with the stronger catalog G17 gate. Preserve CQR-101, CQR-103 and the scope maturity ladder. Do not infer semantic equivalence of different route validators from green current data. D3 Keep non-catalog landscapes outside the CQR/G17 domain, following the existing 12 November decision. Their legacy constructs and runtime fallback stay outside this implementation. D4 Deliver the interdependent packages as separately reviewable commits in one PR against main. No merge or production operation is authorized. Run the complete CI tier when the PR is ready.

docs.title: 5. Legacy inventory
docs.text:
Principle: never harden a legacy construct. Delete dead code, repair legacy data, and retire a rule once a stronger gate implies it within the deliberately covered catalog domain. Retirement does not expand the successor gate to non-canonical landscapes.

ID Legacy item Evidence Disposition L1 Hessen rollout ID lists and the rules scoped to them (GVR-004, GVR-005, GVR-006; the Physics-to-Mathematics cross-reference guard keyed on the archived Hessen Physics ID) No listed ID is a loaded landscape Delete in WP1 L2 VALIDATE_GRAPH_STRICT_RULES=0 warn-only mode Not set by any CI entry point; documented as a legacy mode Delete in WP1 L3 Cluster requires and the root-requires-"Warum"-child construct in six catalog subjects Section 2.2 Repair in WP2 L4 check:transitive-minimality and the floor check missing from CI entry points Section 2.4 Wire in WP3 L5 Floor policy v1: 10 of 21 curricula; stale knownPreBaselineRegressions entry for Wirtschaftswissenschaften (now M7 with an M7 floor); hard-coded baselineDate equality app/scripts/config/curriculum-maturity-floor-policy.json, checkCurriculumMaturityFloors.ts Replace by v2 in WP4 L6 Leniencies in the promotion chain: CQR-104 is skipped when a scope has no compositionViewStage; CQR-004 blocks only on fail and CQR-005 only on warn deriveScopeMaturity, deriveCurriculumMaturity Close in WP5 L7 Catalog maturityTarget for CQR-104 (M3) and CQR-203 (M4) differs from the level they actually gate (M4, M5) ruleCatalog in the generator; register prose "abweichend" Align metadata in WP5 L8 Two hand-maintained route profile lists for one invariant validateGraph.ts profiles versus routeProfiles Unify in WP6 L9 Codes implied by G17 or duplicated: GVR-006, GVR-013, CQR-103 (no cluster may carry requires at all), CQR-101 (equals CQR-102 once no cluster carries requires), GVR-011 (implied by GVR-012) Section 2.3 WP7, subject to D2 L10 Historical reduction proofs (prerequisiteReductionProof in the status artifact) Still used to reuse dependent review evidence Out of scope; removing them needs its own decision because M6/M7 evidence depends on them

docs.title: 6. Working rules
docs.text:
• One integration PR against main, with Conventional Commits separating work packages and each subject migration. Use local checks while developing; draft CI is only the quick tier, and the final ready PR must run the complete remote tier. Do not merge.
  • Never lower or remove a floor, add a floor exception, bulk-decide a review queue or hand-edit a generated file to make a check pass.
  • Changes under curricula/ are evidence-bound. WP2 mechanically materializes existing prerequisite statements, removes their invalid self-pairs and transitively reduces the atomic relation. Do not invent prerequisite intent, alter other goal fields or rewrite review decisions. G17 acceptance uses the current graph; the 12 November decision supersedes historical closure and frontier preservation as acceptance requirements.
  • After any curriculum or generator change run npm --prefix app run quality:curriculum-status and confirm that no protected maturity dropped.
  • Scope every search to a concrete directory. Never search from the repository root; tmp/ and site/ are large.
  • Resolve routine implementation findings and record deviations in section 9. Continue independent work when a package hits a genuine evidence gap. Do not fabricate missing reviews, source evidence or semantic classifications.

docs.title: 7. Work packages
docs.text: Order: WP1 and WP2 are independent. WP3 needs WP2. WP4 and WP5 share one enforcement contract and are tested together. WP7 is delivered with WP3; WP8 describes the final integrated candidate and records remote evidence.

docs.title: WP1 – Delete dead validator scope (L1, L2)
docs.text:
Deleting the dead rules and warning switch alone preserves the passing baseline. The integrated PR additionally enforces CQR-102 across all twelve profiles under WP6; that intentionally extends the set of violations rejected by validate:graph.

  1. Prove the scope is empty: add a focused test or assertion showing that no loaded landscape under curricula/ has an ID from motivationRuleLandscapeIds, HESSEN_GYM_OVERVIEW_LANDSCAPE_ID, MATH_LANDSCAPE_ID or PHYSICS_LANDSCAPE_ID.
  2. In app/scripts/validateGraph.ts delete those ID lists, the GVR-004 and GVR-005 blocks, the Hessen Physics cross-reference guard and the VALIDATE_GRAPH_STRICT_RULES switch. Every remaining GVR rule reports error unconditionally. Remove GVR-006 together with WP7 in this PR.
  3. Update the sources docs/qa-ci/source/chapters/03-graph-validation-rules.{de,en}.md and docs/qa-ci/lanes-source/chapters/{01-ci-overview,07-relation-checks}.{de,en}.md, then regenerate (python3 scripts/build_compendia.py --compendium qa-ci --web-and-tex).

Accept WP1 when the dead-scope tests prove no live checks were removed, all remaining graph issues are errors, the 593-landscape baseline still passes, and the related tests and five documentation checks pass. The integrated validator must additionally reject a broken non-Mathematics atomic route under WP6; unchanged baseline pass counts do not mean unchanged enforcement.

docs.title: WP2 – Bring all 21 roots to G17 (L3)
docs.text:
Subjects: Chinesisch, Englisch, Französisch, Griechisch, Musik, Spanisch. The overview root passes once Griechisch does.

  1. Read how the same repair was done and certified for Latin (commits 9f32bfb15d, 31c9dbc063) and the normative expansion rule in Graph Definition §3.1. Reuse its semantic materialization and reduction method; the earlier migration-certificate requirement is superseded. Do not extend the historical proof registry merely to satisfy G17.
  2. Per subject, in this order: a. Resolve the existing inherited and expanded atomic relation, accounting for every containment parent; reject unresolved references or other cycles. b. Replace each authored requires whose source or target is a cluster by the equivalent requirements between atomic goals. This includes the root-requires-"Warum"-child construct. c. Remove redundant authored edges until the auditor reports zero minimality findings. d. Check the complete current target graph and record the exact changed edge counts. A before/after closure comparison may support the mechanical transformation, but is not a historical migration certificate or a G17 acceptance prerequisite. Existing review-reuse evidence remains separate.
  3. One commit per subject.

Accept when (cd app && npx tsx scripts/auditTransitiveMinimality.ts --check) exits 0 with 21 pass lines, validate:graph, validate:view-filters, validate:composition-views and validate:learning-units pass, the existing backend test FirstMathPrerequisiteReductionTest remains green as a regression check for historical proof consumers, and the regenerated status shows CQR-001 pass for all 21 curricula with the ten protected maturities unchanged. That regression test is not a requirement for a new migration certificate or historical closure equality for these six subjects.

docs.title: WP3 – Direct G17 gate and local CI wiring (L4)
docs.text:
1. Add npm run check:transitive-minimality to the curriculum suite of run_ci.sh and to the graph-validation job in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
  2. Add npm run check:curriculum-maturity-floors to run_ci.sh next to the status regeneration.

Accept when both entry points fail on a deliberately introduced cluster requires in a subject without a floor (verify locally, then revert the probe).

Candidate result: CQR-001 satisfies H1–H3 for the complete catalog; H4 requires separately authorized main integration and terminal main CI.

docs.title: WP4 – Complete pin register and direct rule enforcement (L5)
docs.text:
Evolve the existing policy file and checker in place; do not add a second policy file.

  1. app/scripts/config/curriculum-maturity-floor-policy.json, schema version 2:
  2. floors: one entry for each of the 21 catalog curricula, at its current maturity (5 × M7, 5 × M6, 11 × M0).
  3. scopeFloors: one entry for each of the 12 QA scopes at M4, with an explicit compositionVisibilityRequired obligation: true for the eight established visibility scopes and false with recorded gap reasons for the four measured Sek II gaps. The policy must match the declared profile configuration and protect true obligations against removal.
  4. catalogInvariantRules: CQR-001, CQR-002, CQR-501.
  5. Drop knownPreBaselineRegressions and the hard-coded baselineDate comparison. Keep exceptions empty and fail-closed.
  6. app/scripts/checkCurriculumMaturityFloors.ts fails when:
  7. policy or status curriculum identities differ from the independently loaded canonical catalog, or scope identities differ from the shared route-profile inventory; duplicate identities are errors;
  8. a curriculum or scope is below its pin;
  9. a curriculum or scope is above its pin (the pin must be raised in the same change, so no gain is left unprotected);
  10. a catalog invariant rule is missing or not pass in any curriculum;
  11. any rule required by a curriculum or scope pin is absent, duplicated or not exactly pass, even when the reported maturity is unchanged;
  12. a protected curriculum or scope pin is removed or lowered against the Git base policy. CI supplies the PR base SHA or previous push SHA; local checking uses origin/main. Missing explicitly required base data fails.
  13. Export the check as a pure function and add a focused test with negative fixtures for each failure above, including policy/status deletion together, malformed or duplicate identities, every non-pass status, and a forged high maturity with failed required rules. Register it as an npm script and run it in both CI entry points.

Accept when the check passes on the unchanged status and each negative fixture fails with a message naming the curriculum or scope and the rule.

Result: every Class II rule satisfies H1 and H2 for all pinned curricula and scopes, with CQR-104 bounded to its eight pinned visibility scopes. CQR-002 and CQR-501 satisfy H1–H3 for the complete catalog. The main integration and green CI recorded in section 9 also establish H4 for this bounded enforcement.

docs.title: WP5 – Close promotion-chain leniencies and measure visibility gaps (L6, L7)
docs.text:
Each change must leave the ten protected maturities and the twelve scope maturities unchanged. If one would drop, that is a real finding: stop and report, do not lower a pin.

  1. CQR-104: measure the four scopes lacking compositionViewStage (canonical-math-sek2, canonical-physics-sek2, canonical-chemistry-sek2, canonical-biology-sek2). If all pass, make visibility mandatory for all twelve scopes. Otherwise pin the existing eight-scope coverage explicitly, require a result in every covered scope, and prevent coverage removal against the Git base. Keep the four measured gaps visible and the code PARTIAL; no floor exception or invented result.
  2. CQR-004 and CQR-005: require pass for the M1 to M2 step instead of blocking only on fail and warn.
  3. Set the catalog maturityTarget of CQR-104 and CQR-203 to the level they actually gate: M4 and M5, respectively. Scope derivation defaults to strict endpoint visibility. Only the explicit, validated four-profile gap configuration may omit that obligation; arbitrary absence of a result must still fail. Preserve the established maturity ladder and all pins.
  4. Bump the rules version and update docs/qa-ci/source/chapters/02-maturity-scopes-cqr.{de,en}.md.

Accept the bounded implementation when covered obligations cannot be omitted, the protected maturities remain unchanged, and the four unfulfilled visibility obligations are documented. Full WP5 completion requires their genuine current evidence and twelve passing results.

Result: directly enforced Class II obligations satisfy H3 within their pinned coverage. CQR-104 remains partial while any of the four gaps is unresolved.

Measured on 12 November: setting only SekII exposes missing terminals in 80/80 Mathematics, 68/68 Physics, 41/41 Chemistry and 3/3 Biology projection scopes. The existing compiled-jurisdiction mode still reports failures; two Chemistry endpoints have no compiled applicability, and five Biology projections have no applicable terminal. This is not a safe metadata-only configuration change. Any remediation must use authoritative applicability and assessment evidence, without defining the expected endpoint set merely as the endpoints already visible.

docs.title: WP6 – One route gate (L8)
docs.text:
1. Check whether the semantic validator in app/scripts/lib/hardLearningRouteValidation.ts can run over all 12 entries of routeProfiles. GVR-012 depends on a semantic-kind ledger that today exists for Mathematics; establish per scope whether an equivalent classification exists.
  2. Only if equivalent authoritative classification and negative-test semantics are established in all 12 scopes, derive the validate:graph profiles from routeProfiles and delete the separate list. Preserve the distinction between CQR-102 reachability and stronger semantic validation; a passing reachability result alone never licenses the stronger claim.
  3. If not: report the gap per scope, keep GVR-012 PARTIAL, and change no curriculum data in this package. Share the profile inventory where possible, while preserving the stronger semantic validator and directly enforcing CQR-102's distinct route-coverage obligation.

Review finding: CQR-102 currently checks reachability, while GVR-012 also checks semantic kinds, route ordering, ordinary intermediate goals, side prerequisites and Memory ordering. Mathematics profile selection and terminal expansion differ too. Positive data agreement cannot establish equivalence; negative fixtures must distinguish these obligations. Authoritative semantic ledgers currently exist for Mathematics and Physics, not all ten subjects.

Accept when validate:graph fails for a broken route in a non-Mathematics scope (probe, then revert).

docs.title: WP7 – Retire implied codes (L9; delivered with WP3)
docs.text:
1. Add a test showing that the G17 auditor reports a violation for a cluster that requires its direct child and for an atomic goal that requires a cluster.
  2. Delete GVR-006 and GVR-013 from validateGraph.ts and from the legend; point GD-C19 and GD-C22 to CQR-001. Retired codes are never reused.
  3. Preserve CQR-101 and CQR-103 in this implementation. Any future retirement needs an independent semantics argument and deliberate scope ladder change; equal results on today's data alone are insufficient.

docs.title: WP8 – Register and documentation
docs.text:
For the integrated candidate, before marking the PR ready for review:

  1. Update docs/concept/skill-graph/source/rules-and-gates.json in both languages: legend ampel and scope (with the covered domain and count), ampelSection counts and notes, milestone overview limits, and the enforcement text of every GD-* row that cites the gate. Upgrade a GD-* row only when every obligation in that row is gated; otherwise correct the text and keep the grade. Candidates to re-evaluate after WP3: GD-C11, C15, C16, U13.
  2. Update the expected distribution, only if GD group grades change, in scripts/doc_compendium/extensions/skill_graph.py, the affected prose in docs/concept/skill-graph/source/chapters/01-core.{de,en}.md and docs/qa-ci/source/, and the matching statements in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.
  3. Regenerate with npm --prefix app run docs:skill-graph:web and python3 scripts/build_compendia.py --compendium qa-ci --web-and-tex, then run the five documentation checks listed in CLAUDE.md.

docs.title: 10. Follow-up programme: clean Gymnasium (13 November 2026)
docs.text:
A rough roadmap. Each package names its goal, its first steps and its acceptance; the detail is worked out when the package starts.

Execution started on 13 November 2026 in the new goal for F1–F5, on branch feat/cqr-gvr-gymnasium-followup, based on freshly fetched origin/main 4aace519463880860c4c634eee2e801a48098df9. The owner's latest instruction requests one new branch and one new PR; the package-specific PR split below is superseded by separately reviewable commits in that integration PR. Astra Ultra audits the register and documentation; Sol 6.1 Ultra handles the live-inventory and semantic-route implementation. Evidence gaps remain findings, not permission to weaken gates or fabricate reviews.

docs.title: 10.1 Owner decision of 13 November 2026
docs.text:
• Work currently goes into Gymnasium only, and there the state must be clean.
  • The rule domain of the Graph Definition gates is the canonical Gymnasium catalog (curricula/DE/Gymnasium/canonical/, 21 roots). A GD-* row is graded against that domain. It is no longer held at PARTIAL only because landscapes outside Gymnasium are unchecked; the register names that boundary, as GD-C17 already does.
  • Landscapes outside Gymnasium receive no work in this programme: no repair, no retirement, no new gate. Their cleanup needs a separate later decision.
  • Target inside curricula/DE/Gymnasium/: no legacy construct, no bypass and no stale register statement remains.

Record this decision in AGENTS.md next to the 12 November decision in the first pull request that changes a grade (F2), and keep CLAUDE.md consistent.

docs.title: 10.2 Starting point
docs.text:
Measured in the working tree on 13 November 2026 unless a source is named.

Fact Value Code legend 22 HARD, 2 PARTIAL (GVR-012, CQR-104) of 24 GD-* register 4 HARD, 58 PARTIAL, 55 OPEN, 28 OPT/DOC; part C: 3, 22, 11 Loaded landscape files 593: 21 canonical, 45 under curricula/DE/Gymnasium/input/BY/gymnasium/, 527 outside Gymnasium Root requires its own "Warum" child 0 canonical, 45 of the 45 Bavarian input graphs, 519 outside Gymnasium Semantic-kind ledgers covering every current goal, all authoritative Mathematik, Physik (quality/release-model/), Biologie, Chemie (quality/goal-book-publication/) Wirtschaftswissenschaften ledger Only inside versioned rollout packages; the latest (…-v18) lacks 24 of 702 current goals Ledgers for Deutsch, Geschichte, Informatik, Latein, Politik und Wirtschaft None found CQR-104 gaps Sek II scopes of Mathematics (80 findings), Physics (68), Chemistry (41), Biology (3); section 7, WP5, not re-measured

docs.text: Order: F1, F2, F3, F4, F5. F2 and F3 are independent of each other; F4 and F5 are independent of both. F4 precedes F5 because its evidence largely exists.

docs.title: F1 – Documentation hygiene
docs.text:
docs/concept/skill-graph/source/README.md still says 26 repository gates instead of 24. Rebuild the PDFs (npm --prefix app run docs:skill-graph:full) and compare the published matrix page and PDF with the register.

Accept when the five documentation checks pass and web, PDF and source agree.

docs.title: F2 – Regrade the GD-* rows against the declared domain
docs.text:
Standard: the same as for the legend (section 3). A row becomes HARD only when every obligation it states is gated fail-closed in the canonical Gymnasium catalog. Otherwise correct the text, keep the grade and name the remaining gap. No row is upgraded on wording alone: each upgrade cites its gate, the covered count and an existing negative test or probe.

Group Rows Work Limited only by the catalog boundary GD-C11, C15, C16, C19, U13 State the domain as in GD-C17. Check whether the route clause in C11 and C16 is a separate obligation of the rule; if so it follows F4. Justified by floors or protected inventories GD-C04, C08, X26, X29, X45, X46 Re-evaluate against the complete pin register (21 curricula, 12 scopes). A rule that binds from M6 or M7 is graded like its legend code, with the pinned count. A claim that no gate checks stays a named residual. Waiting for F4 or F5 GD-C21, C22, A18 Keep PARTIAL. Verify the A18 statement that CQR-104 applies to Economics only; the legend says eight scopes. OPEN rows 55, about 48 of them runtime or concept obligations Out of scope (10.4). Do not regrade.

Then update the expected distribution in scripts/doc_compendium/extensions/skill_graph.py, the ampelSection counts, the affected chapter prose and the statements in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; regenerate (docs:skill-graph:web, QA compendium) and run the five documentation checks.

Accept when the rendered matrix shows the new grades and every changed row names gate, domain and count.

docs.title: F3 – Clean the Gymnasium remainder
docs.text:
The 45 files under curricula/DE/Gymnasium/input/BY/gymnasium/ are retained Bavarian source graphs (4 to 893 goals). loadGraphValidationLandscapes loads them as live landscapes. None is a manifest root; the IDs of 21 appear in mapping/ and provenance/, those of 5 in canonical/.

  1. Establish their role: which runtime, tooling and evidence consumers read them as graphs (validator inventory, backend LandscapeService, mapping, provenance, deck tooling).
  2. Preferred outcome: they are retained source material, as the input README.md already says, not live graphs. Take them out of the live landscape inventories with their bytes unchanged.
  3. Only if a consumer needs them as live graphs: normalise requires as in WP2 and add them to the G17 domain. Check hash and provenance bindings first; a frozen snapshot is not rewritten.
  4. If neither is possible without breaking evidence, stop and report.

Accept when a test fails for any live graph under curricula/DE/Gymnasium/ that is outside the gated set, and the register states the domain accordingly.

docs.title: F4 – GVR-012 beyond Mathematics
docs.text:
Target: the seven scopes of the five M7 subjects (canonical-math-sek1, -math-sek2, -physics-sek1, -physics-sek2, -biology-sek2, -chemistry-sek2, -economics-crossstage).

Product Owner decision, 13 November 2026: GVR-012 shall become mandatory from subject maturity M7. This is the binding target, with activation deferred until the current M7 evidence gaps are closed. It supersedes the earlier twelve-scope completion condition in WP6: the required domain is every registered QA scope of a subject obligated to meet M7, currently these seven scopes. The full inventory still contains twelve scopes; the other five belong to M6 subjects and enter the mandatory domain when their subjects advance to M7.

  1. Physics probe: run the semantic validator (app/scripts/lib/hardLearningRouteValidation.ts) on both Physics scopes with the existing ledger. Add negative fixtures for each obligation that distinguishes GVR-012 from CQR-102 (semantic kinds, route ordering, intermediate goals, side prerequisites, Memory ordering).
  2. Biology and Chemistry: confirm that the ledgers under goal-book-publication/ follow the same contract and are valid input for route validation, then repeat step 1.
  3. Wirtschaftswissenschaften: there is no current ledger. Classifying the 24 missing goals needs reviewed evidence; report the gap, do not classify in bulk.
  4. Derive the validate:graph profiles from the shared scope inventory for every scope with a current authoritative ledger and delete the separate Mathematics list. The legend states the covered count.

A route that fails the semantic validator is a curriculum finding: report it per scope and repair it only with evidence. Never weaken the validator or change a classification to pass. The five M6 scopes have no classification; that work belongs to their M7 path and is not part of this programme.

GVR-012 remains PARTIAL: four of the seven current M7 scopes are directly required and pass. The remaining three need current classification and route evidence before the complete M7 obligation can be activated. A later HARD grade requires fail-closed enforcement across the complete M7 domain, including its expansion on future promotions, with meaningful negative tests. That is a prerequisite for regrading GVR-012, not an automatic upgrade of broader GD-C21, GD-C22 or GD-A18 obligations. Do not activate the incomplete obligation now, lower existing floors, remove required scopes, or treat this decision as passing evidence. The current four required scopes and every existing pin remain unchanged and protected against removal or reduction even through a later status change.

The semantic route audit remains a complete twelve-scope diagnostic. Its nonzero exit for route findings or unavailable ledgers, including those of M6 subjects, is not an M7 promotion check. 4/12 continues to describe current inventory coverage; 4/7 describes coverage of today's normative M7 domain.

docs.title: F5 – CQR-104 from eight to twelve scopes
docs.text:
1. Biology first (smallest gap). Find the cause before fixing anything: missing applicability data, missing view placement, or no assessment at that level.
  2. After Biology, decide whether one mechanism serves all four subjects and note it here before continuing.
  3. Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics: one reviewable commit per subject. Set compositionVisibilityRequired to true for a scope in the pull request that makes it pass.

The expected endpoint set comes from authoritative applicability and assessment evidence (state, Sek II course level), never from what is already visible. No pin is lowered. A gap that cannot be evidenced stays documented and the code stays PARTIAL.

After twelve passing scopes: grade CQR-104 HARD and re-evaluate the rows that waited for it. This does not automatically make GD-C22 or A18 hard: C22 additionally needs the semantic route obligation; A18 includes assessment coverage/path and runtime obligations beyond endpoint visibility.

docs.title: 10.4 Out of scope
docs.text:

  • The OPEN rows that state runtime or concept obligations. They need runtime conformance tests, a separate programme; no CQR or GVR work reaches them.
  • The frozen prerequisite-reduction registry (contract V9) and its parent.
