docs.title: 6. Duale Curriculum-Release-Verträge
docs.text: DPK-003 legt den Fail-Closed-Semantikvertrag für ein gekoppeltes Paar aus SkillPilot-JSON-Laufzeitpaket und Core-first-FWU-Ontologiepaket fest, ohne damit bereits ein Produktivpaket zu veröffentlichen.

docs.title: 6.1. Verbindliche Vertragsinvarianten
docs.text:
• Lückenlose Feld-Registry: Jedes Feld des Release-Modells muss exakt einem versionierten Registry-Eintrag entsprechen (Skalare, geordnete Listen, Mengen, Maps, Binärreferenzen, generierte nicht-semantische Felder). Unbekannte Felder blockieren das Ontologie-Release.
  • Explizite nullbasierte Ordnung in RDF: Lernziele, direkte contains- und requires-Kanten, Ressourcenlinks, View-Kinder, Karten und Bewertungsschritte sind geordnet. RDF speichert eindeutige, lückenlose nullbasierte Positionen, da ungeordnete Core-Relationen die Autorenreihenfolge nicht rekonstruieren können.
  • Strikte Wertunterscheidung & Verbot breiter JSON-Container: Fehlend, null, leer und Standardwert bleiben getrennt, sofern ein einzelner Registry-Eintrag nichts anderes festlegt. Bekannte curriculare Konzepte nutzen den FWU-Core; SkillPilot-Vokabular dient nur der Laufzeitsemantik und exakten Rückübersetzung. Kanonische JSON-Literale erfordern eine feldspezifische Core-Lücke, Granularität und Byte-Obergrenze; paket- oder landschaftsweite JSON-Träger sind verboten.
  • Pfadneutrale Binäridentität: Binärressourcen gehen über stabile Ressourcen-ID, kanonische öffentliche Referenz, MIME-Typ, Byte-Länge und SHA-256 in den gemeinsamen Index ein; variantenspezifische ZIP-Pfade ändern contentDigest nicht.
  • Äquivalenzbericht & Signaturprojektion: Ein bestandener Äquivalenzbericht bindet beide finalen ZIPs und Manifeste, Verträge, FWU-Core-IRI, Toolchain, Feldabdeckung, Rollen-Digests, Graph-/View-/Karten-/Asset-Vergleiche, isolierte Rückübersetzung, Validierung beider JSON-Pakete, hermetische Consumer-Läufe und Reproduzierbarkeit. Der externe Release-Index entfernt vor dem kanonischen Hashing den Signaturblock (keine Selbstreferenz); der DPK-003-Validator weist jeden verified- oder stable-Anspruch ab, bis DPK-011 Signatur-, Identitäts- und Provenienzprüfungen ausführt (staging darf unsigniert bleiben).

docs.title: 6.2. Ausführbares Gate und Abgrenzung
docs.text:
Ausführung vom Repository-Root (Teil der optionalen Ontologie-Lane in ./run_ci.sh owl, ./run_ci.sh full und .github/workflows/owl-ci.yml; erfordert jsonschema==4.26.0):

python3 -B scripts/validate_curriculum_dual_release_contracts.py

Der Validator weist doppelte JSON-Schlüssel, nicht-endliche Zahlen, ungültiges Unicode und RDF/XML-unsichere Steuerzeichen ab, prüft alle Schemata und Positiv-Fixtures, berechnet logische/binäre Records sowie den Gesamt-contentDigest neu und führt eine Mutationsmatrix aus (verlorene Ordnung, mehrdeutige Pfade, verwischte missing/null-Semantik, unzulässige JSON-Träger, gefälschte Digests, substituierte Berichte, nicht-isolierte Rekonstruktion, unbestätigte stable-Promotion).

Synthetische Vertrags-Fixtures sind keine Curriculum-Evidenz

Die positiven Release- und Äquivalenzdateien unter contracts/curriculum-package/v1/fixtures/dual-release/valid/ enthalten synthetische Hashes und Zähler ausschließlich zum Vertragstest und dürfen niemals als Curriculum-Nachweis veröffentlicht werden.

docs.title: 6. Dual Curriculum Release Contracts
docs.text: DPK-003 defines the fail-closed semantic contract pairing a SkillPilot JSON runtime package with a Core-first FWU ontology package, without by itself publishing either production artifact.

docs.title: 6.1. Binding Contract Invariants
docs.text:
• Total field-registry coverage: Every release-model field must match exactly one versioned registry entry (scalars, ordered lists, sets, maps, binary references, generated non-semantic fields). Unknown fields block the ontology release.
  • Explicit zero-based ordering in RDF: Goals, authored direct contains and requires edges, resource links, view children, cards, and scoring steps are ordered. RDF carries unique, contiguous zero-based positions because unordered Core relations cannot reconstruct authored order.
  • Strict value distinction & ban on broad JSON carriers: Missing, null, empty, and default values remain distinct unless a specific registry entry states otherwise. Known curricular concepts use the FWU Core; SkillPilot vocabulary is restricted to runtime semantics and exact reverse reconstruction. Any canonical JSON literal requires a field-specific Core gap, granularity, and byte cap; package- or landscape-wide JSON carriers are forbidden.
  • Path-neutral binary identity: Binary resources enter the shared index via stable resource identity, canonical public reference, MIME type, byte length, and SHA-256; variant-specific ZIP paths never alter contentDigest.
  • Equivalence report & signing projection: A passing equivalence report binds both final ZIPs and inner manifests, trusted contracts, FWU Core IRI, toolchain, field coverage, role digests, graph/view/card/asset comparisons, isolated reverse compilation, validation of original and reconstructed JSON packages, hermetic consumer runs, and reproducibility. The external release index strips the signature block before canonical hashing (avoiding self-reference), and the DPK-003 validator rejects every verified or stable claim until DPK-011 performs cryptographic signature, identity, and provenance checks (staging may remain explicitly unsigned).

docs.title: 6.2. Executable Gate and Boundary
docs.text:
Run from the repository root (part of the optional ontology lane in ./run_ci.sh owl, ./run_ci.sh full, and .github/workflows/owl-ci.yml; requires jsonschema==4.26.0):

python3 -B scripts/validate_curriculum_dual_release_contracts.py

The validator rejects duplicate JSON keys, non-finite numbers, invalid Unicode, and RDF/XML-unsafe control characters, validates all schemas and positive fixtures, recomputes logical/binary records and the aggregate contentDigest, and runs a mutation matrix covering lost ordering, ambiguous paths, blurred missing/null semantics, broad JSON carriers, forged digests, substituted reports, non-isolated reconstruction, and unverified stable promotion.

Synthetic contract fixtures are never curriculum evidence

Positive release and equivalence files under contracts/curriculum-package/v1/fixtures/dual-release/valid/ carry synthetic hashes and counts strictly for contract testing and must never be published as curriculum evidence.

docs.title: 6. SkillPilot-Qualitätssicherung: Das Vier-Stufen-Champion-Modell
docs.text:
Zukunftsgerichteter Ausbauplan

Zielbild für den stufenweisen Ausbau der Curriculum-QS zwischen algorithmischer CI, KI-Agenten und menschlicher Praxiserprobung. Für die heute produktiv ausgewiesenen Reifegrade und Erprobungsbadges gilt verbindlich 1 (Level 1a und Level 2 sind heute produktive Anker; Level 1b und Level 1c beschreiben geplante Ausbaustufen).

docs.title: 6.1. Einordnung und die vier QS-Stufen
docs.text:
Damit Fachexpertinnen und -experten beim Übergang von KI-extrahierten Rohgraphen zu schulreifen Skill-Landschaften nicht mit JSON-Formalia oder DAG-Mathematik überlastet werden, gliedert das Zielmodell das frühere Level 1 in drei technische/agentische Vorstufen (1a, 1b, 1c) vor dem menschlichen Praxissiegel (Level 2):

Stufe Heutiger Stand Prüffokus und typische Aufgaben Level 1a: CI-Pipeline Produktiv aktiv Algorithmische Strukturintegrität ohne Inhaltsdeutung: Zyklenfreiheit in contains/requires, Schema- und ID-Prüfungen, gültige View-Projektionen (3). Level 1b: Statischer KI-Agent Zukunftsgerichtet Statische didaktisch-formale Leitplanken ohne Laufzeitsimulation: Routenabdeckung von Motivation bis Autonomie, saubere Trennung von sourceRef und Didaktikmaterial, formale Vollständigkeit von Prüfungs- und Bewertungsschemata. Level 1c: Dynamischer KI-Agent Zukunftsgerichtet Simulierte Lernendendurchläufe unter Laufzeitbedingungen: Frontier- und Filterverhalten, Sackgassen/verdeckte Blocker, Prüfungssimulation mit unvollständigen/falschen Antworten sowie SRS-Memorize-Abläufe. Level 2: Menschlicher Champion Produktiv aktiv Reale didaktische Praxiserprobung in WebGUI oder KI-Lerncoach: Tonalität, Altersangemessenheit, Motivation, fachliche Passung und UX mit Rückmeldung über Issues/PRs bis zum Status Menschlich erprobt (5).

docs.title: 6.2. Zusammenspiel und Governance
docs.text:
Das Modell folgt einer klaren Mensch-Agenten-Arbeitsteilung:

  1. Level 1a blockiert mathematisch oder technisch defekte Graphen frühzeitig in der CI.
  2. Level 1b und Level 1c strukturieren künftig formale und simulierte Befunde automatisiert vor.
  3. Level 2 beurteilt die tatsächliche Unterrichts- und Lernqualität am echten Curriculum.
  4. Befunde fließen transparent in GitHub Issues und Pull Requests zurück.
  5. Menschliche Maintainer entscheiden Konfliktfälle und wahren die fachdidaktische Richtung.

docs.title: 6. SkillPilot Quality Assurance: The Four-Level Champion Model
docs.text:
Forward-looking expansion roadmap

Target architecture for scaling curriculum QA across algorithmic CI, AI agents, and human practice reviews. Currently shipped public maturity and trial badges are governed strictly by 1 (Level 1a and Level 2 are active anchors today, whereas Level 1b and Level 1c represent planned expansion stages).

docs.title: 6.1. Positioning and the Four QA Levels
docs.text:
To scale from AI-derived raw graphs to classroom-ready skill landscapes without burdening domain educators with JSON schemas or DAG invariants, this roadmap unfolds the former Level 1 into three automated/agentic stages (1a, 1b, 1c) ahead of the human practice certificate (Level 2):

Level Current status Inspection focus and representative checks Level 1a: CI pipeline Active today Content-agnostic algorithmic integrity: acyclicity of contains/requires, schema and ID checks, valid projected learner views (3). Level 1b: Static AI agent Forward-looking Static didactic and formal guardrails without runtime simulation: route coverage from motivation to autonomy, clean separation of sourceRef and didactic assets, formal completeness of exam and rubric schemas. Level 1c: Dynamic AI agent Forward-looking Simulated learner walkthroughs under live runtime rules: frontier and filter behavior, dead ends or hidden blockers, exam simulations with incomplete/wrong answers, and SRS Memorize mechanics. Level 2: Human Champion Active today Authentic pedagogical evaluation in the WebGUI or AI coach: tone, age fit, motivation, subject alignment, and UX — filing issues/PRs toward Human-tested (5).

docs.title: 6.2. Human-Agent Workflow and Governance
docs.text:
The cascade operates as structured human-agent teamwork:

  1. Level 1a blocks mathematically or structurally broken graphs automatically in CI.
  2. Level 1b and Level 1c are designed to pre-triage static and simulated findings at scale.
  3. Level 2 evaluates real pedagogical quality in authentic learning contexts.
  4. Findings are tracked and resolved transparently via GitHub issues and pull requests.
  5. Human maintainers arbitrate edge cases and safeguard pedagogical intent.

docs.title: Goal feedback: production-to-Codex intake
docs.text: Status: implemented with a source-level default-off; production activation is an explicit operator state Scope: public learning-goal and general feedback, production custody transfer, and local critical triage

docs.title: Trust and custody model
docs.text:
Feedback is written to the production PostgreSQL inbox. Codex runs in a separate development environment and never receives production database or shell access.

public form -> production inbox -> digest-bound HTTPS batch
            -> verified local inbox -> If-Match DELETE on production
            -> candidate-only critical review

The production operations API accepts only its dedicated bearer token. The local client pins that credential to https://skillpilot.com; only HTTP loopback origins are accepted by tests. Feedback prose is external untrusted input. For goal feedback, the exact server-derived publication snapshot is stored separately from that prose. General feedback has the closed context {"scope":"general"}; it carries no automatic learner, session, goal or book identifier and no fabricated publication snapshot.

docs.title: Submission variants
docs.text:
Both variants use the existing public POST /api/public/goal-feedback/v1/submissions and the wrapper {clientSubmissionId, website, envelope}. The form exposes one free-text field, feedback.observation, bounded to 4,000 characters. A goal submission retains the complete immutable V2 publication context and sets the existing category to other; historical V2 submissions with other categories and optional fields remain readable. General submissions use the new contracts/goal-evidence/v3/goal-public-feedback.schema.json, schemaVersion: 3, context: {scope: "general"}, and feedback: {observation: "…"}. Unknown fields, mixed scopes, missing acknowledgements and extra identities are rejected. General feedback needs no context lookup or authenticated learner session.

The export payload remains version 1. General records have bindingStatus: "general"; their serverTrustedContext contains exactly schemaVersion: 1, the general context and submissionEndpoint, with no goal field. The local intake validates V2 and V3 independently and reports general records as general/not_applicable for publication comparison. A general-only inbox needs no local goal-book index. Mixed batches preserve each goal record's original publication binding. Canonical envelope and payload digests, durable local verification before the digest-bound DELETE, capacity, rate limits and retention apply to both variants unchanged. The existing deterministic critical-review instruction artifact remains unchanged so retained local inboxes stay verifiable.

docs.title: Production activation gate
docs.text:
The checked-in default is disabled. A production operator must complete all of the following before enabling intake:

  1. Publish the bilingual, provider-neutral feedback-specific privacy details on /lernziel-feedback#feedback-datenschutz. They stay collapsed by default and cover purpose, consent, the processed data, technically assisted review, the 30-day pending threshold, retention after review begins, backup limits, and statutory requests without exposing internal service or storage names. Every new envelope binds the current notice version 2026-11-13.1 and the displayed de|en locale. This version covers both general feedback and the optional published-goal context. Both explicit acknowledgements remain required. The V2 schema continues to recognize the earlier 2026-08-30.1 and 2026-08-31.1 versions so retained historical envelopes remain verifiable. General V3 feedback requires the new notice version. During the cache-transition window the live endpoint accepts all three issued versions for V2 and preserves the version actually submitted; new forms emit only 2026-11-13.1. Retiring an older accepted version requires a separate, cache-aware decision. The frozen general Coach privacy text is not silently broadened.
  2. Generate a distinct, high-entropy token of at least 32 characters. It must never equal SKILLPILOT_AI_API_KEY, an OAuth secret, or a database password.
  3. Configure SKILLPILOT_GOAL_FEEDBACK_OPERATOR_TOKEN in production and in the authorized local secret store.
  4. Deliberately set SKILLPILOT_GOAL_FEEDBACK_ENABLED=true in production.
  5. Review the bounded row/byte capacity and public rate-limit settings for the deployed proxy topology. The intake filter unwraps Spring forwarding wrappers and never uses X-Forwarded-For. It accepts exactly one valid X-Real-IP only when the raw socket peer is loopback; otherwise it falls back to the raw peer's shared bucket. The first-party Nginx vhost binds the backend to loopback and replaces X-Real-IP with $remote_addr, so a caller cannot manufacture per-address buckets even while the legacy vhost still appends X-Forwarded-For. Missing, duplicate, chained, or malformed X-Real-IP values fail closed to the shared proxy bucket. Context lookup and validated submission use separate bounded windows; rejected origins, media types, and oversized POST bodies do not consume the submission window.
  6. Verify the exact current publication snapshot and complete a live canary submission, pull, local validation, and deletion-receipt check.

The checked-in configuration never activates the channel itself. Production activation is a separate, reviewed operator operation with fail-closed source/file shape checks, recovery bytes readable only by the service owner, readiness and real-context probes, and a dedicated operator credential that is never printed. The preferred root helper additionally installs a root-owned backup timer and defense-in-depth forwarding-header cleanup. If interactive root access is unavailable, the service owner may use an external Spring configuration outside Git only after the raw-peer/X-Real-IP regression is deployed, the live database credential has been rotated, and the application backup entrypoint has been rebound to the content-excluding repository script.

docs.title: Maximum pending retention and backup boundary
docs.text:
Content that has not been acknowledged through the digest-bound DELETE uses the fixed maximum age P30D. A conflicting property or environment value fails startup because it would contradict the published notice. Cleanup runs before public submission and every operator export operation, and a bounded background job starts after 60 seconds and then runs at an immutable daily cadence. The scheduler drains the bounded queue through a non-transactional coordinator; each bounded cleanup owns its independent transaction before a request-scoped submission/export transaction begins. This avoids nested-transaction connection pool exhaustion. During normal service operation, the daily cadence makes 31 days the upper bound; an intake/export request usually removes expired content earlier, and after a service interruption the initial cleanup begins within 60 seconds.

Unbound expired submissions are removed in full. An OPEN export is indivisible: as soon as its own age or any bound submission reaches the cutoff, all of its content is removed and the batch becomes a content-free EXPIRED tombstone. EXPIRED explicitly does not claim that a local copy was verified; only a digest-confirmed operator DELETE creates the DELETED receipt. Capacity is checked and updated under the same singleton database lock used by intake and export.

The application-level SQL backup script excludes data from goal_feedback_submission, goal_feedback_export_batch, and the derived goal_feedback_inbox_capacity singleton, so it does not deliberately duplicate feedback prose or an OPEN batch payload. It appends a deterministic empty capacity singleton for a consistent restore and publishes a dump only after the complete temporary file succeeds. Its remaining owner-only dumps older than the configured period (30 days by default) are removed on each successful application-level backup run. Logical live-row deletion cannot rewrite PostgreSQL WAL or any independently managed infrastructure backup; those leave custody only through the respective infrastructure rotation and must not be treated as active inbox records.

docs.title: Pull and delete
docs.text:
Run from the repository without putting the token on the command line:

export SKILLPILOT_GOAL_FEEDBACK_OPERATOR_TOKEN='<from the authorized local secret store>'
npm --prefix app run feedback:pull
unset SKILLPILOT_GOAL_FEEDBACK_OPERATOR_TOKEN

The default origin is exactly https://skillpilot.com; the default local root is the ignored tmp/goal-feedback/inbox/. A successful command:

  1. obtains the oldest still-open batch or creates one from bounded unbound submissions;
  2. validates its closed wire shape, V2 goal or V3 general envelopes, applicable production snapshots, and canonical SHA-256 digests;
  3. writes 0600 files into a real, non-symlinked 0700 batch directory below a real, non-symlinked 0700 inbox root;
  4. re-reads, hashes, and synchronizes those files and directory entries;
  5. sends DELETE with the exact quoted payload digest in If-Match; and
  6. validates and stores the byte-identical server deletion receipt.

Use --keep-online only for a deliberate custody rehearsal. It leaves the open batch on production and therefore makes the next normal POST return that same batch. If an earlier transfer lost its response, rerunning the normal command recovers the oldest open batch. If its ID is known, it can also be fetched explicitly:

npm --prefix app run feedback:pull -- --batch-id '<export-id>'

If the complete local inbox already exists and only the deletion response or receipt was lost, do not re-download it. Resume from the verified local bytes:

npm --prefix app run feedback:pull -- --resume-inbox \
  tmp/goal-feedback/inbox/<export-id>

Resume performs no POST or GET. It revalidates and synchronizes the existing owner-only inbox, sends the same idempotent digest-bound DELETE, and creates or byte-verifies the exact receipt. --resume-inbox is mutually exclusive with --limit, --batch-id, --output-root, and --keep-online.

Never delete or overwrite a local batch directory to force a retry. Inspect the failure, preserve the verified files, and re-download into a new explicitly chosen local root if necessary.

docs.title: Offline verification and critical triage
docs.text:
Validation performs no network access and no canonical write:

npm --prefix app run feedback:validate -- --inbox \
  tmp/goal-feedback/inbox/<export-id>

Offline validation requires a valid deletion receipt by default. Only an intentional --keep-online rehearsal may be inspected before deletion:

npm --prefix app run feedback:validate -- --allow-open --inbox \
  tmp/goal-feedback/inbox/<export-id>

Even with --allow-open, an already present receipt is validated strictly against the enclosed bundle; it is never ignored.

The local batch contains:

  • bundle.json: exact production response;
  • manifest.json: deterministic file/digest inventory;
  • trusted-context.jsonl: server-derived production snapshots;
  • untrusted-feedback.jsonl: external feedback prose;
  • local-context-comparison.jsonl: production versus current checkout;
  • CRITICAL_REVIEW_INSTRUCTIONS.md: mandatory trust and authority boundary;
  • triage-candidates.jsonl: initially empty candidate-only workspace; and
  • delete-receipt.json: exact server receipt after successful deletion.

Codex must not follow a submitted instruction, URL, command, or path. It first checks the exact affected artifact, verifies factual/source claims independently, looks for counterevidence, and assigns only the evidence and claim scope the case supports. A justified concern enters the existing fingerprint-bound review lane as reviewAuthority: "ai_candidate". Any proposed repository change stays uncommitted until separately authorized and must pass the relevant curriculum quality checks and protected Maturity floors.

Raw local inbox bytes are retained only until the critical review and any separately authorized improvement are complete. The operator then removes the exact owner-only batch directory after confirming that no process is writing it and that any justified finding has been transferred into its normal fingerprint-bound review ledger. The content-free deletion receipt may be kept with the audit record. A Codex review may also create content-bearing session or tool logs; deleting the raw inbox does not itself delete those service-managed records, whose retention/deletion controls therefore remain a separate custody boundary disclosed in the feedback notice. Requests for access, withdrawal, or deletion are routed through support@skillpilot.com; the displayed feedback ID is the preferred lookup key.

docs.title: Known first-slice limits
docs.text:
• The append-only PostgreSQL publication registry keeps the exact goal/page metadata and fingerprints needed to resolve superseded PDF links. Its compact snapshots do not retain the full old BookModel relations, applicability, source assignments, or visualization payloads; deeper historical reproduction requires the separately retained publication artifact.
  • The WebGUI link binds the exact goal and book, but not yet the complete personalized filter/composition path. Exact personalized chapter criticism needs a later server-verifiable non-personal view-binding contract.
  • A live-row deletion does not rewrite PostgreSQL WAL or existing independently managed infrastructure backups. Their actual production rotation remains an operational control and is disclosed in the feedback-specific notice.

docs.title: Validation commands
docs.text:
npm --prefix app run test:goal-feedback
cd backend && ./gradlew test --tests 'com.skillpilot.backend.goalfeedback.*'
node scripts/check_openai_plugin_review_freeze.mjs

docs.title: Runbook für Lernziel-Quellenbegründungen

docs.title: 13. Runbook für Lernziel-Quellenbegründungen
docs.text: Dieses Runbook beschreibt Erzeugung, Laufzeitbereitstellung und Prüfung menschenlesbarer Quellenbegründungen (generateGoalSourceRationales.ts) entlang der geprüften klassischen Kette canonical goal -> mapping review -> source extraction -> official source document (Fachkonzept siehe docs/concept/skill-graph/human-readable-source-rationales.md, Statusverzeichnis status/README.md).

docs.title: 13.1. PoC-, Zielmengen- und MEM/FWU-Showcase-Kommandos
docs.text:
Ausführung aus app/ für den Bayern-Mathematik-PoC (goal-source-rationales-poc.md + .json), benutzerdefinierte Zielmengen und die Bayern-LehrplanPLUS-Showcases mit Live-MEM/FWU-Abgleich (:plain blendet Ziel-UUIDs zugunsten des SkillPilot-Pfads aus und ergänzt konkrete SPARQL-Abfragen):

cd app
npm run quality:goal-source-rationales:poc
npx tsx scripts/generateGoalSourceRationales.ts \
  --jurisdiction=DE-BY --goals=<goal-id>,<another-goal-id>
npm run quality:goal-source-rationales:mem-examples
npm run quality:goal-source-rationales:mem-examples:plain

Wichtige CLI-Optionen: --landscape=<path>, --mapping-root=<path>, --output-json=<path>, --output-md=<path>, --no-md, --goals=source-backed | source-backed-relevant-leaves | all-relevant-leaves, --jurisdiction=all, --include-mem, --mem-config=<path> und --mem-replay=<path>.

--mem-replay=<path> verwendet statt einer Abfrage des Endpunkts die MEM-Erwartungstexte, die in den konsistenten Wegen eines früheren Berichts dieses Generators festgehalten sind, und wendet denselben Abgleich auf die aktuellen klassischen Wege an. Ein Weg, der nicht mehr passt, wird mem_sparql_review_needed; durch eine Wiedergabe wird nichts neu konsistent. Die Option dient, mit dem eingecheckten Bericht als Eingabe, für den Fall, dass sich nur kanonische Zieltexte geändert haben und der Endpunkt nicht ausgewertet werden kann. Seit November 2026 verbindet der Endpunkt Pläne mit ihren Teilen und Kompetenzen über lp:LP_0000565 („hat direkten Teil“) statt über bfo:BFO_0000051 und liefert die bayerischen Ressourcen unter https://w3id.org/lehrplan/resource/by/. Die Abfrage folgt seit dem 14. November 2026 lp:LP_0000565+; der Live-Lauf dieses Tages hat alle 234 bisher konsistenten Wege mit den neuen IRIs bestätigt und 26 weitere gefunden. Das MEM-Konsistenzaudit (quality:mem-sparql-consistency) scheitert weiterhin an seinen Abfragen zur Verfügbarkeit von Ländern und Plänen (HTTP 500, transitives rdfs:subClassOf* über den ganzen Bestand); sein eingecheckter Bericht stammt vom Juni 2026.

docs.title: 13.2. Öffentlicher Laufzeitindex (Repository- vs. Paketmodus) & Deployment-Smoke
docs.text:
• Repository-Modus: Der Explorer lädt bei Bedarf genau zwei Kompatibilitätsindizes außerhalb von JS-Bundle und Service-Worker-Precache nach: /data/goal-source-rationales-math-public.json (bevorzugt DE-BY für sichtbaren MEM/FWU-Abgleich) und /data/goal-source-rationales-physics-public.json (die generische Deck-Route darf sie nicht abfangen).
  • Paketmodus: /data/** ist gesperrt; das UI ermittelt die Bindungen über Catalog API 1.2 (/api/ui/curriculum-catalog) und lädt Einzelziele generationsgebunden über /api/ui/curriculum-source-evidence/packages/{packageId}/{packageVersion}/goals/{goalId} ohne Repository-/Classpath-Fallback.

Erzeugung, Build-Artefaktprüfung und Live-Deployment-Smoke (automatisch im Deploy-Skript nach Service-Neustart ausgeführt; erkennt anhand von /api/ui/curriculum-catalog 404 vs. 1.2 den aktiven Modus):

cd app
npm run quality:goal-source-rationales:public
npm run check:goal-source-rationales:math-public
npm run check:goal-source-rationales:build-artifact
npm run smoke:goal-source-rationales:deployment
npm run smoke:goal-source-rationales:deployment -- --base-url=http://127.0.0.1:8080
cd ..
SKILLPILOT_BASE_URL=https://staging.example.org \
  ./deploy_skillpilot.sh --coach-variant openai-mcp

docs.title: 13.3. Review-Checkliste und Folge-Issues
docs.text:
Je gerendertem Ziel sind fünf Punkte zu prüfen:

  1. sourceRationaleStatus: classic_source_reviewed (regulär zulässig), classic_source_partial (nur mit nachvollziehbarer Teil-Begründung) oder classic_source_gap (erfordert nicht-blockierendes Folge-Issue).
  2. Originalquelle finden: Offizielle URL oder archivierter Quellpfad samt konkretem Such-/Abschnittshinweis vorhanden.
  3. Extrahierter Quellenbeleg: Dokumentmetadaten aufgelöst, sourceGoalId und Referenz konsistent, Markdown-Auszug knapp gehalten (Volltext nur im JSON).
  4. Begründung des SkillPilot-Ziels: Verständliche Zuordnungsbegründung ohne Übertreibung von partial-, split- oder aggregate-Mappings.
  5. MEM/FWU-SPARQL-Route: mem_sparql_unavailable im klassischen PoC bzw. mem_sparql_consistent im Bayern-Showcase (stets sekundäre Route, solange kein Scope als Primärquelle freigegeben ist; bei Widersprüchen oder fehlenden Metadaten manuelles Review-Issue anlegen).

docs.title: 13.1. PoC, Custom Goal Sets, and MEM/FWU Showcase Commands
docs.text:
Run from app/ for the Bavaria Mathematics PoC (goal-source-rationales-poc.md + .json), custom goal selections, and the Bavaria LehrplanPLUS live MEM/FWU showcases (:plain replaces UUIDs with readable SkillPilot paths and embeds concrete SPARQL queries):

cd app
npm run quality:goal-source-rationales:poc
npx tsx scripts/generateGoalSourceRationales.ts \
  --jurisdiction=DE-BY --goals=<goal-id>,<another-goal-id>
npm run quality:goal-source-rationales:mem-examples
npm run quality:goal-source-rationales:mem-examples:plain

Key CLI flags: --landscape=<path>, --mapping-root=<path>, --output-json=<path>, --output-md=<path>, --no-md, --goals=source-backed | source-backed-relevant-leaves | all-relevant-leaves, --jurisdiction=all, --include-mem, --mem-config=<path>, and --mem-replay=<path>.

--mem-replay=<path> takes the MEM expectation texts recorded in the consistent routes of an earlier report of this generator instead of querying the endpoint, and applies the same matching to the current classic routes. A route that no longer matches becomes mem_sparql_review_needed; nothing becomes consistent through a replay. Use it, with the committed report as input, when only canonical goal texts changed and the endpoint cannot be evaluated. Since November 2026 the endpoint links plans to their parts and competencies through lp:LP_0000565 ("hat direkten Teil") instead of bfo:BFO_0000051, and serves the Bavarian resources under https://w3id.org/lehrplan/resource/by/. The query follows lp:LP_0000565+ since 14 November 2026; the live run of that day kept all 234 previously consistent routes, with the new IRIs, and found 26 more. The MEM consistency audit (quality:mem-sparql-consistency) still fails at its state and plan availability queries (HTTP 500, transitive rdfs:subClassOf* over the whole store); its committed report is from June 2026.

docs.title: 13.2. Runtime Public Index (Repository vs. Package Mode) & Deployment Smoke
docs.text:
• Repository mode: The Explorer source-rationale button lazily fetches two compatibility indexes kept outside the JS bundle and service-worker precache: /data/goal-source-rationales-math-public.json (preferring DE-BY so aligned MEM/FWU examples stay visible) and /data/goal-source-rationales-physics-public.json (never intercepted by the generic deck route).
  • Package mode: /data/** is disabled; the UI discovers bindings via Catalog API 1.2 (/api/ui/curriculum-catalog) and fetches generation-bound per-goal evidence from /api/ui/curriculum-source-evidence/packages/{packageId}/{packageVersion}/goals/{goalId} with zero repository/classpath fallback.

Regeneration, build-artifact verification, and live deployment smoke checks (invoked automatically by ./deploy_skillpilot.sh after service restart, auto-detecting 404 repository mode vs. Catalog API 1.2 package mode):

cd app
npm run quality:goal-source-rationales:public
npm run check:goal-source-rationales:math-public
npm run check:goal-source-rationales:build-artifact
npm run smoke:goal-source-rationales:deployment
npm run smoke:goal-source-rationales:deployment -- --base-url=http://127.0.0.1:8080
cd ..
SKILLPILOT_BASE_URL=https://staging.example.org \
  ./deploy_skillpilot.sh --coach-variant openai-mcp

docs.title: 13.3. Review Checklist and Follow-Up Issues
docs.text:
Inspect five items on every rendered goal:

  1. sourceRationaleStatus: classic_source_reviewed (ready for public index), classic_source_partial (usable only when the rationale explains the partial fit), or classic_source_gap (open a non-blocking follow-up issue).
  2. Reaching the original source: Official URL or retained source path plus a concrete section/search locator is present.
  3. Extracted source evidence: Document metadata resolves, sourceGoalId and reference match the mapping decision, and the Markdown excerpt stays concise (full text remains in JSON).
  4. Why the SkillPilot goal is justified: Understandable mapping rationale that never overstates partial, split, or aggregate mappings.
  5. MEM/FWU SPARQL route: mem_sparql_unavailable for classic-only PoC runs and mem_sparql_consistent for aligned Bavaria showcase items (treated strictly as a secondary route until a scope is approved as primary-ready; file a manual review issue on disagreements or missing metadata).

docs.title: Graph Definition: Rules, Traffic-Light Status, and Milestones (Appendix A)
docs.text:
Generated artifact. Do not edit manually.

Generated by: docs/concept/skill-graph/build_spec.py Regenerate with: cd app && npm run docs:skill-graph:web Source of truth: docs/concept/skill-graph/source/rules-and-gates.json

Language / Sprache: English (EN) · Deutsch (DE) | PDF: English PDF · Deutsches PDF

Compendium: §§1–5 Core · §§6–10 Context · §§11.1–11.4 Units · §11.5 Progression · §12 Planning · §13 Implicit Mastery · Appendices B–F · Appendix A (Rules & Ampel)

This appendix is the reference register for all 145 skill-graph rules (GD-*) in this document. For every rule, it answers three questions: what is required, which validation area owns the obligation, and what the existing checks actually prove.

  • How to read a row. Each GD-* row links an obligation to its designated validation area (target), existing checks (actual), and their evidentiary limits: ID (GD-, the document-part letter, and a sequential number: C for the formal core, X for context, U for learning units, P for planning, A for implicit-mastery recognition, and D for the document appendices); Traffic light (technical enforcement level at the stated audited repository state: HARD for rules enforced fail-closed across their entire declared domain, PARTIAL for a materially incomplete intended domain or enforcement, including merely indirect maturity-floor protection, OPEN for binding obligations without an established hard gate on the core claim, and OPT/DOC for optional profiles, undecided policy, or document checks); Obligation (concise statement of the rule); Target (the validation area assigned to the obligation: a milestone M0–M7 or one of the area codes in Section A.2); Actual and gap (what existing checks prove and what remains open); Section (the named section where the rule is defined). Rows use concise telegraphic style and recurring shorthand: Unit for learning unit, Exam or Assessment for an exam or assessment goal, Memory for a memory goal or memorization, Normal and Strict for normal mode and strict mode, Closure for transitive closure, Scope for validation or applicability scope, Runtime for runtime execution, unit-wide lock for holistic unit gating, and human trial for learner evaluation.
  • Milestones and rule families. Milestones M0–M7 structure automated curriculum QA; runtime contracts, concepts, optional profiles, and artifact or document obligations are tracked separately. The two existing rule families are Curriculum Quality Review (CQR) and graph-validation rollout rule (GVR), denoting curriculum quality checks and skill-graph validator rollout rules respectively. The legend in Section A.2 defines every code referenced here along with its actual scope.
  • An assignment is not a pass. Target assignment names the validation area responsible for each obligation; the existing gates listed alongside prove only their actual scope. A binding rule without a complete gate is an open verification obligation, not an already passed check. M0 is a possible incomplete starting state, not a quality seal. Profile-bound route gates apply within their declared QA scopes. By contrast, the global base check for complete atomic normal form and transitive minimality (check code G17) must cover the entire declared canonical subject inventory, including relevant cross-subject prerequisites and inheriting ancestors; a QA profile subset or partial scan is insufficient.
  • Base before every milestone. Complete atomic normal form and a full transitive-minimality check are the required target base before any promotion to M1–M7. A G17 violation or an incomplete check blocks every milestone pass M1–M7 in the affected subject, even though individual source or review checks may still pass on their own. The current atomic target state \(R \subseteq A \times A\) and its transitive minimality are binding. Under the Product Owner decision of 12 November 2026, a particular migration order and equality with an earlier prerequisite closure are no longer acceptance conditions. Complete current validation is independent of historical reduction proofs. CQR-102 and GVR-012 remain directly atomic.
  • Memory goals. Flashcard repetitions belong to the learning process. Completing a memory goal requires its own explicit verification record; subsequent review due dates alone do not revoke that completion. Ordinary completed goals receive neither review due dates nor any mastery revocation derived from them. No new assessment entity or schema is introduced by this contract.
  • Scope of the register. The 145 stable GD-* IDs cover all six parts of the compendium. Section references use named sections rather than volatile line numbers. Runtime contracts, new recognition and learning-unit semantics, optional planning, and publication or document obligations are never assigned a fabricated M7 gate; where the Product Owner fixes a target area, such as M5/M7 for the coverage evidence of learning units (R2), the row states that it is not yet enforced. Subject-matter accuracy, human trials, and learning effectiveness remain independent forms of evidence. Under the Product Owner decision of 13 November 2026, the grading domain of GD-* rows is the 21-root canonical Gymnasium catalog. Milestone-bound obligations apply from their stated threshold (ten M6/M7 subjects, including five M7 subjects; twelve route scopes). Non-canonical landscapes alone do not prevent a hard grade; open runtime or subject-matter sub-obligations within this domain remain. The graph validator loads 548 live files: 21 canonical Gymnasium roots and 527 landscapes outside Gymnasium. The 45 unchanged Bavarian input graphs remain source-only; explicit compatibility access stays separate from the canonical live domain. The source audit documents consumers, boundaries, and negative tests.

docs.title: Traffic-Light Status: What Is Truly Hard-Enforced Today
docs.text:
Many of the 145 GD-* rule groups bundle a technically gated structural core together with broader runtime, migration, or subject-matter obligations. The four-state traffic light therefore makes visible—both per individual validator gate and per rule group—where a technically hard (fail-closed) gate already operates today and where scope limits or open obligations remain. The CQR/GVR hardening from PR #131 is integrated into main; the later mainline state 2129b207f4 passes the complete CI #2315. The scope statements below also reflect the Gymnasium decision of 13 November and the current follow-up work; broader GD obligations retain their own classifications. Historical CI does not automatically verify later changes. The delivery record distinguishes PR verification, integration, and the two remaining expansion targets.

Traffic Light Meaning for Enforcement and CI Count 🟢 HARD Fully hard-enforced. The entire core claim is technically gated fail-closed across its declared domain; no material sub-obligation of the row remains open. Fully gated within the canonical 21-root catalog: GD-C05, C07, C11, C15–C17, C19, X07, U13. G17 applies independently of maturity pins; catalog completeness and negative cases are evidenced in the register. Additionally hard at their milestone thresholds: GD-C08, X45, X46, requiring atomicity reviews for ten M6/M7 subjects and complete D/P/A/M/V evidence for five M7 subjects. Every upgrade names its gate, domain, and existing negative tests (12 groups). 12 🟡 PARTIAL Incomplete intended domain or incomplete enforcement. A material part of the row remains outside the checked domain, has only indirect floor protection, or has no established fail-closed check. A precisely declared and fully checked profile domain alone does not make a gate partial. The policy pins all 21 catalog roots and twelve route scopes against a Git base. A bounded but completely gated milestone domain alone does not justify a partial grade. Material gaps remain: positive weights and description quality below M7 (GD-C04), missing-card runtime behavior (GD-X26), and session grading (GD-X29). Semantic route and general assessment-coverage obligations (GD-C21, C22, A18) exceed their evidenced gates. Other closure, unit, content-package, license, package, and release contracts remain separately bounded (50 groups). 50 🔴 OPEN Binding, core obligation still without a hard gate. Normatively binding target, runtime, or concept rule without a cross-cutting fail-closed gate established in this register. Atomic expansion before closure in result derivation (GD-C13), open cluster atomization in goalEntry (GD-X09), cluster satisfaction across all atoms instead of isCoreForPrereqs (GD-C26), not-yet-implemented global implicit-mastery recognition including its recognition gate and the learning-unit validity rules R2 and R5 of 11 November 2026 (GD-A01–A17, C25, C30, X18, X32, X36), recursive LearningUnits including their purpose and boundary criterion (GD-U01–U03, U07–U11, U15), and pure runtime, dialogue, and edge-provenance contracts (55 groups). 55 ⚪ OPT/DOC No production mandatory gate. Deliberately optional planning, explicitly undecided lock policy, or pure document/model verification outside curriculum and runtime gates. Optional acquisition and time planning (GD-P01–P11, X33–X35, X37), undecided unit-wide access lock (GD-U14), and appendix, model-checker, and PDF-build rules (GD-D01–D12; build and model scripts check fail-closed locally, while pure docs/** changes are exempted in ci.yml; 28 groups). 28

Total register: 12 HARD, 50 PARTIAL, 55 OPEN, 28 OPT/DOC (total: 145 rule groups).

docs.title: Overview of Validation Areas
docs.text: Code Status Meaning M0 Base, before M1 🟡 PARTIAL Obligation: Identity, references, structure, and base graph; complete atomic normal form and transitive-minimality check as the target base before every higher milestone pass; validity of every authored learning unit (R1, R3, R4). Actual limit: Schema and skill-graph validators check core invariants hard across all loaded skill landscapes; CQR-002 checks explicit types of canonical Gymnasium roots; since 11 November 2026, CQR-001 adds the full G17 check for every root of the complete canonical Gymnasium catalog (a violation caps the subject at M0; hard in CI through the direct complete-catalog G17 check). Non-canonical roots have no G17 gate. Unit validity (R1, R3, uniqueness part of R4) is checked by the standalone CI gate validate:learning-units for the learning units authored in the canonical Gymnasium landscapes, ownership completeness only for landscapes that declare learningUnitCoverage as complete; it does not enter the maturity status. M1 🟡 PARTIAL Obligation: Readable, traceably registered source inventory. Actual limit: CQR-000 is directly hard-gated through pinned required individual passes; this does not prove subject-accurate mappings. M2 🟡 PARTIAL Obligation: Bidirectionally source-evidenced views, course-level mapping, and goal-count plausibility. Actual limit: CQR-003/004/005 are directly hard-gated through pinned required individual passes; broader source fidelity remains subject review. M3 🟡 PARTIAL Obligation: Additional complete directly atomic orientation-to-autonomy routes within the named scopes. Actual limit: CQR-101/102/103 across twelve profiles; GVR-012 additionally in Mathematics lower/upper secondary, Biology and Physics upper secondary. Its complete M7 obligation is decided but not yet activated. The independent G17 gate covers the 21 canonical roots. M4 🟡 PARTIAL Obligation: Visible route endpoints and concrete terminal assessment tasks. Actual limit: CQR-201/202 are direct pinned obligations across the twelve profiles; CQR-104 is a pinned visibility obligation in eight scopes, with the four remaining stage profiles explicitly recorded as gaps. Its catalog target and promotion threshold are both M4. This does not prove live grading conformance. M5 🟡 PARTIAL Obligation: Assessment approval/coverage metadata, current atomicity reviews, composition views, and cleared applicability warning debt; reviewed application coverage of every own ordinary unit goal (R2). Actual limit: CQR-203/301/401/501 are directly pinned obligations plus composition and filter validators; the catalog target of 203 is M5, and view file counting alone does not prove full domain sign-off. R2 is not checked: validate:learning-units only verifies claimed coverage reviews and reports missing ones; no M5 gate consumes them. M6 🟡 PARTIAL Obligation: Justified memory-support decisions, traceable cards/decks, and required view visibility. Actual limit: CQR-302 across all ten protected M6/M7 floors plus card-review check; makes no claim about personal due dates or mastery revocation. M7 🟡 PARTIAL Obligation: Simultaneously current D/P/A/M/V evidence for all current curricularAtomic goals, all mandatory checks passed, and zero blockers; current per-goal binding of the R2 coverage evidence. Additionally, complete semantic route checking by GVR-012 shall apply from M7 (Product Owner decision of 13 November 2026). Actual limit: CQR-303 on five M7 floors atop all lower stages; implies neither human sign-off, learner trials, learning effectiveness, nor general runtime conformance. None of the six required checks covers R2. GVR-012 is hard only in four of the seven current M7 scopes; the complete M7 obligation awaits current evidence and technical activation. Cross-Stage 🟡 PARTIAL Obligation: Learner state, satisfaction, frontier, Personal Curriculum, roles, focus, goal-type, and persistence contracts; versioned recognition contracts (R5). Actual limit: Closure compiler (10 November 2026), seed-scope fallback for non-compilable contexts (11 November 2026), and view/role checks established; remaining runtime and interaction proofs stay separate, with no blanket curriculum M-gate; R5 is a precondition before recognition is enabled. Concept / Optional 🔴 OPEN / ⚪ OPT/DOC Obligation: New global implicit-mastery recognition and recursive learning units (OPEN), plus optional time/budget planning and undecided unit access (OPT/DOC). Actual limit: Derive neither implemented new semantics nor a hard access lock from M7. Artifact / Document 🟡 PARTIAL / ⚪ OPT/DOC Obligation: Interchange, publication, licensing, data protection (PARTIAL), and document sign-off (OPT/DOC). Actual limit: Package, license, and release checks run in CI; a local document build is neither publication nor host acceptance.

docs.title: Gate Reference and Actual Scope
docs.text:
Stable codes name individual existing checks (maturity and route documentation, graph validation rules). The legend explains every code; the subsequent assignment key maps their actual effect onto the milestones. The legend covers the exact six GVR and eighteen CQR codes cited in this register; additional validator rules are neither introduced nor claimed as verified here. The 24 delivered gate entries comprise 22 HARD and 2 PARTIAL gates (GVR-012 and CQR-104); broader GD groups retain their independently assessed classifications. Mainline integration is evidenced at 2129b207f4 by complete green CI. Direct CQR checks reject missing, duplicate, non-passing, and deconfigured required results; independent inventories and Git-base comparison prevent silent domain shrinkage. The eleven roots pinned at M0 are not claimed to pass higher source or review obligations.

Gate Status Actual Scope GVR-001 🟢 HARD A goal must not directly require any of its own contains ancestors; local skill landscape (all loaded skill landscapes). GVR-003 🟢 HARD A goal must not directly require its direct contains parent node; local skill landscape (all loaded skill landscapes). GVR-009 🟢 HARD A stored structural node type must match its classification as leaf or cluster; local skill landscape (all loaded skill landscapes). GVR-010 🟢 HARD An optional shortKey must be unique within a logical skill landscape; language editions of the same goal may share the same ID/shortKey pair. GVR-012 🟡 PARTIAL Binding target since 13 November 2026: semantic direct atomic routes for every registered scope of subjects obligated to meet M7. Today: seven scopes of five M7 subjects, with four hard (Mathematics lower/upper secondary, Biology and Physics upper secondary). Physics lower secondary and Chemistry upper secondary have 5/3 route findings; Economics lacks 24 current classifications. The full inventory remains twelve scopes; five M6 scopes without ledgers become mandatory on promotion to M7. The route audit diagnoses all twelve and is not an M7 promotion check. validate:graph continues to block on the four required scopes. The complete M7 obligation is activated only after evidence-backed gap closure. The code stays PARTIAL until fail-closed enforcement of the whole M7 domain, including future promotions; no floor is lowered and no existing required scope is removed. A later HARD grade does not automatically upgrade broader GD rules. The Physics lane now also includes reviewed explicit stage targets. Another 43 upper-secondary targets inherited only through subtrees remain separate alignment debt, 42 without terminal routes; this is not complete stage-target coverage. GVR-014 🟢 HARD Orientation goals are prerequisite-free atoms without exam, memory, example, or assessment metadata; all loaded skill landscapes. CQR-000 🟢 HARD Source inventories are readable, linked to official HTTP(S) sources, and have their extracted goals registered. Direct required pass for curricula pinned at M1 or higher: currently 10 of 21 catalog roots. CQR-001 🟢 HARD Since 11 November 2026: every declared root of the complete current canonical Gymnasium catalog, with its required cross-subject goals and inheriting ancestors, passes the shared reference and effective-DAG audit, atomic requires normal form, explicit type consistency, and transitive minimality (G17). Direct required pass for all 21 canonical Gymnasium catalog roots, independently of maturity. CQR-002 🟢 HARD Stored structural node types match the atomic or cluster structure. Direct required pass for all 21 canonical Gymnasium catalog roots, independently of maturity. CQR-003 🟢 HARD Jurisdiction views have atomic source evidence and cover all registered original source goals completely; checked bidirectionally. Direct required pass for curricula pinned at M2 or higher: currently 10 of 21 catalog roots. CQR-004 🟢 HARD Upper-secondary source goals match the GK/LK mapping of canonical goals; unspecified course levels apply to both GK and LK unless a reviewed LK exception exists. Direct required pass for curricula pinned at M2 or higher: currently 10 of 21 catalog roots. CQR-005 🟢 HARD Extracted goal counts are plausible against the reviewed HE/BW baseline or have explicitly reviewed deviations. Direct required pass for curricula pinned at M2 or higher: currently 10 of 21 catalog roots. CQR-101 🟢 HARD Complete routes across effective (including inherited) prerequisites connect motivation and terminal autonomy; configured QA scopes. Direct required pass for scopes pinned at M1 or higher: currently all 12 declared route scopes (each pinned M4). CQR-102 🟢 HARD Complete routes across directly authored atomic prerequisites connect motivation and terminal autonomy; configured QA scopes. Direct required pass for scopes pinned at M2 or higher: currently all 12 declared route scopes (each pinned M4). This gate proves atomic reachability; the stronger semantic GVR-012 route obligation is gated in four of twelve scopes (Mathematics lower/upper secondary, Biology and Physics upper secondary). CQR-103 🟢 HARD Clusters selected within the QA scope carry no requires; not a global proof across all authored edges. Direct required pass for scopes pinned at M2 or higher: currently all 12 declared route scopes (each pinned M4). CQR-202 🟢 HARD Their exam tasks are concrete and usable in assessment mode rather than placeholders.
