docs.title: Assignment Key
docs.text:
Register rows name validation areas using the eleven codes below. Each entry explains a code together with its existing checks and their evidentiary limits.

  • BASE. CQR-001 (references, effective DAG, atomic normal form, explicit types, and transitive minimality, i.e. G17, over the complete canonical Gymnasium catalog since 11 November 2026) and CQR-002 (explicit structural node types) carry catalog target M0. validate:graph runs additional standalone GVR and integrity checks across all loaded skill landscapes. Unit validity (R1, R3, R4) is assigned here; the standalone gate validate:learning-units checks R1, R3, and the uniqueness part of R4 fail-closed for the learning units authored in the canonical Gymnasium landscapes, ownership completeness only for landscapes that declare learningUnitCoverage as complete, and outside the maturity status computation. This does not imply complete verification of every mathematical or runtime rule.
  • SOURCE. CQR-000 targets M1 and CQR-003/004/005 target M2. The direct checker requires each source rule to pass in its pinned domain (currently ten of 21 curricula); M2 promotion also requires passes, including 004 and 005. Source inventory, bidirectional registered source coverage, course mapping, and count plausibility remain distinct technical claims. None alone establishes subject-matter accuracy or complete original-PDF extraction.
  • ROUTE. CQR-101/102/103 \(\to\) M3, configured QA scopes only. CQR-102 uses exclusively directly authored atomic edges; CQR-103 forbids requires on selected clusters. GVR-012 adds the semantic route check for Mathematics lower/upper secondary, Biology and Physics upper secondary (four of twelve scopes); CQR-102 is a shared reachability obligation, not that stronger semantic guarantee. CQR-104 carries catalog target M4 and is required for promotion there in its eight pinned visibility scopes. The Product Owner decision of 13 November 2026 places the stronger semantic obligation at M7; four of seven current M7 scopes are secured, and complete activation remains pending.
  • EXAM. CQR-201/202 carry catalog target M4; CQR-203 carries target M5, matching its promotion threshold with core reviews. Metadata and task-readiness checks prove neither accurate live-session grading nor independent application coverage across every passing score combination.
  • VIEW. CQR-401 and CQR-501 \(\to\) M5. 401 counts existing view files rather than proving their complete domain sign-off. Standalone validate:composition-views and validate:view-filters gates check further, individually bounded structural and projection obligations. Never equate these blanketly with all runtime rules.
  • REVIEW. CQR-301 \(\to\) M5 (current semantic atomicity decisions), CQR-302 \(\to\) M6 (memory decisions, cards, and visibility), CQR-303 \(\to\) M7 (complete current D/P/A/M/V intersection with required checks passed and zero blockers). M7 remains automated curriculum QA.
  • RT. Cross-stage runtime and interaction contract; no curriculum M-gate is designated for this overall claim. Individual implementations and tests must be evidenced separately; their mere existence is not a live conformance check.
  • CONCEPT. Normatively specified, but new global implicit-mastery recognition and recursive learning-unit semantics are explicitly not yet implemented in production. No existing curriculum M-gate. Structural or content shares may be mapped to target validation areas for future implementation without fabricating M7 fulfillment.
  • OPTIONAL. Optional planning profile or still-undecided holistic unit-access policy. No curriculum M-gate; do not derive a new hard runtime lock from the specification.
  • ARTIFACT. Standalone publication, interchange, licensing, or data-protection contract; no automatic M0–M7 assignment. Any specific package or release check must be evidenced within its own declared scope.
  • DOCUMENT. Document build, mathematical formula model, or diagram check; neither a curriculum M-gate nor proof of runtime conformance or learning effectiveness.

docs.title: Actual Promotion Chain and Additional Gates
docs.text:
Actual maturity promotion is governed by deriveScopeMaturity and deriveCurriculumMaturity in the status generator; catalog metadata alone never computes maturity. Catalog targets now match promotion thresholds: CQR-104/201/202 at M4 and CQR-203 with core reviews at M5. The eight-scope CQR-104 boundary is explicit in the pinned policy; the remaining four visibility scopes stay open.

  • M0 \(\to\) M1: CQR-001/002 and CQR-000 must be pass. Both base graph rules carry catalog target M0; since 11 November 2026, CQR-001 includes the G17 check, whose violation also caps every scope at M0.
  • M1 \(\to\) M2: CQR-003/004/005 must each be pass. Missing results, fail, warn, and not_configured prevent promotion to M2.
  • M2 \(\to\) M3: Route profiles must exist; CQR-101/102/103 must be pass in every configured scope.
  • M3 \(\to\) M4: CQR-201/202 must be pass in all twelve scopes; CQR-104 must be present and pass in its eight explicitly pinned visibility scopes. The other four upper-secondary scopes are documented visibility gaps. The catalog target and promotion threshold are M4.
  • M4 \(\to\) M5: All scoped CQR-203 checks plus CQR-301/401/501 must be pass. CQR-203 carries catalog target M5; CQR-401 counts registered view files.
  • M5 \(\to\) M6: Additionally CQR-302 must be pass.
  • M6 \(\to\) M7: Additionally CQR-303 must be pass: non-empty current curricularAtomic denominator, complete D/P/A/M/V intersection, all six mandatory checks passed, and zero blockers.
  • Missing route profiles cap an otherwise source-ready curriculum at M2. CQR-003/004/005 each require exactly pass for promotion; their required results are additionally pinned directly. CQR-401 counts view files. Source coverage binds existing parseable registered snapshots rather than proving exhaustive extraction of official PDFs on its own.
  • Routes are evaluated across twelve declared profiles for ten curricula: Mathematics and Physics each lower/upper secondary; Chemistry and Biology upper secondary; Economics, Politics and Economics, Computer Science, History, German, and Latin cross-stage. The shared evaluator enforces direct atomic reachability (CQR-102) for all profiles; Mathematics lower/upper secondary, Biology and Physics upper secondary additionally receive the stronger semantic GVR-012 check (four of twelve scopes). CQR-103 checks selected clusters. The independent check:transitive-minimality gate enforces the atomic target state and minimality across all 21 canonical Gymnasium roots, independently of protected floors. Retired GVR codes remain reserved; no environment variable downgrades graph errors.
  • The transitive-minimality auditor also runs standalone with CLI and contract tests (check mode fails on findings, whereas report mode can emit findings with exit code 0); CI runs its tests (test:transitive-minimality). Since 11 November 2026, its zero-finding result per canonical Gymnasium root, together with atomic normal form, is part of CQR-001 through the graph-integrity adapter; wherever CQR-001 passes, the historical raw-edge criterion coincides with atomic minimality. Before emitting status rows, the generator validates the current catalog inventory from the curriculum manifest, the canonical overview's subject declarations, and the complete canonical directory independently of historical evidence. The prerequisite-reduction proof registry remains separate for historical review comparisons that depend on it.
  • Commands quality:curriculum-status, quality:curriculum-status:check, check:transitive-minimality, and check:curriculum-maturity-floors are registered in package.json. The status producer computes the report; domain failures lower maturity without alone changing its exit code. The direct obligation checker validates the complete 21-root catalog and twelve scope identities, exact subject/scope maturity pins, and mandatory individual rule passes against the Git base selected with --base-ref (PR base SHA, push-before SHA, or local origin/main). Missing, duplicate, non-passing, or deconfigured required obligations fail closed; policy/configuration changes cannot silently remove base obligations. The standalone complete-catalog G17 gate also rejects regressions in M0 roots. Both checks run in graph-validation and the local curriculum suite. Generated status freshness remains independently checked. PR #131 is integrated; the later complete mainline CI at 2129b207f4 evidences the delivered gates within their declared domains. The CQR-104 obligation is explicitly pinned to its existing eight scopes; all twelve route profiles remain inventoried for the other scoped obligations. Removing a configured visibility scope cannot erase its obligation.

Workflow triggers are manual dispatch, push to main, and pull request to main under path filters; pure documentation changes are generally exempted while generated QA status files are re-included. No single CI or build result on its own proves all runtime, subject-matter, and learning-effectiveness rules.

docs.title: C – Formal Core
docs.text:
Sections 1–5 (01-core). Every row cites its section; GD-* IDs remain stable regardless of later section renumbering.

ID Status Section Rule (concise summary) Area Enforcement and boundary GD-C01 🟡 PARTIAL §1.1 Finite learning-goal graph \((G,C,R)\); contains and requires are the sole authored goal edges. Inverse and non-empty transitive closure are distinct operations. DAG checks apply to the respective named relations rather than blanketly to \(C \cup R\). BASE (M0 base); semantic definition cross-stage BASE, GVR-008, and schema enforce finite goal sets, permitted edge fields, and separate DAGs; mathematical operation semantics is not a standalone CQR pass. GD-C02 🟡 PARTIAL §1.1 contains: parent goal \(\to\) child; requires: dependent goal \(\to\) prerequisite. Any learning-flow diagram drawn in the reverse direction must explicitly declare the inversion. BASE (M0 base) / presentation cross-stage BASE/ROUTE consume the edge direction; diagram labeling is not a CQR check. GD-C03 🟡 PARTIAL §1.2 Canonical UUID identity is injective and persists across language, placement, and view; local formula letters do not define an alternative storage format. BASE (M0 base); identity preservation additionally RT/ARTIFACT BASE plus UUID and view validators enforce ID format and uniqueness, but do not on their own prove all version and migration guarantees. GD-C04 🟡 PARTIAL §1.2 Base attributes are total: ID, title, and strictly positive weight. description must be intelligible and verifiable; examples are illustrative references, neither quality proof nor competency evidence. BASE (M0 base) for form/data domain; M7 for current content evidence Schema-required fields apply across the canonical Gymnasium catalog (21 roots); CQR-303 requires current content evidence for the five M7 subjects. The runtime schema permits any numeric weight, rather than only positive values; intelligible and verifiable descriptions are not fully gated below M7. These two sub-obligations remain open. GD-C05 🟢 HARD §1.2 An optional shortKey is unique per logical skill landscape; localized language files for the same goal may reuse the same ID/shortKey pair. BASE (M0 base) Hard-enforced via GVR-010 in validate:graph across all loaded skill landscapes, including the localization boundary. GD-C06 🟡 PARTIAL §1.2 phase is compatibility/display metadata, neither identity nor sequencing. area/tags never replace authoritative goal-type or scope decisions; level denotes difficulty; core does not on its own determine the selected target scope; weight denotes progress share rather than duration or evidentiary strength; new optional materials belong in content packages. Cross-stage model contract; M2/M5 for respective mapping/view evidence; material contract ARTIFACT Content-package validator and GVR-008 enforce material separation; no single gate checks every field's semantic boundary. For sources and materials see GD-X38–GD-X43. GD-C07 🟢 HARD §1.3 Structurally atomic iff a goal has no contains children; otherwise a cluster. Polyhierarchy is permitted; explicit structural types must match. Pedagogical goal kinds are neither new structural types nor program units. BASE (M0 base) Structural type, leaf/cluster classification, polyhierarchy, and separation from program units are hard-enforced globally via GVR-009, CQR-002, and schema; semantic atomicity is governed separately by GD-C08. GD-C08 🟢 HARD §1.3 A structural leaf is not automatically semantically atomic; bundling multiple independent sub-competencies can fail content review. M5, deeper current binding M7 (REVIEW) From M5, CQR-301 requires current accepted atomicity reviews; check:curriculum-maturity-floors enforces the individual pass for all ten M6/M7 subjects in the 21-root catalog. The five M7 subjects additionally require CQR-303. Eleven M0 roots do not claim this higher maturity. Negative evidence: required-pass tests reject missing, failing, warning, and deconfigured CQR-301/303 despite claimed maturity. The producer contract additionally rejects invalid/inconsistent records, parse errors, and duplicates. A structural leaf never substitutes for review. GD-C09 🟡 PARTIAL §2.1 Anc/Desc follow non-empty contains paths; \(\Atoms(a)=\{a\}\) for atoms and atomic descendants otherwise. In a finite DAG every cluster has leaf descendants; set semantics counts multi-paths once. Childless means atom, never empty cluster. BASE (M0 base); RT for evaluation BASE proves structural invariants, not every runtime aggregation path. GD-C10 🟡 PARTIAL §2.2 Multiple prerequisites apply conjunctively. Alternatives require an explicit selection contract; \(R\) is acyclic. BASE (M0 base); selection contract separate BASE checks DAG acyclicity; there is no tacit OR semantics. GD-C11 🟢 HARD §2.2; §2.3 In the target state, all domain prerequisites are authored strictly between atomic learning goals: \(R \subseteq A \times A\). Cluster inheritance remains a transitional compatibility mechanism and never substitutes for complete atomic modeling. Never delete an atomic route in favor of an inherited cluster representation. BASE (M0 target base, before M1): necessary prerequisite for the full G17 check; never deferred to M3 CQR-001 and check:transitive-minimality enforce atomic source and prerequisite goals across all 21 canonical Gymnasium roots, including necessary foreign goals. Cluster route bridges therefore fail independently of the maturity pin. Negative evidence: the G17 producer test rejects minimal cluster sources and targets and caps the subject and scopes at M0. Broader semantic route obligations belong to GD-C21/22; historical route equality is no longer an acceptance condition under the 12 November decision. GD-C12 🟡 PARTIAL §2.3 Effective direct requirements equal a goal's own requirements united with those inherited from all contains ancestors; multiple parents yield set union. Inheritance and transitive closure are distinct operations. BASE (M0 base for valid transition inventory); RT validate:graph checks effective cycles; that alone does not prove all runtime evaluations. GD-C13 🔴 OPEN §2.3 Expand effective requirements to atoms first, then form the transitive closure; further prerequisites of expanded atoms remain included. Mastering an intermediate goal never truncates the closure. BASE (M0 target base for normalized validity); RT/CONCEPT for result derivation Not blanketly covered by CQR-001 or historical G17/completion tests. GD-C14 🟡 PARTIAL §3.1 contains, direct requires, and effective requires are acyclic; self- or back-dependencies induced via atomic expansion are likewise invalid. BASE (M0 base) BASE and effective DAG checks hold only for the relations they actually evaluate; full atomic expansion must be verified separately. GD-C15 🟢 HARD §3.1 Requiring the same target both directly and via ancestor inheritance is locally redundant. In the atomic target state clusters carry no outgoing requirements; absence of local duplicates alone is insufficient for G17. BASE (M0 target base, before M1, jointly with atomic normal form) CQR-001 and check:transitive-minimality check all 21 canonical Gymnasium roots, including relevant foreign goals and inheriting ancestors, for non-atomic and redundant requirements independently of the maturity pin. Negative evidence: G17 integrity tests reject direct redundancy and an inherited foreign alternative route; the producer caps the subject and scopes at M0. GD-C16 🟢 HARD §3.1 Transitive minimality is binding: every authored requirement connects atomic goals and is not reachable through the remaining requirements. Testing raw authored edges against an inherited alternative path alone does not establish this target state. BASE (M0 target base, before M1): full G17 check on the atomic target state; any violation or incomplete check blocks every subject milestone pass M1–M7 CQR-001 and the direct check:transitive-minimality CI gate enforce complete atomic normal form and transitive minimality across all 21 canonical Gymnasium roots, including necessary foreign goals and inheriting ancestors, independently of floors. An incomplete catalog aborts. Negative evidence: the G17 producer rejects redundant and non-atomic edges; the CLI test requires exit 1 for redundancy. The stronger semantic route obligation is a separate rule (GD-C21/22). GD-C17 🟢 HARD §3.1 Before every subject and scope milestone pass M1–M7, completely and deterministically validate G17 on the current declared canonical Gymnasium catalog, including necessary cross-subject prerequisites and inheriting ancestors. Errors or incomplete validation block the pass. Under the Product Owner decision of 12 November 2026, historical closure equality and migration order are no longer acceptance conditions. BASE (M0 base before M1): complete current target-state validation as a prerequisite for every subject and scope milestone pass M1–M7 CQR-001 checks all 21 roots of the complete current canonical Gymnasium catalog. Reference and cycle errors, non-atomic requirements, type contradictions, redundancies, and missing or incomplete validation cap the subject and its scopes at M0; an incomplete catalog aborts the status run. This milestone block applies independently of the subject maturity pin; all 21 roots, including M0, are pinned in the policy. Catalog completeness is checked independently of historical reduction proofs; within the milestone producer, historical proofs serve only valid review reuse, otherwise strict current review inputs apply. Non-canonical roots lie outside this explicitly bounded rule scope. The independent check:transitive-minimality CI command now rejects any failing root even without a maturity floor; all 21 roots pass at the audited mainline state, including the eleven M0 roots. GD-C18 🟡 PARTIAL §3.1 Identities and references must be resolvable; unknown goals are never treated as satisfied prerequisites. BASE (M0 base) + RT BASE checks static references; fail-closed runtime semantics is verified separately. GD-C19 🟢 HARD §3.2 Single-parent tree structure is an optional profile rather than a global DAG requirement. Forbidding own ancestors is profile-bound; requiring own descendants can already induce effective self-dependency. BASE (M0 base for actual cycles); optional profile separate Within the declared domain of all 21 canonical Gymnasium roots, GVR-001/003, CQR-001, and check:transitive-minimality reject ancestor requirements and every cluster source or target, including its own child. Negative evidence: the retirement test rejects a cluster requiring its child and a cluster prerequisite target through CQR-001. No universal single-parent mandate is claimed or introduced. GD-C20 🟡 PARTIAL §3.2 Skill-graph validity, projection validity, and full learnability from a declared entry state are distinct claims. Atomic self-dependency and an empty initial frontier can refute learnability. BASE (M0 base) + VIEW; learnability profile separate A single green validator pass never proves all three claims simultaneously. GD-C21 🟡 PARTIAL §3.3 Every non-exempt atom lies on a direct atomic route Orientation \(\to\) Atom \(\to\) Terminal Autonomy. Exemptions require a documented machine-readable selection contract; clusters do not serve as route bridges. M3 (ROUTE); stronger semantics shall apply from M7 CQR-102 enforces direct atomic reachability across all twelve pinned QA scopes. GVR-012 checks the stronger semantic contract in four scopes (Mathematics lower/upper secondary, Biology and Physics upper secondary). Since the Product Owner decision of 13 November 2026, the expansion target is the complete M7 domain: currently seven scopes, three with unresolved route or classification findings. The five other M6 scopes remain inventoried and become mandatory on promotion to M7. The complete M7 gate is not yet activated; the row remains PARTIAL. A later hard GVR gate still requires an independent review of every obligation in this row. The formula is a structural criterion, not proof of pedagogical quality. The Physics lane now also includes reviewed explicit stage targets. Another 43 upper-secondary targets inherited only through subtrees remain separate alignment debt, 42 without terminal routes; this is not complete stage-target coverage. GD-C22 🟡 PARTIAL §3.3 Route profiles define stage, goal kinds, ordering, and validation scope. Memory support is added only where needed, not as a universally mandatory intermediate step. M3 (ROUTE); memory content decision M6 (REVIEW); stronger route semantics shall apply from M7 CQR-101/102/103 directly enforce their route obligations across twelve scopes; GVR-012 adds complete semantic validation in four scopes (Mathematics lower/upper secondary, Biology and Physics upper secondary). CQR-001 applies to all 21 canonical roots; CQR-302 checks memory evidence from M6. The future semantic obligation covers every scope of subjects obligated to meet M7: three of seven are currently missing; five other M6 scopes await later promotion to M7. Complete activation remains pending. Neither this target decision, twelve visibility scopes under CQR-104, nor a later hard GVR-012 automatically makes the entire row HARD. The Physics lane now also includes reviewed explicit stage targets. Another 43 upper-secondary targets inherited only through subtrees remain separate alignment debt, 42 without terminal routes; this is not complete stage-target coverage. GD-C23 🔴 OPEN §3.3 Cluster overviews may be derived from atomic reachability. An existential summary edge is never a universal prerequisite; percentage coverage requires a declared denominator; author no new cluster requires. Cross-stage presentation; prohibition of new authored cluster edges follows from BASE (M0 target base before M1) No standalone CQR pass covers overview display semantics. GD-C24 🔴 OPEN §4.1 Exactly one stored binary state per atom; partial scoring creates no third mastery tier. Ordinary completions evidence understanding, whereas special goal types use their own completion contracts. RT, cross-stage No curriculum M-gate; see goal-type rules. GD-C25 🔴 OPEN §4.1 \(\Meff\) equals explicit mastery united with derivations from durably valid local contracts. It acts globally on prerequisites and actual progress across focus switches without writing synthetic mastery records. Orientation denotes only a completed entry. CONCEPT, no M-gate New global implicit-mastery recognition is explicitly not yet implemented; M7 does not prove it. GD-C26 🔴 OPEN §4.1 \(\Sat(g)\) holds iff \(g\) has a non-empty atomic basis contained completely in \(\Meff\). Mastering a dependent content goal alone never proves its prerequisites, and cluster completion never writes mastery back to children. RT/CONCEPT Appendix B documents the historical core-biased cluster aggregation divergence; live conformance must be verified separately. GD-C27 🔴 OPEN §4.2 The global frontier consists of unmastered atoms whose full transitive effective atomic prerequisites are satisfied; traversal never stops at mastered intermediate goals, and partial work never counts as satisfaction. RT/CONCEPT No curriculum M-gate covers this overall runtime claim. GD-C28 🔴 OPEN §4.2 A separate cluster frontier uses own and inherited atomic bases together with transitive closure and never replaces the atomic learning frontier. The UI may apply further explicit selection rules. RT Never equate the mathematical frontier with every UI menu listing. GD-C29 🟡 PARTIAL §4.3 Weighted progress counts unique target atoms rather than clusters and children simultaneously. Weights must be positive; an empty target set never receives a fabricated 100% value. Uniform weights are a domain convention rather than a requirement; the Personal Curriculum fixes the target denominator. Progress share is neither fractional per-goal mastery nor a grade or probability. RT; attribute base BASE (M0) Schema enforces numeric weight and the closure compiler (10 November 2026) fixes the personal denominator \(L\); no global gate checks strictly positive weights and every display formula. GD-C30 🔴 OPEN §4.3 Segmented progress views may distinguish explicit and implicit contributions, while total progress counts their union. Any counter restricted to explicit mastery must be labeled as such. RT/CONCEPT Joint explicit/implicit progress accounting is proven neither by M7 nor by current display components. GD-C31 🟡 PARTIAL §5.1 A filter is a predicate; applicability is a partial dimensional map. An omitted dimension is unrestricted, an explicit empty value set excludes concrete values, and ALL ignores a dimension solely as a query value and is never persisted. An unresolved personal stage stays unresolved. VIEW/RT; M2/M5 only for respective source/warning-debt shares Filter validator and CQR-501 check compiled applicability in canonical scopes; not a blanket proof of every runtime filter case. GD-C32 🟡 PARTIAL §5.1 Applicability overrides justify exceptions; runtime evaluates compiled applicability. Visibility alone never proves official source coverage. M2 (SOURCE) for source evidence; M5 (VIEW) for warning debt; RT SOURCE/VIEW are checked separately; an accepted override waiver never substitutes for CQR-003 source coverage. GD-C33 🟡 PARTIAL §5.2 Preserve the full transitive atomic closure prior to view or focus restriction; global inheritance and atomic expansion always precede filtering. Under the 10 November 2026 Product Owner decision, this closure together with the selected seed targets forms the fixed personal learning scope \(L\). Hidden children never turn a cluster into an atom. VIEW/RT Verify full closure and identity preservation separately; existing opaque goalEntry cluster atomization remains an open implementation gap. GD-C34 🔴 OPEN §5.3 Normal mode restricts globally computed transitive atomic requirements to focus endpoints; an empty relative prerequisite basis does not block. Strict mode checks all global prerequisites for candidates inside the focus. The strict frontier is a subset of the normal frontier. Out-of-focus prerequisites are never marked mastered. RT/CONCEPT No curriculum M-gate. Global closure computation prior to filtering must be verified separately. GD-C35 🔴 OPEN §5.3 Given \(g \to x \to p\) and focus \(\{g,p\}\), \(p\) remains required in normal mode while strict mode additionally requires \(x\). Mastering \(x\) never removes the transitive requirement on \(p\). RT/CONCEPT Distinct mediated-transitivity case, not proven by direct-neighbor checks alone. GD-C36 🔴 OPEN §5.4 Global diagnostics reports all missing transitive atoms and distinguishes in-focus from out-of-focus blockers. Listing direct clusters is insufficient; diagnostics creates neither edges nor mastery and is distinct from normal-mode blockers. RT No curriculum M-gate.

docs.title: X – Context, Views, Goal Types, Provenance, and Quality
docs.text:
Sections 6–10 (02-context). Every row cites its section; GD-* IDs remain stable regardless of later section renumbering.

ID Status Section Rule (concise summary) Area Enforcement and boundary GD-X01 🟡 PARTIAL §6 Goals, program units, placements, competency axes, and composition views serve distinct responsibilities. Reordering creates no new competency and deletes no learner results; broad taxonomy categories are not concrete assessable skills. Cross-stage model contract; M5 target (VIEW) for delivered views Schema and composition validator separate the layers structurally; complete migration across all legacy inventories is not claimed. GD-X02 🟡 PARTIAL §6.1 Goal identity persists across new placements. Program-unit type exam is not an exam goal; phase induces neither contains nor requires edges. Historical year trees are compatibility scaffolding rather than durable domain identity. BASE (M0 base for identity); VIEW/RT for projection BASE/VIEW cover only structural sub-obligations. GD-X03 🟡 PARTIAL §6.2 programUnits form a tree or forest; goalPlacements distinguish primary, secondary, and assessed relations; own records without context that a learning unit owns an atomic goal. Secondary relevance or assessment links never create duplicate visible goal nodes. M5 target / VIEW Schema and composition validator enforce structure and duplicate-freeness of compiled views; validate:learning-units checks own placements in the canonical Gymnasium landscapes (LU-PLACEMENT); CQR-401 on its own only counts files. GD-X04 🟡 PARTIAL §6.2 Within a resolved context, a goal has at most one matching primary anchor; an absent placement never permits inventing a parent node. Multiple matching primary placements require reviewed resolution. Context never alters goal IDs. M5 target / VIEW Placement and projection checks run separately; they imply no automatic domain review. GD-X05 🔴 OPEN §6.2 Content view follows contains, program view follows program units and placements, and competency view follows catalog/competency references. Child order stems from declared data order; topological learning order is a distinct view. VIEW/RT No blanket M-gate covers all view-rendering semantics. GD-X06 🟡 PARTIAL §6.3 Composition views specify tree structure, child order, and canonical references—never newly authored atoms or requires. Renderers must not override an authoritative view with title, phase, or placement heuristics. M5 target (VIEW); RT Composition validator enforces reference-based views free of authored atoms or requires; the UI renderer contract remains separate. GD-X07 🟢 HARD §6.3 The compiled default learner tree displays each goal at most once and under at most one parent node. Canonical polyhierarchy requires deterministically validated resolution; role resolution alone never legitimizes duplicates. M5 target / VIEW Hard-enforced across all composition views via CPV-004/005/006 in the composition validator; imposes no global single-parent constraint on canonical goals. GD-X08 🟡 PARTIAL §6.3 Compile early: select context/view, resolve references and full prerequisite closure, verify explicit roles and visible parents, and validate the compiled tree prior to UI rendering. M5 target / VIEW Composition, role, and filter checks verify static compilation of canonical views; CQR-401 only counts files, and cross-subject APV-102 alignment remains open. GD-X09 🔴 OPEN §6.3 No canonical cluster may be turned into an independently completable surrogate atom via goalEntry or display compaction; this rule holds regardless of any semantic-kind review. The canonical atomic basis and required prerequisite chains remain intact, with neither new view requires nor mastery propagation to children. M5 target / VIEW CPV-009 blocks only curricularArea nodes in views; existing runtime cluster atomization is not yet remediated, and M7 does not prove it. GD-X10 🔴 OPEN §7.1 Catalog navigation precedes personalization. Level 1 is the base curriculum, Level 2 the backend-owned durable personal scope, Level 3 the temporary focus with one active atom, and Level 4 the binary result bound to stable goal IDs. View or focus changes preserve results; cluster state is derived. RT, no curriculum M-gate Curriculum QA maturity implies no blanket runtime implementation claim. GD-X11 🔴 OPEN §7.1 LK is a per-subject course attribute rather than an implicit stage; an absent stage remains unresolved. Changing Level 2 revalidates focus and the active goal without granting or deleting global results. Configuration occurs in designated first-party SkillPilot surfaces, never autonomously inside the OpenAI V1 coach. RT Provider and authorization boundaries are not an M7 gate. GD-X12 🟡 PARTIAL §7.1 \(L\) comprises seed targets together with all necessary atomic prerequisites, independent of current mastery; mastered goals stay satisfied inside the denominator. Focus narrows active work only, never total progress or completion. Open necessary atoms require an acquisition target in the full Personal Curriculum; each canonical ID counts once. VIEW/RT; M2/M5 only for concrete view shares 10 November 2026 Product Owner decision; implemented in backend and WebGUI. Full native, curriculum, and remote CI acceptance remain separate; CQR maturity is no substitute. GD-X13 🟡 PARTIAL §7.2 Authored subject roles and their specificity precedence hold: omitted role defaults to target, direct goalEntry overrides subtree inheritance, closer root overrides broader root, and ties resolve to target. Roles are never inferred from age or phase. The explicit personal closure rule adds necessary atoms; a subject-local prerequisiteOnly role is valid when an acquisition target exists elsewhere in \(L\). VIEW/RT CPV-008, role unit tests, and the closure compiler check projectionRole and specificity; no single CQR gate proves every cross-view overlap case. GD-X14 🟡 PARTIAL §7.2 Authored seed references remain hard-validated. A necessary atom's compiled target role backed by a verified canonical path and provenance suffices without manual per-atom authoring. Unknown references, cycles, and missing or unreachable necessary atoms are errors of validation, curriculum QA, and native acceptance; under the 11 November 2026 decision, a learner read of a context whose canonical graph is not strictly compilable keeps the reviewed seed scope without derived closure, claims no learning basis, offers no goal with broken demand, and logs once per curriculum and error code. Seed-selection errors stay hard. Normal mode continues to ignore valid out-of-focus requirements. Cross-stage projection/RT contract CPV-002 and validate:graph enforce reference and cycle errors; the personal closure (10 November 2026) and the seed-scope fallback (11 November 2026, b511654efb, with regression tests) are implemented in the backend; applicability validation and complete acceptance of the current state remain separate. GD-X15 🟡 PARTIAL §7.3 Applicability describes evidenced visibility and placement describes structural location; neither implies mastery. Declared mapping-inheritance boundaries shield supplementary branches from false broad provenance while retaining direct sources. Local endpoint visibility may follow from requires under an explicit contract without proving official source coverage. M2 (SOURCE) for source evidence; M5 (VIEW) for warning debt/views; RT SOURCE/VIEW; inheritance boundaries and derived applicability never automatically satisfy CQR-003. GD-X16 🔴 OPEN §7.4 Focus is the union of selected visible roots and their descendants within the Personal Curriculum. Normal mode checks internal transitive effective requirements while strict mode checks global ones; ignoring out-of-focus blockers never grants mastery. RT Refers to GD-C33–GD-C35; no additional curriculum M-gate. GD-X17 🔴 OPEN §7.4 Focus expansion follows the unique visible parent path, forms a strict superset containing at least one open goal, replaces only subsumed multi-root branches while preserving independent roots, and requires the coach to adopt the exact backend option and await learner confirmation. RT Standalone backend and interaction conformance; not an M-gate. GD-X18 🔴 OPEN §7.4 Only genuine focus completion justifies expansion; an empty frontier may indicate a prerequisite blockade. Newly exposed prerequisites are evaluated normally; mere successor mastery never propagates backward, whereas validly recognized implicit application persists globally and is never reopened. RT/CONCEPT Global recognition remains conceptual; distinguishing true completion from blocked empty frontiers is verified separately. GD-X19 🟡 PARTIAL §8 The skill graph receives a binary result resolved according to goal type and never grades answers, dialogues, or flashcards itself. Ordinary understanding must cover all required competency aspects; one right exercise is not automatically full mastery, nor is there an arbitrary minimum task count. RT; positive content evidence M7 (REVIEW) CQR-303/P checks authored performance profiles, not live learner success per session. GD-X20 🔴 OPEN §8.1 Sufficiently evidenced mastery is persisted immediately; success may be announced only after confirmed persistence. Extra learner consent to save is not a completion condition. Moving to a new topic requires a backend-selected proposal and recognizable learner agreement. RT Persistence and coach-interaction contract; not an M-gate. GD-X21 🟡 PARTIAL §8.2 Orientation conveys honest, motivating possibilities and tests neither prior knowledge nor subject competency, recall, or transfer; there are no motivation percentages. Orientation nodes are pure prerequisite-free atomic entries without exam or memory metadata. BASE (M0 base)/M3 (ROUTE) for structure; RT for dialogue GVR-014 enforces structure and route profiles check embedding; dialogue quality is not proven thereby. GD-X22 🔴 OPEN §8.2 Selecting an interest opens exploration rather than immediate completion: concrete connection, personal response, then—after a meaningful reply or explicit wish to move on—a positive summary with a separate completion offer, completed only upon further confirmation. Never apply this flow to content goals. RT No curriculum M-gate covers the conversational turn sequence. GD-X23 🔴 OPEN §8.2 Upon a genuine fresh start without subject progress, open orientation goals are the sole selectable frontier goals; existing subject progress never reverts a learner back into an entry lock. RT GVR route and orientation structure checks do not prove personalized frontier entry logic. GD-X24 🟡 PARTIAL §8.3 A memory goal bundles its required flashcards. SRS practice and controlled verified recall are distinct process states; card flipping or self-rating is never proof of verified recall. Exactly one binary goal result exists, with no extra mastery tiers. RT; M6 (REVIEW) only for memory content justification CQR-302 does not inspect individual learner SRS or recall results. GD-X25 🔴 OPEN §8.3 Repetitions belong to flashcard learning; completing a memory goal requires its own explicit verification record. Subsequent review due dates alone do not revoke that completion. Ordinary completed goals receive neither review due dates nor any mastery revocation derived from them; voluntary practice stays separate. RT, binding Product Owner decision; no curriculum M-gate Individual practice scheduling and durable goal completion are separated. Historical code descriptions are dated audit findings rather than competing norms. The contract introduces neither an extra assessment entity nor a new schema; specification prose is not proof of runtime implementation. GD-X26 🟡 PARTIAL §8.3 Every required flashcard deck must resolve completely and validly; missing cards must never be treated as an empty auto-completed deck. M6 (REVIEW) for authored deck integrity; RT for individual completion CQR-302 and check:curriculum-maturity-floors require a current individual deck/card-integrity pass for all ten M6/M7 subjects in the canonical 21-root catalog. The runtime obligation never to treat missing cards as an empty already-completed deck remains open; the data check does not prove that behavior. GD-X27 🔴 OPEN §8.3 The specified SRS process tracks interval, repetition count, ease factor, and next due date: unscheduled cards are due immediately, successful practice extends intervals, and insufficient recall resets the streak. Scheduling never substitutes for verified recall. RT Documented runtime process; M6 proves neither its runtime conformance nor any mastery revocation. GD-X28 🔴 OPEN §8.3 Controlled recall may begin on the active memory goal even while SRS practice items remain queued: prompt first, independent learner response second, expected answer and recall evaluation third. Passing updates the practice trace; failure affects the card process. RT Card scheduling and goal completion are separate claims. Subsequent due dates alone never revoke a completed memory goal; no mastery revocation is introduced here. GD-X29 🟡 PARTIAL §8.4 An exam goal carries task, reference solution, and grading rubric; valid step points yield \(\Score = \min(\sum_j p_j, \MaxPoints)\), passing at \(\PassingPoints\). The formula legitimizes neither fabricated or negative step points nor ad-hoc task alteration. M4/M5 (EXAM) for authored examData; RT for grading Schema and GVR-016 check authored data in the canonical 21-root catalog; check:curriculum-maturity-floors directly requires CQR-201/202/203 across all twelve pinned M4 scopes. Actual live-session grading by the formula, rejection of fabricated/negative step points, and unchanged assessment content during the session remain open. GD-X30 🔴 OPEN §8.4 Normal learning progression checks transitive effective prerequisites. A deliberately chosen direct exam attempt is not blocked by missing preparatory mastery, though a valid task, scope, and authorized session remain required. Direct attempt access itself is not global implicit recognition. RT Not covered by M7; any future holistic unit-lock profile remains undecided. GD-X31 🔴 OPEN §8.4 An exam presents the complete unaltered task without substantive hints and grades the full submission against the rubric. A pass is persisted immediately and awaits confirmation; a failed attempt persists neither result nor score and leaves prior mastery intact. RT Static metadata checks do not prove live session conformance. GD-X32 🔴 OPEN §8.4 Post-exam feedback reports outcome, score, rationale, and solution, with fresh tasks on retakes. Unlimited retakes remain available; prior exposure to a solution creates no extra mastery tier. Broader implicit-application recognition requires a reviewed local content contract, neither a second personal status flag nor a follow-up exam. RT/CONCEPT; independent content review separate EXAM/CQR-303 do not fully establish the new implicit-recognition contract. GD-X33 ⚪ OPT/DOC §9 A schedule binds target scope, curriculum revision, calendar, capacity, and plan version. Absolute calendar dates never belong on canonical goals, clusters, or placements; rescheduling never alters goal identity. OPTIONAL/RT No curriculum M-gate. GD-X34 ⚪ OPT/DOC §9 Time planning is supplementary execution scheduling rather than a fifth personalization level. It prioritizes available goals without creating requires, frontier entries, or results; planned acquisition must precede planned downstream use. OPTIONAL/RT Claims no new runtime access validator. GD-X35 ⚪ OPT/DOC §9 Use net available minutes after calendar outages; fit learning activities, reserve buffer, and binding subject budgets without double counting. OPTIONAL Detailed formulas in GD-P07–GD-P09; no M-gate. GD-X36 🔴 OPEN §9 Planned target and actual progress share the exact same named scope. Explicit and validly derived implicit completions form total actual progress; manual classroom-coverage markers neither replace nor mask learner completion. Open gaps remain visible, and revisions never rewrite historical events. RT/CONCEPT Joint global actual-progress accounting is not proven by M7. GD-X37 ⚪ OPT/DOC §9 Keep the local planning pilot distinct from the target backend-owned architecture; the learning-unit definition claims no implemented cross-subject budget validator. OPTIONAL/DOCUMENT Local pilot and target architecture must be documented as distinct implementation states. GD-X38 🟡 PARTIAL §10.1 Official sources justify a goal, first-party visualizations explain it, and supplementary materials support acquisition. None of the three is personal competency evidence. M1/M2 (SOURCE) sources; M7 (REVIEW) image QA; RT boundary SOURCE, image QA/REVIEW, and the content-package validator enforce separated reference types in their scopes; none proves personal competency. GD-X39 🟡 PARTIAL §10.1 Materials reference the curriculum rather than embedding provider lock-in inside the graph. New optional external materials live in separate content packages bound to stable goal IDs; package selection alters neither scope nor requires, mastery, or completion, and material gaps never block learning. ARTIFACT/RT Content-package and link-migration checks enforce separated packages with stable goal IDs in CI; no M-gate covers the entire runtime contract. GD-X40 🟡 PARTIAL §10.1 Sources, mappings, and provenance stay with the curriculum, and first-party visualizations retain their canonical quality contract. Legacy links never establish a permanent second authoring architecture, and returning a URL never proves its content was read. M1/M2/M7 (SOURCE/REVIEW) respective evidence; ARTIFACT GVR-008 forbids legacy goal links globally while SOURCE and image QA check evidence in their scopes; coach content fetching is not gated. GD-X41 🟡 PARTIAL §10.2 Maintain a traceable provenance chain: goal \(\to\) official source \(\to\) concrete section \(\to\) extraction \(\to\) reviewed mapping decision. Justify 1:1, partial, aggregating, or split mappings explicitly rather than claiming verbatim identity everywhere. M1/M2 (SOURCE) SOURCE; technical completeness alone does not substitute for domain source review. GD-X42 🔴 OPEN §10.2 For requires and contains, distinguish explicit official-source statements from pedagogical modeling decisions. Never fabricate provenance; keep unresolved, stale, or conflicting evidence visible. M2 target (SOURCE) for provenance; M3 (ROUTE) for sequencing review No current CQR gate automatically verifies every individual edge rationale. GD-X43 🟡 PARTIAL §10.2 Human-readable source rationales are derived views of structured evidence, never a second authoritative register. Keep references and fingerprints consistent across documentation, exports, and runtime; MEM/FWU alignment replaces the official source route only under an explicitly reviewed scope contract. M1/M2 (SOURCE) + ARTIFACT/RT Source-rationale and package-conformance checks verify consistency in covered scopes; not a blanket substitute across all interchange formats. GD-X44 🟡 PARTIAL §10.3 Parser, reference, cycle, projection, route, and content checks carry distinct evidentiary claims and each requires a declared scope. No single migration gate or structural pass certifies them all. Cross-stage (BASE/ROUTE/VIEW/REVIEW) BASE/ROUTE/VIEW/REVIEW are explicitly separated. GD-X45 🟢 HARD §10.3 Five current content-evidence dimensions: D domain-clear description, P observable understanding performance, A appropriate atomic sizing, M justified memory-support decision, and V domain-accurate hash-bound visualization. M5 A, M6 M, M7 simultaneous D/P/A/M/V completion (REVIEW) CQR-301 (from M5) and CQR-302 (from M6) require current A/M evidence for the ten M6/M7 subjects. CQR-303 requires the simultaneous current D/P/A/M/V intersection for every curricularAtomic goal of the five M7 subjects in the 21-root catalog; check:curriculum-maturity-floors enforces the individual passes. Negative evidence: the D/P/A/M/V test removes each of the five dimensions separately and rejects a stale image hash; required-pass tests reject every non-passing mandatory result. GD-X46 🟢 HARD §10.3 M7 is complete automated curriculum-QA closure atop all lower maturity levels for the declared scope. It implies neither human sign-off, learner trials, nor learning effectiveness; multi-model AI agreement never substitutes for mandatory human decisions. M7 boundary (REVIEW); human evidence outside M0–M7 CQR-303 and check:curriculum-maturity-floors enforce complete automated M7 QA, including the lower milestones, for the five M7 subjects in the canonical 21-root catalog. Negative evidence: the M7 completion test rejects missing dimensions, empty inventories, missing mandatory checks, and M7 without passing M6; human sign-off never substitutes for automated visualization QA. Human trials and learning effectiveness are explicitly outside this rule. This grade concerns the currently activated automated closeout contract; the decided but not yet fully activated GVR-012 obligation from M7 remains explicitly open under GD-C21/C22. GD-X47 🟡 PARTIAL §10.3 Reviews bind the exact artifact revision; an old image hash never certifies a new image. Content or prerequisite edits can invalidate evidence, technical moves require narrowly justified compatibility, and blanket hash refreshing is forbidden. M5/M6/M7 per review dimension (REVIEW) REVIEW checks current digest bindings; never infer substantive review validity from a mechanical hash update. GD-X48 🟡 PARTIAL §10.4 Author domain changes in canonical sources and regenerate downstream artifacts; keep published historical archives byte-immutable. ARTIFACT Plugin-freeze, release, goal-book, and status-diff checks guard canonical regeneration and archive immutability in their CI paths; they grant no publication authorization. GD-X49 🟡 PARTIAL §10.4 Build JSON and ontology packages from the identical canonical source state; the JSON runtime remains normative. Roundtrips preserve identities, relations, roles, prose, and domain fields per equality contract (semantic equality for texts, byte identity for binary assets) without divergent runtime semantics. ARTIFACT Package-contract and conformance checks verify JSON/ontology parity in CI (fast mode in routine CI); full standalone roundtrip verification remains a dedicated release check. GD-X50 🟡 PARTIAL §10.4 Close external goal references completely—including cross-subject prerequisites—without empty placeholders. Complete package closure does not by itself define Personal Curriculum targets. BASE (M0 base for references) + ARTIFACT/VIEW validate:graph, standalone-builder tests, and the closure compiler check reference closure in their scopes; package closure and Level 2 targets stay separate. GD-X51 🟡 PARTIAL §10.4 Every verification or release claim names its exact artifact, scope, version, and source digest binding. A local build proves neither host display nor learning effectiveness, and this compendium grants neither release nor production sign-off. ARTIFACT/DOCUMENT Release, submission, and goal-book checkers bind artifact, version, and source hashes in CI; prose claims, live host display, and production approval lie outside. GD-X52 🟡 PARTIAL §10.5 Function determines license: software, technical schemas, developer docs, and functional coach instructions carry Apache-2.0; first-party skill landscapes, content, and didactic media carry CC-BY-4.0. There is no blanket dual licensing. Third-party rights stay intact; provenance or AI generation proves neither ownership nor quality; exports carry license, attribution, and modification notices. ARTIFACT First-party license and package checks enforce Apache-2.0/CC-BY-4.0 declarations on covered repository artifacts in CI; third-party rights clearance is not an M-gate. GD-X53 🟡 PARTIAL §10.5 Private learner results, sessions, and conversations fall neither under the public content license nor into public source or review packages. ARTIFACT/RT Submission-ZIP audits and package-contract checks reject extraneous or private files in CI; end-to-end runtime privacy is not an M7 claim.

docs.title: U – Recursive Learning Units
docs.text:
Section 11 (03-learning-units). Every row cites its section; GD-* IDs remain stable regardless of later section renumbering.

ID Status Section Rule (concise summary) Area Enforcement and boundary GD-U01 🔴 OPEN §11 A LearningUnit recursively binds a learning promise, own atomic goals, and optional child units. Calendar periods are not synonyms; personalization levels, QA maturity, and difficulty retain independent meanings. CONCEPT, no M-gate Not claimed as an implemented runtime feature. GD-U02 🔴 OPEN §11.1 Unit motivation explains purpose ahead of individual tasks. Only a genuine orientation goal uses the orientation completion contract; a synthetic heading is not a goal, and derived unit completion never claims an orientation dialogue actually took place. CONCEPT/RT Unit display derives no synthetic orientation mastery. GD-U03 🔴 OPEN §11.1 A pure aggregate unit requires no extra exam. Added integrative synthesis claims may require a synthesis exam, and genuinely new competencies require own acquisition assignment plus valid exam coverage; pure synthesis forces neither artificial ordinary goals nor re-passing child units. CONCEPT; content review independent EXAM/M7 do not prove a complete learning-unit contract. GD-U04 🟡 PARTIAL §11.2 \(\Own(U)\) denotes own atomic goals and \(\Children(U)\) mandatory child units after choice resolution. \(T(U) = \Own(U) \cup \bigcup_{V \in \Children(U)} T(V)\) is non-empty. Structural markers are not goals; an aggregate unit may have empty \(\Own(U)\) when its child scope is non-empty. CONCEPT For the learning units authored in the canonical Gymnasium landscapes, validate:learning-units (required curriculum CI) rejects fail-closed: a malformed declaration (a programUnits entry of kind learningUnit with exactly the contract fields, ownership only through goalPlacements of relation own without context; LU-UNIT, LU-UNIT-ID, LU-PLACEMENT), own goals that are not atomic goals of the same landscape or that carry more than one goal kind (LU-REF, LU-ATOMIC, LU-KIND), an empty total scope \(T(U)\) (LU-EMPTY-SCOPE), and unresolved or cyclic child units (LU-CHILD, LU-HIERARCHY); a pure aggregate with empty \(\Own(U)\) passes. parentUnitId expresses required children only, so there is no choice resolution; no CQR gate or runtime consumes the units. GD-U05 🟡 PARTIAL §11.2 R4: every acquisition target has exactly one directly owning unit, the smallest authoritative owning unit. Viewing a parent never turns child goals into parent-owned goals; overlapping references unite as sets, and focus switches alter neither ownership nor local recognition contracts. BASE (validity condition of every authored unit definition, same class as acyclicity): hard from the first authored unit; a violating unit cannot be merged validate:learning-units (required curriculum CI) rejects fail-closed every goal that two learning units own (LU-R4-MULTIPLE). The completeness part, an owning unit for every acquisition target, is enforced only for a landscape that declares learningUnitCoverage as complete (LU-R4-UNOWNED); otherwise the validator reports unowned goals as a count, and no landscape declares complete yet. Whether the owner is the smallest authoritative unit remains a review question. Multi-view display creates no duplicate acquisition or progress counter. GD-U06 🟡 PARTIAL §11.2 R1: every own ordinary content goal lies on a prerequisite path from at least one own assessment of the unit, directly or transitively; a path that leads only to a memory goal does not count. The reviewed application coverage of such an assessment is R2 (GD-A08). Without both the local contract is invalid; arbitrary manual waiver masks never substitute for it. BASE (validity condition of every authored unit definition, same class as acyclicity): hard from the first authored unit; a violating unit cannot be merged; content share R2 see GD-A08 validate:learning-units (required curriculum CI) rejects fail-closed every authored unit with an own ordinary goal that no own assessment requires over the inherited, atomically expanded relation; being required only by an own memory goal does not count (LU-R1). The closed unit declaration cannot express waiver lists. R2 is not part of this validity check (GD-A08). The optional check inside offered curricula (LU-R1-OFFERED: a goal the view itself targets needs an own assessment that requires it within the learning scope) needs an inventory from the backend projection and is not part of required CI. ROUTE/EXAM check related properties rather than this unit condition; no fabricated M7 gate. GD-U07 🔴 OPEN §11.2 Authoritative program/placement or reviewed composition structure defines a learning unit. Expanding an arbitrary contains cluster never turns it into a learning unit; general cluster satisfaction stays distinct. CONCEPT/VIEW Clusters are never automatically classified as learning units at runtime. Under the Product Owner decision of 12 November 2026 (curriculum-package contract 1.2), a learning unit is declared in the placement layer as this rule requires: a programUnits entry of kind learningUnit that owns atomic goals through goalPlacements of relation own. validate:learning-units checks these declarations (LU-UNIT, LU-PLACEMENT) and rejects a cluster as an own goal (LU-ATOMIC). No check prevents a runtime or view from treating a cluster as a unit, and no runtime consumes units yet. GD-U08 🔴 OPEN §11.3 \(\Complete(U)\) holds iff all own goals lie in \(\Meff\) and all mandatory child units are complete. Neither extra unit-mastery state is stored nor is mastery written backward onto children. CONCEPT Document-model verification is neither a runtime nor an M-gate. GD-U09 🔴 OPEN §11.3 Exam and memory goals remain explicit; passing a parent exam replaces neither a child exam nor verified recall. Synthesis assessment is an additional own obligation, card decks alone never prove application, and child recall obligations must never be hoisted onto parents to fake child completion. CONCEPT/RT Never infer runtime fulfillment from M6 card review or M7 content status. GD-U10 🔴 OPEN §11.4 Own ordinary competencies can be implicitly recognized ahead of independent memory, child, or parent completion. Recognize only own goals of the local contract—never via a second parent contract spanning all descendants. Open parent synthesis never revokes valid child recognition. CONCEPT Global runtime effect is not yet implemented; see GD-A10–GD-A14. GD-U11 🔴 OPEN §11.5 An explicitly authorized whole-unit prerequisite denotes full unit completion and lives outside \(C\) and \(R\). An atomic prerequisite requires only that competency rather than the entire foreign unit; neither compiler nor coach may conflate the two. CONCEPT; access policy OPTIONAL An atomic edge induces no whole-unit hard lock. GD-U12 🟡 PARTIAL §11.5 The unit hierarchy is acyclic. Any claimed undivided unit-completion sequence must additionally be checked for block cycles; an atomic DAG alone does not suffice. Cyclic block grouping requires regrouping or finer interleaved sequencing rather than inducing an implicit unit-wide lock. CONCEPT / conditional structural contract validate:learning-units enforces fail-closed an acyclic hierarchy of authored learning units in which parentUnitId names a learning unit of the same landscape (LU-HIERARCHY, LU-CHILD). No block-cycle check of the projected unit dependency graph exists, and the closed declaration cannot express a whole-unit sequence; the finite document model verifies examples only. GD-U13 🟢 HARD §11.5 Transitive minimality remains binding for authored requires in accordance with the atomic target norm and complete current G17 validation. No extra minimality rule is posited for a not-yet-decided holistic unit-access relation. BASE (M0 target base before M1 per GD-C11/GD-C16); unit relation OPTIONAL CQR-001 and check:transitive-minimality enforce the authored atomic prerequisite relation across all 21 canonical Gymnasium roots independently of floors. Negative evidence: the G17 CLI test requires exit 1 for a transitive redundancy in the complete catalog. The undecided unit relation is explicitly not an additional obligation of this row and is not represented as implemented. GD-U14 ⚪ OPT/DOC §11.5 Both a hard unit-access profile and direct exam access under it remain undecided. The illustrative equations \(\operatorname{Open}(U) = \bigwedge_{V \in \operatorname{Pred}(U)} \operatorname{Cleared}(V)\) and \(\operatorname{Cleared} = \operatorname{Open} \land \Complete\) apply only if an access profile is later authorized. \(\Complete\) denotes evidentiary state and \(\operatorname{Cleared}\) course policy; neither grants mastery, and the formula does not settle direct-exam exceptions. OPTIONAL, no curriculum M-gate Claim neither authorization nor implementation of a technical unit lock. GD-U15 🔴 OPEN §11; §11.1 A unit establishes secure independent application of its promise before planned learning builds on it; its assessments expose essential misconceptions, and a gap leads to focused learning and a fresh equivalent assessment. Boundaries follow meaningful conceptual transitions, not existing assessments, target quotas, headings, or edge density; edges are never changed to fit a cut. The ordinary grading contract applies: no hidden pass rule, no second stored outcome. CONCEPT; content review (REVIEW) separate; no access lock Didactic design and review criterion; no validator or M-gate checks unit boundaries or purpose. validate:learning-units checks structure only, not whether a learning promise or boundary is didactically sound.

docs.title: P – Optional Acquisition and Time Planning
docs.text:
Section 12 (04-planning). Every row cites its section; GD-* IDs remain stable regardless of later section renumbering.

ID Status Section Rule (concise summary) Area Enforcement and boundary GD-P01 ⚪ OPT/DOC §12 An optional schedule assigns acquisition targets to calendar levels; it neither defines learning units, alters core skill-graph validity or mastery, nor introduces holistic unit locks or blanket full-year completion gates. OPTIONAL Claims no new production budget validator. GD-P02 ⚪ OPT/DOC §12.1 A plan specifies atomic acquisition targets \(T\), a disjoint declared entry basis \(B\), a positive number of levels, and a unique first-acquisition level \(\ell\) per target defining level sets and prefixes. Later practice or application is scheduled activity rather than a duplicate goal ID. \(B\) writes no learner mastery; personal entry gaps require diagnosis and time. OPTIONAL No curriculum M-gate. GD-P03 ⚪ OPT/DOC §12.2 The hypothetical plan relation prunes outgoing requirements solely at the declared entry basis \(B\), preserving full transitive closure across all planned levels. This planning convention never permits truncating real runtime prerequisite traversal at mastered intermediates. OPTIONAL Purely hypothetical planning construct, not a runtime mastery contract. GD-P04 ⚪ OPT/DOC §12.2 A completion witness orders every level's targets so each enters the global frontier given \(B\), prior levels, and preceding witness atoms. Inherited, cluster, and cross-subject requirements remain intact, with neither normal-mode hiding, direct exam jumps, nor anticipated implicit recognition. OPTIONAL No curriculum M-gate; not proven by current UI navigation paths. GD-P05 ⚪ OPT/DOC §12.2 Required atoms equal the full closure under the plan relation. Necessarily, every target's prerequisite demand lies in \(B\) or at latest its own level: outside \(B \cup T\) is unplanned, a higher level is an ordering error, and same-level dependencies are permitted. Graph and expansion validity precede closure checking. OPTIONAL Structural feasibility check only; does not by itself prove time feasibility. GD-P06 ⚪ OPT/DOC §12.2 The finite fixed-point iteration starts from \(B\) plus prior levels and repeatedly adds currently frontier-eligible level targets, succeeding iff the entire level is reached. Eligibility is monotone, each parallel wave is serializable, the test mutates no learner data, and a purely atomic DAG reduces to standard topological sorting. OPTIONAL/DOCUMENT Algorithmic specification, not claimed as a production validator. GD-P07 ⚪ OPT/DOC §12.3 Any time-feasibility claim states reference learners, entry state, target/elective selection, calendar, estimation method, and uncertainty in a shared calibrated time unit: \(\Work \geq 0\), \(\Reserve \geq 0\), \(\Budget > 0\), and \(\Work + \Reserve \leq \Budget\). Keep reserve protected (or disclose zero explicitly) without double-counting exam or review effort. OPTIONAL Without calibrated estimates there is no time-validity claim; no M-gate. GD-P08 ⚪ OPT/DOC §12.3 The activity model counts actual effort once across acquisition, practice, recall, assessment, and supplementary work. A shared canonical atom is not acquired twice across subjects, though subject-specific application may still consume time. weight and uncalibrated goal counts are never minutes. OPTIONAL Underlying estimation model and empirical data must be evidenced separately. GD-P09 ⚪ OPT/DOC §12.3 Worked numerical examples are not empirical curriculum durations. Binding subject, room, or date sub-budgets must hold simultaneously without double-counting shared time, and concrete prerequisites must be scheduled ahead of their planned application. OPTIONAL Satisfying a total budget alone is insufficient when sub-constraints apply. GD-P10 ⚪ OPT/DOC §12.4 Full validity of an optional plan requires both structural and time feasibility under bound assumptions. Without calibrated time data only structural feasibility may be claimed; every claim binds plan, revision, scope, and estimation assumptions without guaranteeing uniform individual learning speed. OPTIONAL Neither an M7 gate nor proof of learning effectiveness. GD-P11 ⚪ OPT/DOC §12.4 Unit completion follows own and child obligations; learning units and calendar periods may cross-cut one another. A schedule profile never creates a blanket full-year prerequisite for later goals. OPTIONAL/CONCEPT Access policy remains separate.

docs.title: A – Implicit Mastery via Local Assessment Contracts
docs.text:
Section 13 (05-assessment). Every row cites its section; GD-* IDs remain stable regardless of later section renumbering.

ID Status Section Rule (concise summary) Area Enforcement and boundary GD-A01 🔴 OPEN §13 Explicit ordinary completion evidences understanding and a valid local exam evidences independent application; both act globally. Exactly one binary state is stored—without backward writes, extra qualification tiers, manual waiver profiles, or second sub-exams. Exam and memory goals themselves always remain explicit. CONCEPT, no M-gate New semantics is explicitly not yet implemented; never reinterpret legacy tests as proving it. GD-A02 🔴 OPEN §13.1 Each local contract binds authoritative own unit goals, canonical IDs, curriculum revision, and the reviewed evidentiary scope of own exams. Total child scope never forms an inflated parent recognition contract, and display, focus, or schedule roots never alter unit ownership. CONCEPT Future contract and revision check; neither CQR-401 nor M7 substitutes for it. GD-A03 🔴 OPEN §13.1 Determine exam and memory goals authoritatively; \(P_U = Q_U \cup A_{\mathrm{mem},U}\) protects all own goals of both types from implicit completion. Orientation is not a protected demand root, though a derived unit marker claims neither competency nor dialogue. External support neither inflates the unit denominator nor permits local recognition of foreign \(\Own\) goals. CONCEPT Memory content review alone does not establish this recognition logic. For authored units, validate:learning-units reads each own goal's kind from the canonical landscape, mirroring the backend's completion type semantics, and rejects ambiguous kinds (LU-KIND); the protection itself belongs to recognition, which is not implemented. GD-A04 🔴 OPEN §13.1 Operate on the fully inherited and atomically expanded relation—including hidden and cross-subject prerequisite support—with all references resolvable and the normalized graph acyclic. Compute full closure prior to display filtering. BASE (M0 target base for inputs); CONCEPT for recognition use BASE alone does not prove the recognition normalizer. validate:learning-units evaluates R1 and R3 on this relation and reports unresolvable references on the paths from own goals and prerequisite cycles through an own goal (LU-GRAPH); global acyclicity remains the job of validate:graph and CQR-001. GD-A05 🔴 OPEN §13.2 \(N_U = \operatorname{Reach}_{\Rat}^{*}(P_U \setminus M)\) comprises all open protected roots and every transitive prerequisite without stopping at mastered intermediates. \(I_U = \Own(U) \setminus (M \cup P_U \cup N_U)\) is disjoint from \(M\) and \(P_U\). Redundant edges with identical closure leave \(I_U\) unchanged. CONCEPT; formula check DOCUMENT Legacy contextual waiver logic does not implement or prove this equation. GD-A06 🔴 OPEN §13.2 The demand traversal visits reachable atoms \(V_U^{\mathrm{reach}}\) and their outgoing \(\Rat\) edges \(E_U^{\mathrm{reach}}\) at most once; computing \(I_U\) adds one pass over \(\Own(U)\), yielding \(O(\lvert\Own(U)\rvert + \lvert V_U^{\mathrm{reach}}\rvert + \lvert E_U^{\mathrm{reach}}\rvert)\) without materializing a quadratic closure. CONCEPT / algorithmic contract Verified in the finite document model, not a production benchmark. GD-A07 🔴 OPEN §13.3 The implicit-set equation is evaluated only for units whose contract satisfies R1–R4 (GD-U06, GD-A08, GD-A18, GD-U05) with reviewed coverage. Otherwise the unit's own ordinary goals stay open and the violation keeps the curriculum from reaching the respective milestone; a goal that no assessment covers stays open and is a rule violation, never recognized for free. Absence of a downstream consumer proves nothing, and arbitrary waiver masks are forbidden. CONCEPT for the recognition gate; violations count against BASE (R1, R3, R4) and M5/M7 (R2) Recognition is not implemented. validate:learning-units rejects authored units that violate R1, R3, or the uniqueness part of R4 fail-closed in required curriculum CI and reports missing reviewed coverage per unit; no recognition gate consumes this, and as a standalone CI gate it does not enter the maturity status computation. ROUTE is structurally related but not equivalent to a local unit contract. GD-A08 🔴 OPEN §13.3 R2: for every own ordinary goal, at least one own assessment that requires it has reviewed evidence that its tasks and normal grading really test the goal, so that no essential skill can be fully compensated away by unrelated rubric points. Neither requires paths, titles, coveredGoalIds, passing thresholds, nor DAG validity prove this; independent review must verify all tasks, solutions, rubrics, and every passing score combination rather than just their union. M5 (EXAM/REVIEW: assessment approval and coverage metadata), current per-goal binding M7 (REVIEW); without it the curriculum does not reach the milestone CQR-203 checks approval status and coverage metadata of terminal assessments in configured scopes, and CQR-303 current per-goal D/P/A/M/V evidence; neither reviews unit-local coverage, and none of the six required M7 checks is a coverage check. validate:learning-units does not require R2 for a valid unit. Reviewed coverage is recorded in the learning unit's coverageReviews, at most one entry per own assessment; an entry must be well formed, name an own assessment and own ordinary goals of the unit that this assessment requires and lists in coveredGoalIds, cite an existing review record, and carry task and rubric hashes equal to the current examData of that assessment (LU-R2-EVIDENCE); the validator reports per unit which own ordinary goals lack reviewed coverage. No M5/M7 gate consumes this; R2 itself is not enforced today. GD-A09 🔴 OPEN §13.3 Passing an exam remains a single binary learner outcome. Its broader evidentiary reach resides in the pre-reviewed exam contract rather than a second personal status flag; legacy unreviewed exams are never retroactively upgraded by diagrams or software. CONCEPT/RT Stronger evidentiary meaning resides in reviewed exam content; no second stored learner status follows. GD-A10 🔴 OPEN §13.4 The valid contract set \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{valid}}\) is bound durably per learner and revision—neither restricted to the active view/plan nor expanded across all latest revisions. \(\Meff = M \cup \bigcup_{U \in \mathcal U_{\mathrm{valid}}} I_U\) stays available across focus or scope changes and derives strictly from explicit results \(M\) without feeding prior implicit sets back into demand. RT/CONCEPT: versioned contract binding (R5, GD-A12) is a precondition before implicit recognition is enabled in production Not yet claimed in production; no curriculum M-gate. GD-A11 🔴 OPEN §13.4 Subsequent exams or units never reopen an already recognized goal. Under fixed contracts, additional explicit mastery can only grow \(\Meff\), and moving a goal from \(I_U\) into \(M\) preserves satisfaction monotonically. CONCEPT; monotonicity proof DOCUMENT Finite model checking \(\neq\) production runtime conformance. GD-A12 🔴 OPEN §13.4 R5: a later re-cut of units or later edges never grant additional recognition to existing results; the contract is versioned. A stable exam ID carries stable recognition semantics, and task variants satisfy the same contract. Changed claims require a new assessment identity or reviewed migration; unverified historical exams retain explicit pass status without fabricating broader implicit application. Separate genuine error correction from mere plan or consumer changes. RT (runtime contract): precondition before implicit recognition is enabled in production; ARTIFACT for contract versions Not implemented; no recognition runtime exists yet to enable. No extra personal qualification record; no silent historical upgrade. GD-A13 🔴 OPEN §13.5 Full unit completion is recursive—equivalent under complete goal representation to \(T(U) \subseteq \Meff\), with own \(P_U \subseteq M\). Passing own exam and memory goals empties \(N_U\) and can recognize own ordinary goals, never child units. Open parent synthesis never revokes child recognition, and passing a parent exam never replaces child exam or memory goals. CONCEPT Specification equation, not an existing M7 feature. GD-A14 🔴 OPEN §13.5 An open own memory goal blocks full unit completion, yet withholds implicit recognition from another own goal only if it transitively requires that goal. A shared foundation stays demanded as long as any local open protected consumer requires it; a later open consumer in another unit contract never revokes existing recognition. CONCEPT Never conflate local contract demand with downstream units. GD-A15 🔴 OPEN §13.5 Direct exam attempt access remains the baseline given a valid task, auth, session, and explicit selection. Optional unit-wide locking stays undecided; the learning-unit concept creates neither a lock nor an auth bypass. Normal learning progression evaluates \(\Meff\) across full effective transitivity under separate normal/strict focus rules. RT/CONCEPT/OPTIONAL Neither an M-gate nor an access-lock policy decision is introduced here. GD-A16 🔴 OPEN §13.6 Cumulative actual progress counts \(\lvert T_{\mathrm{Plan}} \cap \Meff \rvert\), uniting explicit, implicit, and multi-contract contributions prior to counting. Any explicit-only view must state its distinct numerator/denominator. Current-period reporting counts genuinely dated explicit completion events rather than newly derived implicit items, prior work, or later scope expansion. RT/CONCEPT M7 checks no personal plan or period accounting. GD-A17 🔴 OPEN §13.6 Static contract structures may be cached per revision, whereas derived implicit completions never form a second persisted source of truth. Invalid or unverified contracts stay visible as explicit limitations. Automated formula checks replace neither independent content review nor human trials and learning-effectiveness evidence. CONCEPT/DOCUMENT; evidentiary boundary cross-stage No curriculum M-gate covers the full persistence and disclosure contract. GD-A18 🟡 PARTIAL §13.3 R3: an assessment claims coverage only for goals it requires directly or transitively: \(\operatorname{Cov}(q) \subseteq \{b \in A \mid (q,b) \in \Rat^+\}\). This guarantees that the assessment which actually tests a goal is among the open protected goals the recognition rule waits for. A missing path is a subject-review finding, never a reason for a redundant direct edge. BASE (validity condition of every authored unit definition, same class as acyclicity): hard from the first authored unit; a violating unit cannot be merged validate:learning-units rejects every unresolvable, non-atomic, or non-prerequisite coveredGoalIds entry of own assessments of authored units (LU-R3) in the canonical 21-root catalog. CQR-104 checks general endpoint visibility in eight of twelve pinned scopes; its additional binding of every coveredGoalIds entry to a visible prerequisite path still applies only to terminal Economics assessments. R3 remains open outside own unit assessments and those Economics terminals. CQR-203 only checks that coverage metadata exists; twelve visibility scopes alone would not close this residual obligation.
